title: Klint Kubiak open to naming Aidan O'Connell QB2, Fernando Mendoza QB3
summary: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza might start his rookie season as a third-stringer.
full_text: '' Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza might start his rookie season as a third-stringer. Coach Klint Kubiak has not said who his starting quarterback is, but it's widely expected to be Kirk Cousins. Kubiak was asked today whether, if Cousins is the starter, Mendoza or Aidan O'Connell will be the backup. And Kubiak said that decision has not yet been made. "We've got three guys that are ready to play. It's going to be some hard decisions on who's 1, who's 2. That's not a decision we have to make today, but those are discussions that are ongoing," Kubiak said. It's not often that the first overall pick in the draft starts his career on the third team, but Kubiak seems to be in no rush to get Mendoza on the field. It appears likely that Cousins is going to start the season with Mendoza on the sideline, and Mendoza may not get on the field early in the season even if Cousins goes down.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Federal appeals court rules that states can regulate betting markets
summary: The legal odyssey regarding prediction markets vs. gambling continues.
full_text: The legal odyssey regarding prediction markets vs. gambling continues. On Friday, Kalshi stumbled onto an island full of giants wearing black robes. Via the Associated Press, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit ruled on Friday that federal commodities-trading law does not preempt Nevada’s gambling law as to the regulation of placing wagers on sports. The 3-0 ruling becomes the biggest loss to date by the prediction-market industry, and it could set the stage for the inevitable decision from the U.S. Supreme Court resolving the issue one way or the other. Especially since the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit has ruled that New Jersey cannot regulate Kalshi. A split among the various circuits often becomes a key factor in the Supreme Court's decision to take up a given issue. As noted by the AP, roughly 20 states currently are involved in litigation over the question of whether prediction markets can offer sports-related contracts independent of their gambling laws.
author: Mike Florio

title: SEC loses again in court, on effort to bar schools from signing former NFL players
summary: "[The NCAA] created this cluster, and now they've got to lay in that bed," one of the player's lawyers said.
full_text: '' The SEC now stands for "Sucks when Entering Court." The conference continues to lose rulings regarding the effort to block its member schools from adding players who were on NFL rosters. Most recently, a Louisiana judge ruled that the SEC can't issue punishments to programs that use players who had signed NFL contracts. On Wednesday, a Dallas judge issued a similar ruling . Via Dan Murphy of ESPN, the new temporary restraining order blocks the SEC from penalizing schools for welcoming back players with NFL offseason or preseason experience. The judge also signed an order requiring the SEC and NCAA to show cause as to why the rule doesn't put them in contempt of the prior ruling allowing players to return from the NFL and play. "If Sankey shows up, I'd like to hear his argument," attorney Tony Clayton said, per Murphy. "What gives him the right to anoint himself God and take these constitutional rights from these kids?" Clayton also blamed the NCAA for making the current mess. "[The NCAA] created this cluster, and now they've got to lay in that bed," Clayton said. "If this were going to happen every year, they might be on to something. But this is a one-time deal that they opened up." He's right. The situation flows from the NCAA's new five-year rule — and from an effort by players to have it applied retroactively to them. Even the loss counts as a partial win. The notion of NFL players playing college football is not popular, and the SEC, other conferences, and the NCAA obviously hope to harness that into momentum for getting the Protect College Sports Act passed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Man who posed as 49ers player is arrested for fraud
summary: The week began with news of the arrest of the 49ers' owner posing as a man named "Joe."
full_text: The week began with news of the arrest of the 49ers' owner posing as a man named "Joe." It's ending with news of the arrest of a man posing as a 49er. Via Nick Wagoner of ESPN, federal authorities have arrested two men in connection with a fraudulent scheme that entailed one of them repeatedly posing as a 49ers player. The men allegedly defrauded 26 women out of roughly $1.3 million. Daejon Love, 35, and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, have been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud in Idaho. It allegedly started in 2022, with Love meeting multiple women on dating apps. He repeatedly told them he was a member of the 49ers or a wealthy real-estate investor. He used the names Jon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love. Chan posed as Love's financial advisor. From the U.S. attorney's office in Boise: "Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars. Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims." Some of the victims loaned Love significant amounts of money. Some took out personal loans to pay Love. When the women ran out of money or started asking too many questions, Love blocked communications with them. The FBI believes there are "many more victims" than the 26 who have been identified.
author: Mike Florio

title: Browns start slashing roster, cut 15 players from active roster
summary: The Browns have started the process of setting their initial 53-man roster.
full_text: The Browns have started the process of setting their initial 53-man roster. They announced 15 cuts from their training camp roster and one cut from injured reserve on Friday afternoon. All 32 teams need to get down to 53 players by Sunday afternoon's deadline. Four of the players were released as vested veterans. Cornerbacks Tre Avery and Tyler Hall joined offensive tackle Tyre Phillips in getting dropped from the active roster while tight end Jack Stoll was released from injured reserve. They also waived tight end Drew Biber, offensive tackle Jeremiah Byers, punter Nik Constantinou, safety Christopher Edmonds, cornerback Nate Evans, defensive tackle Coziah Izzard, defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins, cornerback Jeremiah McClendon, offensive tacke Izavion Miller, defensive end Jamil Muhammad, wide receiver Ben Patterson, and tight end Jermaine Terry. Cleveland has many more moves to make to hit the roster limit and there will likely be some immediate churning as other players shake free around the league in the coming days.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brandon Staley: I'd be a more poised, composed head coach now
summary: Brandon Staley is heading into his second season as the Saints' defensive coordinator, but his previous experience as an NFL head coach has him thinking about what a second chance in that spot might look like.
full_text: Brandon Staley is heading into his second season as the Saints' defensive coordinator, but his previous experience as an NFL head coach has him thinking about what a second chance in that spot might look like. Staley earned a reputation for being ultra-aggressive while going 19-15 in his first two seasons as the head coach of the Chargers, but the weight of some of those decisions misfiring and a blown 27-point lead against the Jaguars in the playoffs put him on the hot seat when the 2023 season started badly. The Chargers wound up firing him after Week 15 and Staley spent the 2024 season with the 49ers before joining Kellen Moore in New Orleans. Staley said "as tough and impossible as it was at the end" of his time with the Chargers, he feels he has to use them the right way to grow as a coach. He shared what he thinks he would do differently if given another opportunity to run a team. “I would have a lot more poise and composure in terms of knowing when to push and when to pull,” Staley said, via Jeff Howe of TheAthletic.com. “I was trying to push it, and I was trying to get us there as fast as we could. When you have more experience, you know when to do both of those things. You just have a better feel and understanding, and that’s in all aspects of being a leader. That’s why the next time, I just have so much more experience now — I didn’t have any back then. I could have done a better job. I know for a fact I would do a better job just with more turns at it, living through more — little decisions and big decisions.” There's high hopes for the Saints heading into this season thanks to a strong finish to last year after handing the offensive reins to quarterback Tyler Shough. If Staley's defense can help push the team even further this fall, he could get a chance to expand on his new coaching philosophies with teams looking for a new head coach.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalon Daniels will start tonight for Bucs with chance to secure No. 2 QB job
summary: Jalon Daniels will start tonight's preseason finale against Jacksonville and will play the first half and possibly into the third quarter, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
full_text: '' Jalon Daniels will start tonight’s preseason finale against Jacksonville and will play the first half and possibly into the third quarter, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports. The Bucs are giving the undrafted rookie from Kansas a chance to win the backup job to Baker Mayfield. Jake Browning and Connor Bazelak will follow Daniels tonight. Daniels rallied the Bucs to come-from-behind wins against the Jets and Chiefs the past two weeks, and in two weeks, he is 19-of-20 for 182 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions. He also has rushed for a score. Daniels took the majority of reps during the Bucs' seven-on-seven period after Mayfield today, per Stroud.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jeff Hafley: Success won't be measured in Ws, Ls this year, it's about development
summary: The Dolphins have been mired in mediocrity in recent years.
full_text: '' The Dolphins have been mired in mediocrity in recent years. But with a new General Manager in Jon-Eric Sullivan and a new head coach in Jeff Hafley, the team’s path back to prominence may be a long one. Hafley admitted as much in an interview with Stephen A. Smith that was released this week. “Success is not gonna be measured in wins and losses this year — and I know nobody wants to hear that ,” Hafley said, via Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN. “I want to see where we end and how far we can take this thing, and how much we develop these players ... Success for me is gonna be we go on that field and we play so hard that even you turn it on and say, 'man those guys are flying around.' "I just think this year's so much about developing who we are as a football team, finding the right guys and by the end of the year saying, ‘We've got something real powerful moving forward.’” The personnel moves the Dolphins have made over the course of the offseason signal that building the club is going to be a process. But getting some Ws along the way will make a difference, showing that Miami is moving in the right direction.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Wan'Dale Robinson is not believed to have suffered a concussion
summary: There is some positive news on the injury front for the Titans.
full_text: There is some positive news on the injury front for the Titans. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, receiver Wan’Dale Robinson is not believed to have suffered a concussion after he was hit during a joint practice with the Bears this week. While the team will continue to monitor Robinson, the early indications have been positive. Titans head coach Robert Saleh called out Chicago safety Xavier Woods for what he termed a “cheap” hit. Woods played for the Titans in 2025 and was released shortly after the club hired Saleh earlier this year. Robinson, 25, signed a four-year deal with Tennessee in March, reuniting with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll, who previously served as Giants head coach. A second-round pick in 2022, Robinson appeared in 54 games for New York over his first four seasons. He caught 92 passes for 1,014 yards with four touchdowns in 2025.
author: Myles Simmons

title: How can Tony Romo accept "full responsibility" in a statement from an unnamed spokesperson?
summary: Confusion was the first reaction to the TMZ item in which former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo accepted "full responsibility" for his recent OWI arrest in Milwaukee, in a statement issued by an unnamed spokesperson.
full_text: Confusion was the first reaction to the TMZ item in which former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo accepted “full responsibility” for his recent OWI arrest in Milwaukee, in a statement issued by an unnamed spokesperson. The same statement arrived, unsolicited, in the PFT email box. "Reaching out as we are working with Tony Romo’s team," the email began. "Below please find a statement to be attributed to an unnamed spokesperson : 'Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps.'" (Emphasis in original.) While we won't name the spokesperson or his firm as a courtesy, any email that suddenly lands in the PFT account without prior communication is fair game to be used on the record. The ability to speak on an off-the-record basis can't be unilaterally activated — especially when there's no prior relationship whatsoever between the person who sends the email and the person who receives it. The bigger issue is this. How can Romo, or anyone, accept "full responsibility" by issuing a statement through an unnamed spokesperson? To accept full responsibility, the responsibility must be fully accepted. That can't happen by issuing a statement through an unnamed spokesperson. Really, who uses an unnamed spokesperson, for anything? Romo has a spokesperson who, for whatever reason, won't attach the spokesperson's name to the statement. If Romo wants to accept "full responsibility," he needs to conduct a press conference, issue a statement in his own name, or submit to an interview. Maybe he eventually will. For now, though, it's impossible to regard a statement from an unnamed spokesperson as the acceptance of responsibility, full or partial.
author: Mike Florio

title: Klint Kubiak: We're counting on Ashton Jeanty for Week 1
summary: The Raiders wrapped up their preseason games on Thursday night and running back Ashton Jeanty's status will be one of the team's focal points as they turn their attention toward Week 1.
full_text: The Raiders wrapped up their preseason games on Thursday night and running back Ashton Jeanty's status will be one of the team's focal points as they turn their attention toward Week 1. Jeanty sprained his ankle last weekend and the team has not shared much detail about the severity of the injury or the outlook for when he will be back on the field. Head coach Klint Kubiak stayed the course on that during a Friday videoconference with reporters, but he did make it clear that the team's plans include having the 2025 first-round pick in the backfield. “Still on the mend, still working to get him back ," Kubiak said. "We’ve got another week to assess how he’s gonna look going into this first game, but we’re counting on him.” Fourth-round pick Mike Washington had a good camp and Kubiak said he will have a role once the regular season is underway, but the Raiders would prefer it to be a complementary rather than starring one.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL's new approach to on-field safety infractions could result in sanctions for coaches, teams
summary: The NFL's new approach to on-field safety infractions creates a three-strike formula for player suspensions.
full_text: The NFL's new approach to on-field safety infractions creates a three-strike formula for player suspensions. The process also extends potential responsibility to coaches and teams. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, fines for position coaches, coordinators, head coaches, and owners are "on the table" in connection with chronic violations by one player of various specific rules (hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, hits on defenseless players, and blindside blocks). There's no specific equation for determining when, and if, responsibility would extend beyond the player. The fact that it's now available is appropriate, and overdue. The new procedure also entails the possibility that the position coach, the coordinator, and/or the coach will be required to make with the player any trips to 345 Park Avenue arising from a string of violations. Coaches lose nothing when players are fined for techniques that violate the rules. When the player is flagged, the team loses field position. When the player is suspended, the coach loses the player. But the coach never faces direct accountability. Now, he does. In theory. It's unclear how it will play out, but the potential exists for direct financial punishment for coaches and teams if a player continues to violate one of the five specific rules that are included in the three-strike formula.
author: Mike Florio

title: Najee Harris set to play tonight, first game action since tearing Achilles 11 months ago
summary: Harris would make his Giants debut against the Jets in the preseason finale.
full_text: After a long rehab from a torn Achilles tendon, Giants running back Najee Harris may finally return to game action tonight. Harris is expected to play tonight against the Jets, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. Harris was playing for the Chargers last season when he tore his Achilles tendon in Week Three, ending his season. Before signing with the Chargers last season, Harris played four seasons for the Steelers, and ran for at least 1,000 yards in all four of them, while never missing a game. The Giants would love to see that version of Harris back on the field this season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Vrabel on trading Kayshoun Boutte: "He probably would have been inactive" on game days
summary: The Patriots recently traded receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Texans.
full_text: The Patriots recently traded receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Texans. After New England's preseason finale against the Browns, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was asked about the decision to move on from the 2023 sixth-round pick. "That was one place where we do have some depth," Vrabel told reporters. "I think for all parties involved, that was probably the best thing without injuries, you know? OK, sure, he probably would have been inactive, unfortunately, because it's kind of the way it was. It's just him not playing special teams." It really does become a numbers game. The deeper a receiver slides on the depth chart, the less he'll play offense. And the more of a role he'll have on special teams. As Vrabel said, Boutte wouldn't have been playing special teams. So they needed to move on. "I tried to thank Kayshon as many times as I could," Vrabel said. "Just his maturity, his growth. His ability to put into words last year and share his own personal struggle, but also the growth that he made from that, that is positively going to affect a lot of people. I know that that wasn't easy for him to do, and I tell him all the time about how much I respect him." Vrabel was referring to Boutte's willingness to go public with his gambling addiction from his time at LSU. And Vrabel is right; Boutte's candor will indeed help others who are dealing with the same issue.
author: Mike Florio

title: Alec Pierce: Week 1 is the goal
summary: Colts receiver Alec Pierce got back to practice on Thursday, having come off the physically unable to perform list after undergoing offseason ankle surgery.
full_text: Colts receiver Alec Pierce got back to practice on Thursday, having come off the physically unable to perform list after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. Pierce said after the session that he’s on schedule with the season quickly approaching. “Yeah, Week 1 is the goal,” Pierce said, via transcript from the team. “[J]ust first time being back out here, wearing the helmet, playing with the other NFL players, right? So, it's — you got to knock a little bit of rust off, but been working in PT, been working kind of off and on with the trainers. They've been doing a good job preparing me, getting me ready. “So, just a little different once you get back out here, get timing from Daniel [Jones] and these other NFL arms.” Though Pierce noted he’s been ramping up throughout camp, the process of getting back on the field was still a little tough on him, mentally. “You just got to find ways to try and stay in it because you're going to be in those meetings and stuff,” Pierce said. “It’s good to be around the guys. They kind of — they keep your spirits up and stuff because sitting and watching film and watching walk-through, watching practice, like it gets a little monotonous. You want to be out there. You want to be out there helping the team, making plays with the team, working with your brothers. But the guys have been great. They've been checking in with me. Other than just not being out there on the field, everything's been the same.” Head coach Shane Steichen said it was great to have Pierce back on the field and the team is working to get him ready for Week 1. That’s a good sign for Pierce as he continues his process. Last season, Pierce caught 47 passes for 1,003 yards with six touchdowns. He’s led the league in yards per reception in each of the last two years.
author: Myles Simmons

title: New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla was, and still is, a Steelers fan
summary: To this day, plenty of Seahawks fans believe the Super Bowl XL officials who were wearing black and white were secretly wearing black and yellow.
full_text: To this day, plenty of Seahawks fans believe the Super Bowl XL officials who were wearing black and white were secretly wearing black and yellow. One person openly wearing black and yellow during the game was new Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla. On Wednesday, after the owners voted to approve the sale of the team to a group led by Khosla, the self-made billionaire made it clear that he was — and still is — a fan of the team that kept the Seahawks from winning their first NFL championship in early 2006. "I also happened to come to this country in '76 when the Steelers were winning Super Bowls," Khosla told reporters on Wednesday. "So, actually, I was originally, and still am, a big Steelers fan also — a little-known fact — but I still watch all the Steelers games, too." Well, it's no longer a little-known fact. And it's not unprecedented. Vikings owner Zygi Wilf, for example, was a long-time Giants fans before buying the Vikings; he once followed Lawrence Taylor to the men's room to seek an autograph. (Wilf waited for Taylor to finish his business and emerge from the facilities.) "I'll always be, deep inside, a Giants fan," Wilf said in November 2005, as the Vikings prepared to face the Giants. " I don’t think it ever goes away ." For Khosla, the Seahawks and Steelers will square off in 2027. Unless, of course, they happen to cross paths in Super Bowl LXI.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joe Brady: Maxwell Hairston is a starting cornerback
summary: The Bills did not play most of their starters against the Steelers on Thursday night, but they did have Maxwell Hairston in the lineup at cornerback to open the game.
full_text: The Bills did not play most of their starters against the Steelers on Thursday night, but they did have Maxwell Hairston in the lineup at cornerback to open the game. Hairston has dealt with a groin injury in camp this summer and did not play in the team's first two preseason games, which is why head coach Joe Brady decided to have him on the field along with second-round pick Davis Igbinosun. "I thought it was important for Maxwell, he hasn't had an opportunity," Brady said, via the team's website. "I thought it was just good for him to just be able to come out, go through it, get a feel for the environment and game, all of that. That was the biggest reason for it." Brady went on to say that Hairston will also be on the field at corner with Christian Benford when the Bills line up for their first defensive snap in Week 1. "He's our starting corner. Maxwell's got exactly what we look for in a corner," Brady said. Hairston also missed time with injury as a rookie and Igbinosun got good reviews for his camp work, so the current plan may not prove to be the final word on how the Bills line up in the secondary this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Deion Sanders must testify in Shilo's bankruptcy trial — after Georgia Tech game (if at all)
summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has gotten a ruling on the question of whether he'll be required to testify in Shilo's upcoming bankruptcy trial.
full_text: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has gotten a ruling on the question of whether he'll be required to testify in Shilo's upcoming bankruptcy trial. The bad news? Deion did not successfully quash the subpoena. The good news? He won't have to testify in the days preceding the regular-season opener at Georgia Tech, next Thursday night. The best news? His testimony likely won't be needed at all. Via Christopher Kamrani of The Athletic , Sanders has been ordered to testify on Friday, September 4, at 1:30 p.m. MT. He will appear virtually, and not in court. And he won't appear at all, unless Shilo's lawyer opens the door to testimony from Deion in a prior case. Deion's lawyer, Harvey Steinberg, told Kamrani that he doesn't expect Shilo's lawyers to open that door. The trial arises from an effort to discharge an $11.89 million civil judgment in a personal-injury case arising from an altercation at Shilo's school in 2015. The key question is whether the injuries were "willful and malicious." If so, the debt survives. If not, the debt will be avoided.
author: Mike Florio

title: Al Michaels made a "Lake America" joke during Patriots-Browns game
summary: Legendary play-by-play specialist Al Michaels returned to the booth on Thursday night for the Prime Video preseason game, between the Patriots and the Browns.
full_text: Legendary play-by-play specialist Al Michaels returned to the booth on Thursday night for the Prime Video preseason game, between the Patriots and the Browns. And Michaels, who has been known to make a non-football topical reference or two , commented on one specific current event during the game. "That is Lake Erie," Michaels said while the screen displayed an overhead shot of the Browns' stadium. "We think it is still called Lake Erie on the right. We're not quite sure at this point. But we'll be by Lake something like Ontario or whatever it's going to be called by the time we get to Buffalo [for Week 2]. "Anyway, you know what I'm talking about, some of you do. Read the news." It was a reference to the recent decision by the Commander-in-Chief to unilaterally rebrand Lake Ontario as Lake America, given the latest iteration of the periodic squabbles with Canada. Making the remark somewhat surprising is that Michaels, who doesn't wear his politics on his sleeve, is widely believed to be far more aligned philosophically with the man who made the change that provided the basis for the joke. Which could make it a tangible example of the reality that even the most ardent supporters of 45/47 have become exasperated and exhausted by his objectively tired and predictable shtick. It's also a reflection of the fact that Michaels has been doing it long enough to say whatever he wants to say, whenever he wants to say it. With his former habit of making subtle (or otherwise) references to the betting line and over-unders in the days the NFL despised gambling now far less noteworthy given the normalization of all things betting, Michaels needs to find other ways to display some periodic cheekiness.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bill Belichick continues to say he's focused on UNC, not the NFL
summary: As should-be Hall of Fame head coach Bill Belichick prepares for his second season in college with an opening game in Ireland, he was asked if he ever sees himself returning to the NFL.
full_text: As should-be Hall of Fame head coach Bill Belichick prepares for his second season in college with an opening game in Ireland, he was asked if he ever sees himself returning to the NFL. "I'm focused on UNC right now absolutely ," Belichick said, via Brian Murphy of WRAL. "I've recruited these kids, two years with them, been with these guys. I want to help them. I had a great experience in the NFL, but I'm very happy at North Carolina. I'm excited to be there. Excited about the future of our program." The reality is that Belichick won't have a chance to return to the NFL unless someone wants him. Through three hiring cycles since the Patriots fired Belichick, he has had one interview. This year, with 10 openings, his name never came up. Last year, the Raiders and Tom Brady hired Pete Carroll without taking a serious look at Belichick. It's difficult if not impossible to imagine Belichick back in the NFL. No fan base is clamoring for him. No front office will want to work with him. No owner will become smitten with the notion that he'll turn an also-ran into a champion. The bigger question is whether he'll unlock a third season at North Carolina. If this season goes like last season for UNC, he may be SOL in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones says he doesn't have a succession plan (but he clearly does)
summary: Jerry Jones has owned the Dallas Cowboys since 1989.
full_text: '' Jerry Jones has owned the Dallas Cowboys since 1989. The single transaction has become intertwined with his very identity. Jerry Jones is the Cowboys and, for better or worse, the Cowboys are Jerry Jones. That's why it's no surprise Jerry said in a recent interview with Zak Keefer of The Athletic: “ I don’t have a succession plan , I don’t. One day I just won’t be here to toss my two cents in.” It's another example of Jerry's legendary hyperbole. Of course he has a succession plan; the league office mandates that, each year, the owner of every team provide the name of the person who would take the reins if an owner dies or becomes incapacitated. It's been obvious for years that, whenever Jerry "won't be here to toss my two cents in," Stephen Jones will be the one running the show. And the article focuses heavily on the potential differences between Jerry and Stephen, as the person in charge of the team. It also centers on one of the biggest disagreements they ever had, when Jerry wanted to take quarterback Johnny Manziel in round one of the 2014 draft and Stephen spearheaded an effort to take offensive lineman Zack Martin instead. Keefer has this jarring quote from Stephen, regarding his recollection of Jerry's reaction to the Martin selection. “I hope you’re happy,” Stephen said, quoting Jerry. “You don’t do special things in life — I would have never bought the Dallas Cowboys — making middle-of-the-road decisions. And what you just did is down the middle. . . . You’ll never be great.” Martin proved to be the greatest player still on the board when the Cowboys picked at No. 16. And, along with Mike Evans, Aaron Donald, and possibly Khalil Mack, Martin is one of the handful of future Hall of Famers from that draft. (Davante Adams, taken in round two, has a chance to get there, too.) Manziel, in turn, was an all-time bust. Which should make Cowboys fans feel a little bit better about an inevitable future in which Stephen will be driving the giant bus with a blue star on each side.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders' online store sells out of merchandise with old name and logo
summary: Controversial or not, there's an appetite for merchandise with the Commanders' outdated name and logo.
full_text: Controversial or not, there's an appetite for merchandise with the Commanders' outdated name and logo. Via Eric Flack of WUSA, who first reported on the sale of gear bearing the abandoned name and logo earlier this week, all items featuring the old logo and name at the team's online store have sold out . Per Flack, items remain available at the team's brick-and-mortar store. The Commanders defended the decision to sell gear with the name and logo by citing accuracy in honoring franchise alumni. The team also mentioned the necessity of keeping its trademark rights viable. The Association on American Indian Affairs promptly spoke out about the apparent backslide toward a name that has evolved over time into a dictionary-defined slur . The latest use of the name is the most blatant embrace of it since the name was dropped in 2020. Time will tell whether the Commanders continue to push the envelope regarding the renormalization of the name — and whether the name, at the right time and under the right circumstances, will officially return.
author: Mike Florio

title: Robert Saleh: Wan'Dale Robinson being evaluated for concussion after "cheap" hit in Bears joint practice
summary: Titans head coach Robert Saleh gave an update on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson after Robinson made an early exit from Thursday's joint practice with the Bears.
full_text: Titans head coach Robert Saleh gave an update on wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson after Robinson made an early exit from Thursday's joint practice with the Bears. Saleh said that Robinson is being evaluated for a concussion after taking a hit from Bears safety Xavier Woods during the session. The hit drew a response from Robinson's teammates on the field and from Saleh while he was at the podium for his press conference. Saleh called the hit by Woods "cheap." Woods played for the Titans last season and was released shortly after Saleh was hired this year. Robinson signed with the Titans as a free agent in March. Robinson will go into the concussion protocol if doctors find he suffered a concussion Thursday. That would keep him out for several days, but would leave ample time for him to be cleared before Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tony Romo addresses his OWI arrest, through a spokesperson
summary: In more than a month since former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo was arrested for suspicion of operating while intoxicated, Romo has said nothing.
full_text: In more than a month since former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo was arrested for suspicion of operating while intoxicated, Romo has said nothing. He has finally spoken, albeit through a spokesperson. Via TMZ, the spokesperson has said this : "Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved." While it may be technically accurate under Wisconsin OWI laws to call a first offense a "civil matter," it didn't feel like one, look like one, or sound like one. He was pulled over. He was put through a field sobriety test. He was handcuffed, his mugshot was taken, he was booked. More importantly for his employment status, he was placed on leave by CBS eight days later. "We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps," the spokesperson said. So what would the next steps be? An abrupt return to the No. 1 CBS booth during the 2026 season? By all appearances, CBS has reconfigured its lineup not for a brief Romo absence but for a full season without him. A sudden return as of, say, Week 5 would be confusing. It would be awkward. It could create a distraction for CBS and a disruption to its apparent plans. The best play would be for Romo to take full responsibility not through a spokesperson but directly, in a press conference or an on-camera interview. And he should plead guilty to the various "civil" charges, pay his fine, and move on. Whether that's enough to keep CBS from moving on remains to be seen.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors related to May arrest
summary: Jacobs could be suspended under the Personal Conduct Policy.
full_text: Packers running back Josh Jacobs has been formally charged with two misdemeanors related to his May arrest in Wisconsin. According to multiple reports, the Brown County District Attorney's Office has charged Jacobs with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property. Those were two of the five charges that Jacobs initially faced in the arrest , which came after a domestic disturbance call, but prosecutors are not moving forward with a felony charge of strangulation and suffocation or two other misdemeanors. Jacobs has been available to practice and play for the Packers since the arrest, but he could face discipline under the league's Personal Conduct Policy as a result of the arrest. General Manager Brian Gutekunst said at a press conference this week that the Packers have prepared for a possible suspension during the 2026 season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Allen makes the case for grass fields everywhere
summary: Allen says he's had "numerous" turf burns that make it difficult to sleep.
full_text: When it comes to the issue of grass vs. turf (as well as any other player-related questions), it's important for the NFL's best players to add their voice to the cause. Bills quarterback Josh Allen, the NFL's MVP in 2024, has done so. "I think grass is healthier for our bodies," Allen said. "I'm to a point in my career now that when we practice inside on the artificial [surface], I can feel it the next day, and when we go out there [on grass], I feel great. I think any guy that was honest would tell you that's how they feel. So, one, I think it's healthier [as to] injury prevention. "I've gotten numerous, numerous burns on my legs from artificial turf, like, to the point where I can't sleep at night because it's bubbling over and, like, it's very painful. So I'm excited to not have to deal with that at home at least. I know we still probably will play games on the road that are turf, but if I can snap my fingers and make every field grass, that's what I would do, for sure." This year, Allen and the Bills will play on artificial turf in Week 1 (at Texans), Week 5 (at Rams), Week 9 (at Vikings), Week 10 (at Jets), and Week 13 (at Patriots). The issue of getting rug burns on fake grass is a problem. Injuries like that won't end up in the NFL's calculation of injury rates between grass and turf. But it's painful. And unsanitary, especially with the billions of toxic rubber pellets and all of the other stuff (spit, sweat, blood, vomit) that end up interspersed with the plastic. From a 2022 article published by the National Institutes of Health: "Numerous studies have shown that chemicals identified in artificial turf, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), phthalates, and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), are known carcinogens, neurotoxicants, mutagens, and endocrine disruptors. . . . [F]ew laboratory and epidemiology studies have been performed on the potential health impacts of artificial turf in athletes and communities, despite the abundance of evidence of carcinogens, neurotoxicants, mutagens, and endocrine disruptors in its components." In other words, it's obviously not healthy for humans to be exposed to the various components of a turf field. The compounds get in player abrasions, in their mouths, in their noses, in their eyes. It seems inevitable that, with further research, a study will emerge linking playing on artificial turf fields with one or more specific and serious long-term health risks. Until then, many NFL teams will opt for the fake stuff, because it's cheaper to install and maintain — and because it's easier to have non-football events in stadiums that use it. And all of them will hide behind the inherently misleading notion that the injury rate is identical on grass and turf.
author: Mike Florio

title: Klint Kubiak still doesn't name a starting quarterback for Week 1
summary: The Raiders face the Dolphins in 17 days.
full_text: The Raiders' preseason has ended. Both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza played in the finale, against the 49ers. After the game, coach Klint Kubiak still didn't name a starting quarterback. The audio was dead for the first couple of questions during Kubiak's postgame press conference. Apparently, one of them dealt with the QB1 issue. Via Vincent Bonsignore of the Las Vegas Review-Journal , Kubiak said he's not ready to name a starter for the Week 1 game at Miami. In the portion of the press conference for which the sound was on, Kubiak arguably spoke about Mendoza as a player who may not be spending extensive time practicing or playing moving forward. "He needs another three preseason games," Kubiak said. "You know, all those rookies do. And now that the season's starting, you know, the practice reps get smaller, and that's just life. But, us as coaches, we gotta get them ready to play, keep developing them." Later, Kubiak said regarding Mendoza, "We got him plenty of time, and I'm happy where he's at, but we just got to keep pushing him to be better." Regardless, Kubiak hasn't named a starter. And the first real game is only 17 days away.

title: Raiders' Klint Kubiak still won't name Week 1 QB starter, here's why all signs point to Kirk Cousins
summary: Kubiak has said it's Cousins' job to lose, but won't officially name a QB1
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are making us wait a bit longer to find out who the starting quarterback will be, as the competition between veteran Kirk Cousins and rookie first overall pick Fernando Mendoza comes to a close. Head coach Kirk Kubiak has been adamant about waiting to name his QB1, though many signs have pointed to Cousins as their guy. With just over two weeks until the team's opener against the Miami Dolphins , the mystery remains, but the hints are there.
Following the team's final preseason game, Kubiak said his No. 1 overall pick could benefit from a few more preseason games, but unfortunately for Mendoza, that's not something he has. The NFL now only holds three preseason games per team, meaning the players, especially the rookies, have less time to prove themselves and get those valuable in-game reps.
"[Mendoza] needs another three preseason games, all those rookies do. Now that the season's starting the practice reps get smaller and that's just life," Kubiak said after the Raiders' 18-12 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday. "Us as coaches we gotta get them ready to play, keep developing them."
The HC noted that this time in the preseason is beneficial not only for the rookie to learn from his own reps but also for him to learn from Cousins. Kubiak called the time "very valuable" for Mendoza.
"I'd love to play [Mendoza] the whole game but there's other guys we want to get looked at and I thought overall this preseason that we got him plenty of time," Kubiak said.
Both played in Thursday's game, with Cousins taking the first two drives and Mendoza taking over until the beginning of the fourth quarter, when he was swapped for Aidan O'Connell .
The 38-year-old went 8 of 11 with 51 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions, while Mendoza went 7 of 14 with 57 yards, no touchdowns, an interception and two sacks, producing a low passer rating. It was not as strong as his debut, where Mendoza went 10 of 16 with 97 yards, one touchdown and one sack against the Arizona Cardinals .
Cousins began training camp as the starting quarterback and has been listed first on the depth chart throughout the practices. He's led the first-team offense through training camp and has seemed to have the edge in the competition since the beginning. When Cousins has struggled, Mendoza hasn't been able to outplay him when his chances come. Despite some great moments in camp, Mendoza had some lowlights as well, including a pick-six during joint practice with the Texans.
At the start of preseason, Kubiak said Cousins was in charge of his own fate , noting, "Kirk's been getting the reps with the ones. I think he's had a solid training camp, and it's his job to lose."
He referred to Cousins as the starter on Day 1, on July 28, but hasn't mentioned it again since then.
"When we go out to practice tomorrow, Kirk Cousins is the starting quarterback," Kubiak said at the time. "He's the guy, and he's going to get a ton of reps. He deserves them because he's played really good football. But I want Fernando and I want Aidan (O'Connell) to push him."
Looking at his preseason numbers compared to Mendoza, Cousins hasn't struggled enough to hand the rookie the job, and the No. 1 pick hasn't excelled enough to make an obvious leap ahead.

title: Christian Gonzalez landing spots: Cowboys, Giants among trade candidates as Patriots CB seeks record contract
summary: Gonzalez and the Patriots are reportedly not close to striking a long-term deal
full_text:
Christian Gonzalez easily stands among the most talented cornerbacks in the NFL . As he graduates from his rookie contract to his first megadeal, he ought to be compensated as such. The New England Patriots have been outward in their willingness to pay a premium to keep Gonzalez around for the long term, but according to ESPN , the sides are not close to an agreement.
Patriots owner Robert Kraft said at the start of training camp that the team offered Gonzalez a contract that would make him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. That, however, was before Seattle Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon reset the market with a four-year, $132 million extension. That deal raised the bar for Gonzalez and appears to have raised it too high for the Patriots.
"I don't think that at any one point here that they have been close to a deal," ESPN's Adam Schefter said on "The Pat McAfee Show." "Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez have the same agent, so in a way, he can kind of dictate how this is going to go and see into the future in a better way than each of the two teams can. Witherspoon was going to get done first, and it got done at an average of $33 million a year. The Patriots have not been in that category. Witherspoon has established the benchmark, and the Patriots haven't gone there. They weren't there before, and they don't appear to be going there right now."
To be clear, there is no immediate deadline for this deal to get across the finish line. The Patriots picked up Gonzalez's fifth-year option for 2027, and he has not threatened to hold in during training camp or sit out of regular-season games.
In a now deleted tweet reacting to the Adam Schefter news saying the Patriots and Gonzo aren’t close to a deal, Christian Gonzalez trainer says the Patriots should just trade him. He is saying what the Patriots have been behind the scenes. There is a lot more to this story. pic.twitter.com/uXcIKVD4me
Anytime a team struggles to find an acceptable number for a star player, though, the negotiations come with the risk of blowing up . The Micah Parsons saga last summer proved how teams can ultimately lose the best players on their rosters if they are unwilling to pay a premium.
"I have conversations with Christian, and I understand that this is probably something that's difficult," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said, via Patriots wire . "I've never been in that position to this extent. Try to treat it with class, but he and I communicate, and our players are always free to feel how they feel. They just have to stay patient and just hope that we can work to some kind of agreement."
The Patriots could do what the Dallas Cowboys did in 2025 and trade their defensive asset, but for a team squarely in its contention window (and with a reigning MVP runner-up quarterback on his rookie contract, no less), parting with a player of Gonzalez's caliber over a contract dispute would be an extreme move. That does not mean it will not happen, though, so here are a few potential landing spots should Gonzalez be moved out of New England.
Jerry Jones has been hinting for a while that he'd be interested in making another big move, even if in the past 12 months he's already made plenty: trading away Micah Parsons, trading for Quinnen Williams and moving up to draft Caleb Downs . When the Cowboys opened training camp, he said he'd be "very interested" to "give up the future to substitute where we are today."
Dallas has made a concerted effort to improve its secondary, not just with Downs, but with free agents Jalen Thompson and Cobie Durant. But after a woeful 2025, a player like Gonzalez would take this secondary to an entirely different level -- not only a No. 1 cornerback, but a superstar one. Gonzalez is in the upper tier at a position the Cowboys look middling at best. He's a big name. Maybe Jones pulls off the reverse Parsons, acquiring a disgruntled star in his prime and paying him, rather than trading one away.
As recently as this summer, the Lions had to have felt great about the state of their cornerback group. Terrion Arnold's arrest, release from the roster and plans to sign with the Seahawks flipped the unit on its head. All of a sudden, D.J. Reed is thrust into the No. 1 job, and the depth behind him is questionable. That is not to mention the injury woes that continue to plague the rest of the defensive backfield.
Bringing in Gonzalez to not only fill Arnold's shoes but also potentially provide an upgrade over his production would be a home-run move for a team that needs to make strides defensively in order to get back to the playoffs. Signing him to a long-term deal would limit the Lions' flexibility at other positions, but they can afford it so long as it does not go into effect until next year.
Commanders fans have looked at Gonzalez and wondered "what if?" ever since the 2023 NFL Draft . Washington took Emmanuel Forbes 16th overall, one pick before Gonzalez went to New England. Forbes didn't even last two seasons before being cut.
Washington went on a spending spree this offseason on defense, but is still set up to have a relatively open checkbook in the future, even with a potential Jayden Daniels extension. Adam Peters has pulled off big trades for Marshon Lattimore (which didn't work out) and Laremy Tunsil (who played excellently last year but tore his triceps in training camp this year). Might he have another big move up his sleeve?
For the "buyer beware" idea, Gonzalez is much younger than either Lattimore or Tunsil was when they were acquired; he's an ascending superstar, having just turned 24. The Commanders have gotten younger, faster and more athletic all offseason, and this would continue that trend. Trey Amos has missed almost all of training camp, and the rest of the group has been inconsistent. It's a win-now year for Dan Quinn and, if it's a bad year, Peters would be under a microscope, too. Washington never should have let Gonzalez slip past them. This regime could right the old one's wrong.
A young and inexpensive core gives the Giants all the flexibility they need to not only acquire Gonzalez now but also make him the highest-paid cornerback in league history. To place a cornerback entering his prime on the same defense as recent first-round picks Arvell Reese and Abdul Carter would set that unit up to flourish as a talent-rich operation for years to come.
The Giants can easily move on from Greg Newsome II after signing him to a one-year, $8 million deal, which would clear a lane for Gonzalez to form a tandem with Paulson Adebo , who remains under contract for the next three seasons.
The young pieces are starting to fall into place with the aforementioned defenders plus Jaxson Dart , Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo . Any established stars New York can pair them with would be welcome additions that could help fast-track the team's rise to contention.
Gonzalez isn't the only cornerback at a frustrating impasse with his team. In Pittsburgh, Joey Porter Jr . and the Steelers are at odds. Porter is technically still on the PUP list, but really, it's a hold in regarding his contract. As such, the Steelers might be able to offer New England something other teams could not: a good young player at the same position Gonzalez plays.
This, of course, would be contingent on the Patriots presenting a financial solution to Porter and the Steelers doing the same for Gonzalez. Maybe dealing with Gonzalez within the AFC is a non-starter for New England anyway. But the Steelers are giving it one more go with Aaron Rodgers , and there's a very good defense opposite him. It could go from very good to elite with Gonzalez.
