title: What's next for Shedeur Sanders? NFL sources question whether Browns QB has a starting future
summary: After Deshaun Watson won Cleveland's starting job, NFL coaches and front-office officials explain why Sanders faces an uncertain future -- and why some teams wouldn't trade for him even if he became available
full_text:
Leading up to the Browns ' preseason game against the Bills last week, there was a widespread expectation inside the Cleveland building that Deshaun Watson would prevail over Shedeur Sanders to win Cleveland's starting quarterback job.
While it was fair to question afterward whether the sloppy showcase from Watson in that game, and even more so his well-publicized postgame comments, could impact head coach Todd Monken's thought process with the competition, it didn't end up deterring Monken from going with the quarterback he believes clearly gives the Browns the best chance to win -- Watson, whom he officially named as Cleveland's starting QB Monday morning.
However, because of Saturday, the Browns are left with additional external skeptics that Watson will have any success as Cleveland's starting quarterback. It's also led to another question among some in NFL coaching and front office circles: What's next for Sanders now that he's officially lost this competition?
The short answer: There aren't many,  if any, NFL front office staffers that view him as an NFL starting-caliber quarterback.
"Him not even being able to beat out Deshaun (who hasn't played in an NFL regular season game since his first Achilles injury in 2024) is probably telling," an NFL front office staffer told CBS Sports.
To be clear, there have been some positives from Sanders these last two years in Cleveland, including the 24-year-old finishing 9-for-11 against the Bills on Saturday with a touchdown pass and an interception that was a byproduct of a catchable pass tipping into the air off of the hands of his intended receiver. There's also still a clear chance he could end up starting at some point this season depending on the play of Watson.
However, it shouldn't come as a surprise that the universal expectation around the league is that the future of the Browns' quarterback room is currently playing for a college team and that it's not Sanders, Watson, 2025 third-round draft pick Dillon Gabriel or rookie sixth-round selection Taylen Green . There are also even questions about Sanders' fit as a backup, including -- fair or not -- because of the celebrity and distraction components that come along with him being such a high-profile and polarizing figure.
That factors into why front office officials from multiple NFL teams have told CBS Sports that they wouldn't have interest in trading for Sanders even if he were available.
"Do you really want to deal with that (especially with someone who's not your starting quarterback)?" a front office staffer said.
It's not like any of this should come as a shock.
Sanders slipping to the fifth round of last year's NFL wasn't just because of some pre-draft team interviews that reportedly didn't go well or concerns about him being a distraction. Frankly, there were a number of personnel and scouting sources who'd told CBS Sports during the buildup to the draft that they didn't have starter grades on Sanders and that -- just from a skill set perspective -- they questioned his capability to become an effective starter at the NFL level.
Though Sanders wound up being the Browns' starting quarterback for their final eight games last season, his QB rating (68.1) ranked last in the NFL among quarterbacks with more than 22 pass attempts. NFL sources also still see clear weaknesses in his game -- beyond just arm strength that's far from elite -- such as holding onto the ball too long and being a slow processor at times.
And while many who have been around Sanders describe him as likable and genuinely being of good character, there have also been sources critical of his preparation at different points and who have referenced him being challenging to manage at times, including last year for example when he knew he wasn't going to be starting.
It's why there are even some around the NFL who even wonder if Gabriel would be a better fit as Cleveland's backup, referencing things such as his work ethic and the ability to function on short notice.
Nevertheless, at least for now, the Browns have indicated they're moving forward with Sanders as their backup quarterback and it remains to be seen how badly Watson would need to struggle for Sanders to get an opportunity to replace him as Cleveland's starter.
"All Monk cares about," a source said, "is being in the best position to win."
author: Matt Zenitz

title: Commanders offense called 'worst I've ever seen' in years: Fact or fiction from joint practice vs. Ravens
summary: Washington's offensive line looked awful, while Lamar Jackson and Baltimore offered plenty of reasons for optimism
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- If a neutral observer only saw the tail end of the Washington Commanders ' joint practice with the Baltimore Ravens , they would have said Washington more than held its own.
In the final drill, both teams got one possession, trailing by four with under a minute left. The Commanders' defense got a fourth-down stop when Mike Sainristil intercepted Lamar Jackson . The Commanders' offense followed that up with Jayden Daniels fading away from heavy pressure and lofting a beautiful pass to Antonio Williams for a touchdown. The Commanders' sideline erupted and stormed the end zone.
But if said observer had watched the entire two-hour session, they might have thought the two teams didn't even belong on the same field. Baltimore's thorough dominance was both eye-opening and telling of where both teams stand with the regular season two and a half weeks away.
Training camp and the preseason deliver us a lot of information at once. Some of it proves to be overreaction, but some of it proves prescient. As such, let's play a game of "fact or fiction" from Wednesday's developments.
By far the biggest mismatch was the Commanders' ragtag offense against Baltimore's defense, a unit already loaded with talent and poised to be one of the league's best under new head coach Jesse Minter.
Yes, Washington was without three starting offensive linemen -- LT Laremy Tunsil (torn triceps) will miss extended time, if not the whole season; C Nick Allegretti (calf) continues to miss much of training camp; and RG Sam Cosmi (illness) was also out -- and its top two running backs, Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White .
But at a time when teams are supposed to be building and evaluating depth, Washington looked in disarray. As longtime Commanders beat writer Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic posted ...
This is the worst I’ve ever seen the Commanders’ offense in years. Inoperable offensive line.
There were multiple miscues on snaps, the most basic aspect of football at any level, as sixth-round rookie center Matt Gulbin got first-team reps. Julian Good-Jones , who had been working at center in Allegretti's absence, shifted to right guard with Cosmi out but hardly fared any better. Tanoa Togiai also worked in with the first team.
If the day could be summed up in one play, it was Daniels being forced to field a wayward snap, only to throw an interception to Kyle Hamilton on a play doomed from the start.
"I feel like we were just out of sync, a little bit, with our combos," RT Josh Conerly Jr . said . "There was a little bit of a mixup in the lineup as well, so there were some guys next to each other that haven't worked next to each other all camp."
Daniels found Terry McLaurin for one chunk gain but otherwise was limited mainly to underneath throws, scrambles and would-be sacks.
"Not the best day that I thought we could have had, all-around, from myself to everybody else, but these are the opportunities that you get to learn from," Daniels said. "Good thing about it, man, it's August."
He's right. It is August. But August is slowly slipping away, and not in the right direction. In preseason Week 2 -- the only preseason action the starters got -- Daniels was heavily pressured on his first play and sacked on his second. Washington ran a draw on third down to escape any further damage and punted. As such, this joint practice seemed to be a crucial one, and it did not go well.
The offensive line is, plainly, a mess. The Commanders were never anticipating Gulbin playing significant snaps (and he still might not). Good-Jones has played two NFL snaps, back in the 2023 season finale. Togiai is an undrafted rookie. They are back-of-roster or practice-squad players.
"I gotta do my job at the end of the day," Daniels said. "They have to do their job. I'm never one to go out there and complain about X, Y and Z, because at the end of the day, I can [only] control what I can control. ... Julian, Matt, they're doing a tremendous job up front with the situation that they're in."
The situation they're in, though, is the issue. The entire operation can't just fall apart when backups are called upon. Injuries happen and, in fact, already have. There are limited ways to improve substantively this late in the preseason, but whether it's via free agency, waivers or trade, Washington must do so.
The season is by no means over. To say that would be ridiculous. But the past week -- the awful cameo against the Lions and the rough extended performance today -- shows Adam Peters and Dan Quinn that they desperately need to add up front. They've added five journeyman veterans since training camp opened, but much more significant work needs to be done. They are behind the eight ball, but they're not doomed to stay there.
The goal is for new offensive coordinator David Blough's schematic changes to make the sum greater than its parts. It will all be for naught, though, if the offensive line gives him no chance to do so. Here's one example: Blough drew up a beautiful play-action look for Daniels against the Lions, but John Bates -- a good blocking tight end who had missed significant time earlier in training camp -- got beat. Does Washington have the players to execute what could be a promising scheme?
The dots don’t lie. Burks wide open on the PA but … pressure/sack. pic.twitter.com/pYY7GhmaoP
If one were to look on the bright side, they'd see that Daniels himself has been terrific throughout training camp. Allegretti has been a quality backup (and sometimes starter) throughout his career, and the Commanders are bullish on what he provides at center, even though he has made only two starts there in his career. Cosmi is an excellent tackle, and while the falloff from him shouldn't be as steep as it is, this was a one-day absence for him. Coleman has looked mostly solid taking over for Tunsil at left tackle, though he, like most Commanders, was none too happy .
Croskey-Merritt and White could be a better running back tandem than most are giving them credit for, as Croskey-Merritt was ninth in the entire NFL in rush yards over expected per carry . McLaurin and Stefon Diggs form by far the best receiver duo Daniels has ever had, and Chig Okonkwo fits this offense to a T.
Furthermore, the defense should be miles better than it was last year. Neither Odafe Oweh nor K'Lavon Chaisson practiced Wednesday, but both dominated the Dolphins when Miami came to town a few weeks ago. Dorance Armstrong had back-to-back excellent reps, one of which might have been a sack of Jackson and the other of which almost certainly would have. He also had a nice run stop on Derrick Henry . There's going to be a transition period for Sonny Styles , but his speed alone will be crucial. Defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, like Blough on the offensive side, is trying to have the sum exceed its parts.
Lamar Jackson looked solid -- not spectacular, but certainly solid -- even without Zay Flowers . In an 11-on-11 drill, he fired a perfect pass outside to Rashod Bateman and also completed quick passes to Bateman and Elijah Sarratt for decent gains. He then hit Mark Andrews in the middle of the field for a chain mover.
His biggest play, though, was a strike to Devontez Walker , who had gotten between the linebacker and the safety. Walker took it to the house untouched. It's the final play below.
Offense stacking pic.twitter.com/3VvgcJTJtU
Jackson usually had plenty of time in the pocket, too. The offensive line did a stellar job in pass protection.
Jackson's biggest adjustment will be getting more under-center play action reps, but this is actually an area in which he's thrived.
Here are a bunch of examples of Lamar Jackson throwing over the middle of the field off under center play action Excited to see Declan Doyle put Jackson in more of these situations. From 2022-2025, Jackson ranked #1 in EPA/dropback off UC PA, per @SumerSports pic.twitter.com/1voQn3lckl
With a more physical offensive line than was in place last year, Derrick…

summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cardinals fans and fans across the country. full_text: Jun 9, 2026; Tempe, AZ, USA; Arizona Cardinals outside linebacker Josh Sweat (10) looks on during minicamp at Arizona Cardinals Training Center. title: The biggest positional questions that need to be answered versus the Packers
summary: The Arizona Cardinals end their exhibition schedule against the Green Bay Packers tonight. None of the starting players will suit up for the contest. Head coach Mike LaFleur has already stated that his starting offense and defense will not play, along with RB Jeremiyah Love and punter Blake Gillikin. What both the Packers and the […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Tre Tucker #1 of the Las Vegas Raiders picks up a first down on a pass play as BJ Ojulari #9 of the Arizona Cardinals defends in the first quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals end their exhibition schedule against the Green Bay Packers tonight. None of the starting players will suit up for the contest. Head coach Mike LaFleur has already stated that his starting offense and defense will not play, along with RB Jeremiyah Love and punter Blake Gillikin. What both the Packers and the Cardinals want to accomplish is to see which players to keep and which to send on their way to seek employment elsewhere. The final cutdown is this Sunday, August 30, at 4:00 p.m. (Eastern). RELATED: UPDATE FROM PACKERS-CARDINALS JOINT PRACTICE There are plenty of storylines that need to be solved. Will this final preseason game address those concerns, or will there be little resolution? Here are four questions that need answers this weekend: Who will play right guard? During training camp, rookie Chase Bisontis and Isaiah Adams were in a heated battle for the starting role. Then Bisontis suffered a knee injury against the Las Vegas Raiders and had surgery. Next, he was placed on season-ending IR. This left Adams (6’-4”, 315 pounds) as the default starter at right guard. However, he recently started having knee issues on his own during the joint practice sessions with the Packers. He did not travel to Green Bay and missed the Monday practice. Now what? His replacement on the depth chart is listed as Oli Udoh, but for the Green Bay game, it appears backup center Jon Gaines (6’-4”, 320 pounds) will either replace Adams or split time with Udoh. Gaines has had a very good training camp. He has looked really good when the second-team offense plays against the opponent’s second-string. Which is not really an apples-to-apples comparison, but it does show he has consistency. Udoh (6’-6”, 320 pounds) is fighting for a roster spot and played extensively against the Dallas Cowboys last weekend. He could become the starting right guard or become quality depth. He is entering his eighth NFL season with 74 games played and 22 starts, so the experience is there. It appears the job is Adams’ unless he cannot go due to an injury. But you can’t look past what Gaines has done so far this preseason and training camp. What will the coaching staff do with LB/DE B.J. Ojulari? The Cardinals did not choose Ojulari in Round 2 a few short years ago just to release him. But where is his production? This is his third year since being drafted in 2023, and he has a grand total of zero starts. He sat out all of 204 with a torn ACL, then began last year on the PUP list. He finally suited up in Week 11. So far, his NFL career consists of 49 total tackles, 5 sacks, 9 QB hits, and 11 pressures, among other stats. This is a guy who was named First Team All-SEC in his final college season. At LSU, he was a beast at rushing the passer with 16.5 sacks, 129 total tackles, and 25 tackles for loss. In his rookie year, he didn’t tear up the league or be named to the NFL All-Rookie Team, but he showed a lot of promise. He was good against the run and had a huge array of pass-rushing moves. Mostly, Ojulari (6’-2”, 248 pounds) was impressive with his change of direction and quickness. He needed some tutelage in losing bigger offensive linemen and consistency in the use of his hands. But again, he showed promise that better days were ahead of him and that he was coachable. Mike LaFleur on B.J. Ojulari's performance Thursday night: "I thought he did some good stuff in the game. He's a fast rusher off that edge right there. And I just think it's just for him just continue to get time on task value received. Continuing to practice. Obviously there's a… — Josh Weinfuss (@joshweinfuss) August 9, 2026 This year’s training camp, he has shown flashes. But are flashes enough to keep him? Other hybrid players such as Jordan Burch, Eku Leota, and Owen Pappoe are outplaying him. So far in the preseason, Ojulari’s numbers are: Panthers: 3 tackles Raiders: 1 tackle, 1 QB hit Cowboys: 3 tackles Yeah, as if at this point the head coach is going to say he's another bust — Dr. Shrimp Puerto Rico (@JkrempskiJerry) August 10, 2026 This Cardinals coaching staff does not care for one second where a player was drafted. They want the best 11 guys on the field at all times. These coaches did not draft Ojulari, so they have no skin in his game. What will the coaching staff do with DE Darius Robinson? Another guy drafted high and yet has not fulfilled his destiny. In this year’s training camp, Robinson (6’-5”, 290 pounds) has been a roller coaster. He will dominate one day and then disappear in the preseason games. Maybe he has learned how to outplay his Cardinals’ offensive counterparts, but can’t do anything against the talent in the league. Yes? No? Maybe? He has excellent size and agility. 12 sacks and 78 tackles in his final two years at Missouri, where he was a pass-rushing demon in a difficult conference. 21.5 tackles for loss tell you about his run-stopping ability. And right now, Robinson is listed as a starter on the defensive line. In most media projections of the final 53-man roster for Arizona, every single one has Robinson listed. So far in preseason, he has one tackle, and that’s it. Coming to the Cardinals, Robinson’s role was to wreak havoc in the opponent’s offensive backfield. But so far, he has just two sacks in two seasons, along with 5 tackles for loss, 3 QB hits, and 6 pressures. He has struggled to consistently rack up sacks or explosive pass-rush plays. Maybe DC Nick Rallis should keep him at one position instead of moving him to various spots along the defensive line like he was a “Swiss Army knife.” Keep him at one position, and let him live or die there. One word? Underperforming. He was taken with the 27 th pick in the first round, for goodness ‘ sake. He is not fulfilling the idea of him coming in and becoming that complement to Josh Sweat. What kind of depth do the Cardinals have at cornerback? Arizona has a really good defensive backfield. They better, because the NFC West Division is full of exceptional receivers and quarterbacks who can place the ball. However, name a player in the Cardinals’ cornerback room who has never been hurt? Exactly. So, the depth machine has got to be there and become a plug-and-play. Will Johnson could become one of those league-wide known corners – if he can remain on the field. Garrett Williams has solidified this group with his veteran presence – if he can remain on the field. Denzel Burke took over last year because of an injury and proved that he belonged in a starting role. Behind them has been a quagmire of talent. Max Melton has shown flashes but has had issues adjusting to the speed at the NFL level. He has had several injuries to his heel and knee. Sean Murphy-Bunting has provided entertainment in that he is a roller coaster himself. He is coming off a horrific knee injury from last year involving a torn ACL plus MCL damage that required surgery. The year before that, it was a neck issue plus a dislocated elbow. The Cardinals’ fanbase was surprised when the front office restructured his deal to a more incentive-laden contract and lowered his salary instead of releasing him. Kei’Trel Clark had found a groove after being drafted in Round 6 last year before ending up on IR with a back injury. He is fighting for the sixth and final roster spot in this room. He sustained a hip injury in the preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys but was playing well in training camp and had five total tackles in the preseason. title: Which Cardinals players will play Friday night
summary: The Arizona Cardinals will play the Green Bay Packers Friday night at Lambeau Field in the first “LaFleur Bowl.” It could be coined the “Melton Bowl,” as Max Melton is a cornerback for the Cardinals while his brother Bo Melton is a Packers receiver. Newly minted head coach Mike LaFleur of the Cardinals will face […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals looks to throw the ball during a preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals will play the Green Bay Packers Friday night at Lambeau Field in the first “LaFleur Bowl.” It could be coined the “Melton Bowl,” as Max Melton is a cornerback for the Cardinals while his brother Bo Melton is a Packers receiver. Newly minted head coach Mike LaFleur of the Cardinals will face off against his older brother Matt, head coach of the Packers. The two have faced off twice when Mike was the OC of the Los Angeles Rams, but this will mark the first time the siblings have squared off while each was an NFL head coach. RELATED: CARDINALS ACTIVATE SWEAT Traditionally, NFL teams do not play any starters in the final preseason game. The coaching staff already knows what they have with their starting players, and the big question marks are involved within the bottom third of the roster. “The Turk” arrives on Sunday, August 30, as NFL teams must announce their 53-man rosters. Currently, teams can have as many as 90 guys in camp. The difficult aspect for the coaches is to find out which players to retain. No coach wants to cut a guy who becomes a valued member of another franchise at some point. Think Kurt Warner. With this in mind, how many starters on offense, defense, and special teams will be playing? The Arizona version of LaFleur answered that question and stated that none of the starters will play. That includes rookie RB Jeremiyah Love, who is still nursing an ankle injury. As far as the quarterback room, only Gardner Minshew and Kedon Slovis will play. Rookie Carson Beck hasn’t thrown a pass in any recent practice as he is healing from a rib injury he suffered in the Hall of Fame Game and has been sidelined ever since. Because Jacoby Brissett is the starting QB, he will not even suit up. Mike LaFleur confirmed that most of the starters will not play, but might be a couple exceptions of a player or two starting Sept 13 playing Friday in Green Bay #AZCardinals — J.P. Shadrick (@jpshadrick) August 26, 2026 Although we stated that none of the other starters will play, well, that just might be incorrect. It is possible to see DE Josh Sweat out there for a couple of series. He hasn’t been practicing and has zero snaps in the three other exhibition games. Perhaps the coaching staff will want him to dust off the rust a bit. Then again, they could just sit him and let the Week 1 outing become his dust-off. LaFleur did touch a bit on Sweat despite him getting in only one workout: “It was great to have him out there. When you get some of those pieces out there, you can feel it with the other guys, too. They were happy to see him again. He’s according to plan. It’s right on schedule in terms of when he was going to get out there. He’ll be out there again today doing some individual drills, and we’ll just kind of take it one practice at a time.” This match will be strictly for jobs. The game will feature backup players, rookies, and roster bubble candidates fighting for final spots on both sides of the ball before roster cuts. That includes backup punter Jack Browning, who played for the Orlando Storm of the UFL this past spring. title: Reasons why the Cardinals released Trey Benson
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are going into the 2026 season with arguably the best running back room in the league. The offense will improve this year with several new pieces in place. The Cardinals went into training camp with a packed and talented running back room. RELATED: CARDINALS SIGN BENSON TO ROOKIE CONTRACT Having selected Jeremiyah […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals are going into the 2026 season with arguably the best running back room in the league. The offense will improve this year with several new pieces in place. The Cardinals went into training camp with a packed and talented running back room. RELATED: CARDINALS SIGN BENSON TO ROOKIE CONTRACT Having selected Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick in this year’s NFL draft added to the talent of the group. Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort had already signed Tyler Allgeier from the Atlanta Falcons during the free agency period. Bam Knight and Corey Kiner were also re-signed from last year’s roster. However, there were two big question marks: Veterans James Conner and Trey Benson. Both were injured and placed on IR last year. What was their status? Training camp was expected to answer those concerns. At the beginning of last year, both were the starting running backs. And now? On Monday, the questions regarding Benson were answered. The Cardinals released him with a waiver/injury designation. He came to Arizona as a third-round draft pick in the 2024 NFL Draft after two seasons at Florida State when he rushed for 990 and 906 yards in his final two seasons. He also scored 23 touchdowns during this time span, so he knew where the end zone was. Teams don’t usually release third-round draft picks after just two seasons. What were the reasons why the coaching staff gave up on him? Lack of trade market Benson had a great opportunity when Conner went down to injury in Week 3 last year. Unfortunately, Benson suffered a significant meniscus injury the following week and was also placed on IR after surgery. But the recovery has lingered into training camp this year. The #Cardinals have waived RB Trey Benson, who was their 3rd-round pick in 2024. pic.twitter.com/TcEJMmj2qk — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 24, 2026 Benson certainly had trade value – if he was healthy. Certainly, the club wasn’t going to keep all eight running backs on the roster, and he was a third-round pick. During training camp, Benson had a flare-up with his left knee that kept him out of practices. He did not play in any preseason games and wasn’t practicing. The team had an option to place him on IR once again, which would have ended his season. This would have allowed Benson to get completely healthy and come back next year. They could also have kept him on the 53-man roster and then, the following day, placed him on IR, which would have allowed the Cardinals to bring him back at some point during this season. By being sidelined, this eliminated any trade interest. Nobody wants a vehicle that has a blown engine. Too many health issues The injury last year wasn’t pretty. It came at a horrible time in Benson’s athletic career. When Conner went down, it was Benson’s chance to become the starting back for an NFL club, and he went down in the very next game. His practice window opened up, but the coaching staff never reinstated him. Yeah his lower body may just be mush at this point pic.twitter.com/1XWrmsYTjS — tjm (@TMundy_15) August 24, 2026 His meniscus injury has caused issues, which have kept Benson out of practices and games. In his rookie year, he had an ankle injury that caused him to miss the final two games. He was placed on IR because of his injury. As a rookie, Benson finished the season with 291 yards and a touchdown on 63 carries and 59 yards on six catches, so he didn’t tear up the league or get named to the NFL All-Rookie Team. In college, he missed the entire 2020 season with a torn ACL. Benson is a talented back – that is a known commodity. However, all of this points to him being injury-prone, and in all likelihood, that would continue. No club wants to pay a guy to sit on IR, especially repeatedly. Other backs shoved Benson out the door Most NFL teams keep either three or four backs. The Cardinals have eight in camp. That means whoever isn’t named Love and Allgeier must have a great camp and preseason to be retained. Conner has been given the first option to stay. Even though the coaching staff is new and hasn’t gotten comfortable with him, they all know his athletic background. He is a bruising back, so his goal-line presence is a huge plus. He is a nine-year veteran who has rushed for over 6,000 yards with 72 touchdowns scored. And other running backs have shown promise. In the three preseason games, Bam Knight had 12 carries for 58 yards (Panthers), led the team in rushing, 3 carries for 15 yards (Raiders), and no stats against Dallas. He also did not have any kickoff returns, which has been one of his duties in the past. Corey Kiner had 10 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown against the Cowboys; he led all rushers against the Raiders with 10 carries for 59 yards and had 14 carries for 57 yards and one TD in the Hall of Fame Game. Even Evan Hull has shown the coaches something and led all rushers with 11 carries for 51 yards against Dallas. Conner has not carried the ball yet in the preseason. Most likely, the coaches do not want him to become re-injured and will wait until the regular-season games begin. That is, if he remains on the roster. One – or two – of these players have played sound, practiced well, and have shown more promise than a guy who is more likely to end up on IR rather than get 1,000-yards in a season. Running back Trey Benson cleared waivers today and he now reverts back to the Arizona Cardinals injured reserve list. pic.twitter.com/UMwfcKUzKL — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 25, 2026 Benson cleared waivers and reverted to the Cardinals. The decision now is to keep him, place Benson on IR and rehab him in the building, or settle with him and outright release him. If that occurs, he will be on his own to get his body right. That decision matters more to him than the diagnosis does. Most likely, he will head to injured reserve or receive an injury/settlement designation.

summary: The Baltimore Ravens’ 2026 preseason will come to an end tonight against the Washington Commanders. Here’s what to watch: Even with many starting roles finalized, there’s still a ton to watch […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens center Corey Bullock (67) and guard Jovaughn Gwyn (54) walk onto the field before the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens’ 2026 preseason will come to an end tonight against the Washington Commanders. Most of the roster is set, but Baltimore Beatdown’s staff will still have their eyes on a few key position groups during the game. Here’s what to watch: Even with many starting roles finalized, there’s still a ton to watch out for. The big one is who gets the only starting job up for grabs, the center role, between Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethic Pocic. Beyond that, its depth. Do the Ravens keep three or four running backs with Adam Randall and Rasheen Ali? Who wins the fifth edge role between Adisa Isaac, Kaimon Rucker, and Ethan Burke? Can a cornerback force them to keep more than six on the roster? On the defensive line, you’ve got John Jenkins, Broderick Washington, Aeneas Peebles, Rayshaun Benny, and CJ Okoye fighting for probably three spots. And lastly, who gets the ninth spot in the offensive line group? Andrew Vorhees, Gerald Lichtenhan, Corey Bullock, and Diego Pounds are the ones fighting there. I don’t expect Carson Vinson to lose his spot to Pounds as the backup swing tackle. – Zach Canter There are a few position battles worth watching in this game, most notably at center. I am curious to see if Pocic will get the start over Gwyn tonight and whether or not he can show enough to win the starting role. Running back is another position to watch, as both Adam Randall and Rasheen Ali fight to prove they belong on the 53-man roster. No competition is more crowded perhaps than the defensive line, where players such as Aeneas Peebles, Rayshaun Benny, and CJ Okoye will duke it out for the one or two open spots at the position. I am also interested to see if Joe Fagnano can force the Ravens to keep three quarterbacks with another strong preseason game. – Dustin Cox My eyes will be on the defensive line rotation tonight. The battle between Aeneas Peebles and Broderick Washington has been well documented and to me, Peebles would be the pick for a final roster spot because of his upside as a pass rusher. Washington brings more solidity to the run game but Baltimore already has plenty of capable run stuffers along the defensive line. Obviously, the center competition by default has been cut down to Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn. Personally, I think Gwyn will be the starter week one and we’ll gradually see Pocic overtake that role as he continues to get healthy. However, the starters that are rolled out tonight should be an indication of how those final roster spots and rotations are going to be handled. – Stephen Bopst
author: Stephen Bopst

title: Top storylines for the Ravens’ preseason finale vs. the Commanders
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are just one game away from real football. Tonight at 6 p.m. ET, they will take on the Washington Commanders in their preseason finale with 53-man roster cuts due just 48 hours later. Here are the team’s biggest remaining questions heading into today’s game: Will a starting center emerge? A season-ending injury […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Ethan Pocic #77 of the Baltimore Ravens holds the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are just one game away from real football. Tonight at 6 p.m. ET, they will take on the Washington Commanders in their preseason finale with 53-man roster cuts due just 48 hours later. Here are the team’s biggest remaining questions heading into today’s game: Will a starting center emerge? A season-ending injury to Danny Pinter turned the Ravens’ starting center competition into a two-man race between Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic . The former has been praised for his athleticism, while the latter brings experience and leadership that could be valuable in a new offensive scheme. The battle is neck-and-neck. The division of reps tonight will be a key marker, as Pocic’s ramp-up from last season’s Achilles tear has limited his time with his potential fellow starters. If Gwyn still gets all of the first-team snaps, he likely has the job sewn up. But the Ravens could mix Pocic in with the first team, indicating the competition is still undecided, or even start him outright, suggesting he has surged ahead. Can an undrafted rookie make the 53-man roster? The Ravens historically retain at least one undrafted rookie on their 53-man roster. Last year, they kept three. But with two of those players returning and plenty of depth across the squad, there may not be room this time around. Outside linebacker Ethan Burke , offensive tackle Diego Pounds , and quarterback Joe Fagnano have all made strong cases, but will the Ravens move on from Adisa Isaac, Carson Vinson, or another player to accommodate them? All three of those players have already stood out in the preseason, so it might take an undeniable performance tonight vs. the Commanders to secure a roster spot. How will the Ravens pick from their defensive line depth? The Ravens have two moral locks at defensive tackle: Travis Jones and Calais Campbell. Broderick Washington could be a trade candidate but is otherwise guaranteed a place. Nnamdi Madubuike is somewhat of an X-factor, as his gradual ramp-up from last year’s neck injury could land him on injured reserve to start the regular season. Then there’s the depth. 2025 sixth-round pick Aeneas Peebles has flashed in the preseason and likely earned his place. One of John Jenkins and C.J. Okoye will take a roster spot as the backup nose tackle. The other will still have a case, as does seventh-round pick Rayshaun Benny. And then there’s David Olajiga, Aaron Graves, and Dion Wilson, who have all popped at different times this summer. Baltimore typically carries five defensive linemen, but depending on Madubuike’s status, there might be a case for six. That could lead the team to carry 26 defenders rather than their usual 25-25-3 offense-defense-special teams split, something Jesse Minter hinted was a possibility this week. I would argue Minter said nothing of the sort and in fact opened the door to keeping an extra player on one side of the ball! Should be defense, imo. This could also be trade bait – telling other teams that the player they may want to sign won’t be available. https://t.co/VZTsCS7MT5 pic.twitter.com/bWZ3ype3Ss — Nikhil Mehta (@nikknowsball) August 26, 2026

title: Ravens news: Best, worst case for Ja’Kobi Lane’s rookie year
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover best- and worst-case scenario’s for Ja’Kobi Lane’s rookie campaign, a 2026 season preview from The Athletic Football Show, and a key injury update for the Ravens’ Week 1 opponent. Let’s dive in! […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Ja'kobi Lane #6 of the Baltimore Ravens lines up against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover best- and worst-case scenario’s for Ja’Kobi Lane’s rookie campaign, a 2026 season preview from The Athletic Football Show , and a key injury update for the Ravens’ Week 1 opponent. Let’s dive in! Best/worst-case scenarios for Ja’Kobi Lane’s rookie year NFL offensive rookies: Best and worst case for 17 players in 2026 – Lance Zierlin (NFL.com) Best-case scenario: Baltimore’s new coaching staff showcases Lane from the jump and he rewards them by continuing his mastery in the red zone. He makes highlight-reel catches and finishes among the team leaders in touchdown grabs. Worst-case scenario: Lamar Jackson focuses his targets on Zay Flowers, Mark Andrews and others, leaving Lane to wait until the 2027 season for his chance to shine. Projected stats: 40 catches for 470 yards, 3 TDs. Excitement around rookie wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane has no doubt been the Ravens’ biggest storyline of the summer. But non-first-round wideouts have rarely seen a substantial target share as rookies for a variety of factors. Luckily for Lane, he is primed to overcome them all. John Harbaugh’s rookie tax: Under the last coaching staff, rookies who were not drafted to be immediate starters often had to earn their playing time on special teams before seeing much offensive or defensive involvement. But Lane has been held out of special teams work at training camp along with Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. He was even dressed in street clothes after a cameo in last weekend’s preseason game in Minnesota. There’s a new sheriff in town, and he and his deputies are looking for Lane to prove himself doing what he does best: catching passes. Lamar Jackson’s trust: Jackson’s chemistry with his receivers has been a key factor in their success. The two-time MVP has been working to develop his connection with Lane in camp, frequently testing the rookie with tough-but-catchable passes to figure out where he likes the ball best. They will need to fine-tune things in live action, especially over the middle, but the early results are promising. Lane has delivered with several highlight grabs, and Jackson has responded with more targets. Target competition: Zay Flowers just got paid like a WR1; now, expect the Ravens to feed him the ball like one. Mark Andrews and Rashod Bateman are also primed for bounce-back seasons, and Baltimore has a host of young pass-catchers jockeying for targets. This is firmly (and literally) in Lane’s hands. Talent wins out in the NFL; if he can take advantage of his early opportunities, the ball will continue to come. In short, there’s every reason to think he can eclipse Zierlein’s projection. How will the Ravens’ defense evolve under Jesse Minter? ‘The Athletic Football Show’ previews the 2026 Baltimore Ravens – Robert Mays (The Athletic) I’m interested in not only the overall quality of this, but also how they play. Do they feel like they can play a little bit more man coverage because they have Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey on the outside? Do they get a little bit matchier? The Chargers played two-and-a-half times the amount of quarters that the Ravens played last year. When the Ravens were at their best with this core of pieces two years ago when Mike Macdonald was there, it was these ideas. Even if the system and the language were the same with Zach Orr, stylistically, they had really drifted away from a lot of the stuff that they were doing with Macdonald when this was the best defense in the NFL. And so I think we’ll see them move back in that general direction. And I think with this collection of players and just what we’ve seen from Minter over the last couple of years, it’s a group that’s pretty easy to get excited about. Ravens’ Week 1 opponents get key injury update Colts CB Charvarius Ward Sr. returns to practice, expects to be ready for Week 1 vs. Baltimore Ravens – J.J. Stankevitz (Colts.com) Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward Sr. participated in individual drills during practice Tuesday and worked his way into a handful of full-team reps Wednesday, which stand as important developments after the veteran was sidelined for the last two weeks with a back injury… …In the immediate future, though, Ward’s availability for Sept. 13’s season opener against the Baltimore Ravens could be key. Cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt, who’s had an impressive preseason and has 38 career passes defensed, is suspended for Week 1; the Colts on Wednesday waived cornerback Mekhi Blackmon, who started 11 games during the 2025 season.

title: Ravens rookie film review: TE Josh Cuevas flashes versatility
summary: Baltimore’s second preseason game didn’t produce much offense on the scoreboard, but it gave us a better look at several young players who had smaller roles during the opener. Against Minnesota, Josh Cuevas showed why his athleticism and versatility make him an intriguing developmental tight end, offensive tackle Diego Pounds continued to strengthen his case […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens tight end Josh Cuevas (85) warms up before the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Baltimore’s second preseason game didn’t produce much offense on the scoreboard, but it gave us a better look at several young players who had smaller roles during the opener. Against Minnesota, Josh Cuevas showed why his athleticism and versatility make him an intriguing developmental tight end, offensive tackle Diego Pounds continued to strengthen his case for a roster spot with an impressive performance in the run game, and seventh-round guard Evan Beernsten finally received his first extended opportunity of the preseason. TE Josh Cuevas (Round 5, No. 173 overall) 36 snaps | 21 receiving | 13 run blocking | 2 pass blocking Cuevas’ 36 snaps against Minnesota gave Baltimore an opportunity to use him in several different roles. That allowed the fifth-round pick to show the athleticism and versatility that made him an intriguing addition to the tight end room. The most noticeable part of his performance was what he offered as a receiver. Cuevas flashed his straight-line speed on an underneath drag route, turning a short completion into a 23-yard gain once he got into space. That ability to create yards after the catch is an important part of his evaluation. Baltimore can manufacture opportunities for him underneath and allow his athleticism to take over once the ball is in his hands. Cuevas also showed good awareness against zone coverage, understanding when to settle into open space rather than continuing to run himself into coverage. He also showed the ability to elevate and attack the football vertically, while making a difficult contested catch in traffic. Josh Cuevas lead the Ravens receivers with 46 yards on 3 catches Did a nice job finding soft spots in zone, flashed athletically climbing the ladder for a ball and moving in space. Also noticed his effort as a blocker. pic.twitter.com/V0pZgJS3AB — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) August 26, 2026 His effort as a blocker was another encouraging part of the performance. Cuevas isn’t going to consistently overwhelm defenders with raw power, but the willingness is there. He competed through contact and continued working to stay attached to defenders. That matters for a player whose athleticism naturally makes him more appealing as a receiving tight end. The more functional he becomes as a blocker, the less predictable Baltimore becomes when he is on the field. Postgame takeaway: Cuevas’ Week 2 performance provided a good look at his receiving profile. He found openings against zone coverage, picked up yards after the catch, and competed at the catch point. The effort he showed as a blocker was equally important. Cuevas doesn’t need to become a dominant in-line blocker, but becoming reliable enough in that area would give Baltimore considerably more freedom in how it deploys him. OT Diego Pounds (undrafted free agent) 20 snaps | 10 pass blocking | 0 pressures allowed | 92.9 PFF run-blocking grade | 95.7 zone-blocking grade Pounds’ pass protection stood out during Baltimore’s preseason opener, but against Minnesota, it was his work in the run game that became the most impressive part of his performance. Pounds looked particularly natural working within Baltimore’s zone concepts. He showed the ability to run the train tracks, stay square while moving laterally and reach his landmarks without sacrificing control. His movement skills allowed him to get into position before contact, and once engaged, he showed enough power to displace defenders and create movement out of his gap. Diego pounds performed well for a second week in a row He allowed no pressure on 10 pass blocking snaps Last week his pass blocking stood out, but to me this week his run blocking was seriously good. Looks like such a natural athlete in space and being able to work… pic.twitter.com/zOvwAMleHr — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) August 26, 2026 The effort after initial contact continued to stand out as well. On one rep, Pounds stayed attached to his defender and drove him roughly 15 yards downfield. Plays like that don’t necessarily tell us much about his technical development, but they do show the temperament Baltimore wants from its offensive linemen. Pounds consistently looks to finish rather than simply completing his assignment and moving on. The grading reflected how effective he was. Pounds received a 92.9 PFF run-blocking grade, including a 95.7 grade on zone runs. More importantly, the film supported why those numbers were so high. His movement skills and comfort blocking in space make him a natural fit for what Baltimore is asking its offensive line to do. Postgame takeaway: Pounds continues to strengthen his case for a spot on Baltimore’s 53-man roster. Allowing zero pressures was another positive step in pass protection, but his comfort operating in space in the run game was the story of Week 2. Given the Ravens’ lack of established offensive tackle depth, Pounds is putting together the type of preseason that could make him difficult to leave off the roster. G Evan Beernsten (Round 7, No. 253 overall) 8 snaps | 77.6 offensive grade, third-highest on team After not getting much of an opportunity during the preseason opener, Baltimore finally gave Beernsten his first real look against Minnesota. Eight snaps obviously isn’t enough to make any definitive conclusions, but there were still a few traits that immediately translated from his college tape. The first was his hand quickness. Beernsten fired his hands immediately after the snap and consistently looked to initiate contact rather than waiting for defenders to attack him. His punch timing was solid, and he showed an understanding of how to establish his hands early in the rep. That initial contact is important for Beernsten because he isn’t going to win consistently through overwhelming length or raw physical tools. His game has to be built around technique, timing and positioning. Rookie Guard Evan Beernsten finally got his feet wet vs the Vikings Impressed by his hand usage, one thing I noted on his report was his quick and active hands. Did a nice job timing his punches. Only 8 snaps so not much to go off of, hope he gets more burn this week pic.twitter.com/1eDwcVieQQ — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) August 26, 2026 We saw some of that against Minnesota. Beernsten was quick out of his stance, established contact early and generally looked comfortable during his limited workload. He ultimately finished with Baltimore’s third-highest offensive PFF grade, an encouraging result considering these were his first meaningful preseason snaps. The difficult part of his evaluation is opportunity. Baltimore has already given several other young offensive linemen significantly larger workloads this preseason, leaving Beernsten with very little time to separate himself before roster decisions are made. Eight snaps can give the coaching staff something to build on, but it isn’t enough on its own to dramatically change the roster picture. Postgame takeaway: Beernsten made the most of a very limited opportunity. His quick hands, punch timing and urgency off the snap were all encouraging, and finishing with Baltimore’s third-highest offensive PFF grade gave him a positive starting point. His biggest problem isn’t necessarily his performance—it’s the lack of remaining opportunities. Unless Beernsten produces an exceptional final preseason game, his path to the 53-man roster remains difficult. At this point, he may be playing more to establish himself as a developmental player Baltimore wants to keep around than to outright win a roster spot. Final Thoughts Baltimore’s offense didn’t generate many points against Minnesota, but Week 2 still provided useful information about several rookies fighting to…

title: Buffalo Bills 53-man roster projection: At conclusion of preseason, before roster cuts
summary: The Buffalo Bills mounted a glorious comeback to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 28-27 on Thursday night to cap a 3-0 preseason. Now Brandon Beane, Joe Brady, and Co. have to trim the roster from 91 players to 53 by Sunday at 6pm EST. Therefore it’s time for my final roster projection of the summer. Quarterback […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 26: Sedrick Van Pran-Granger #62 of the Buffalo Bills looks on prior to his game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on October 26, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills mounted a glorious comeback to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 28-27 on Thursday night to cap a 3-0 preseason. Now Brandon Beane, Joe Brady, and Co. have to trim the roster from 91 players to 53 by Sunday at 6pm EST. Therefore it’s time for my final roster projection of the summer. Quarterback (2) Josh Allen Kyle Allen Allen won the QB2 battle — a competition that did have some legs in training camp — with another surgical performance in the second preseason game. He’s not the best backup in the NFL but appears comfortable in Joe Brady’s system. Running Back (4) * James Cook Ray Davis Frank Gore Jr. Ben VanSumeren Tipping the scales back to Gore Jr. after he demonstrated how he can make something out of nothing on multiple occasions against the Steelers and had another stellar blitz pickup on a Shane Buechele long completion for the second-straight week. This is no slight on Ian Wheeler. He was dynamic in the preseason. Gore Jr. has earned this spot on the roster that he’ll at least hold until Ty Johnson returns from what I’m predicting will be a IR designation to begin the season. Wide Receiver (6) D.J. Moore Khalil Shakir Josh Palmer Keon Coleman Skyler Bell Trent Sherfield No changes here — I wanted to include Mecole Hardman here as the primary punt returner. But he muffed a punt last season and had three drops in the preseason. I’m guessing Ray Davis will be the primary kick and punt returner this season. Yes, his initial muff was ugly. Tight End (3) Dalton Kincaid Dawson Knox Jackson Hawes Despite strong pushes by Keleki Latu and even Shane Zylstra, the Bills opt to keep their normal three tight ends on the roster. Do not sleep on Latu or even Zylstra getting practice-squad elevations this season. They’ve proven their worth this summer. Offensive Line (9) * Dion Dawkins Alec Anderson Connor McGovern O’Cyrus Torrence Spencer Brown Austin Corbett Lloyd Cushenberry Tylan Grable Sedrick Van Pran-Granger For now, I have nine Bills blockers making the roster but there are caveats galore here. Given that Jude Bowry was seen in a walking boot at practice this week, it’s sensible for this raw, high-upside rookie to start the season on IR, making room for another player on the 53-man roster. That player is Van Pran-Granger who, despite losing the backup center job to Cushenberry, pieced together a strong summer. Then there’s this reasonably distinct possibility — the Bills trim the roster to 52 players to prep to add a veteran blocker released by another team after they trade Van Pran-Granger to the Commanders (or another interior offensive line needy club). Defensive Line (6) * Ed Oliver Deone Walker T.J. Sanders Landon Jackson Greg Gaines Zane Durant No changes here, although Durant leaving the Steelers game late with what looked to be a non-serious injury, is worth monitoring. Inside Linebacker (4) Terrel Bernard Kaleb Elarms-Orr Dorian Williams Joe Andreessen Yes, I just advocated a place for Jenkins on the 53-man roster earlier this morning … but Andreessen is more of a proven commodity as a depth linebacker and special teams ace. He is ahead of Jenkins’ developmental track by a year, having first made the team in 2024. In this case, the Bills cling to hope Jenkins isn’t snagged by another club after Buffalo moves him to the practice squad. Rush Linebacker (6) Greg Rousseau Bradley Chubb Michael Hoecht T.J. Parker Javon Solomon Mike Danna Based on WAWW, Danna would not make the roster. He played the majority of the fourth quarter in the final preseason. That’s typically a dead giveaway that a player isn’t going to be part of the original 53-man roster to start a regular season. HOWEVER, Danna provides Buffalo serious experience on the edge — along with some interior rushing flexibility — and I expect Leonhard would want an extra rush linebacker over another inside linebacker (see: Keonta Jenkins). Although special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers probably would lean in the opposite direction. . Defensive Backs (10) Christian Benford Maxwell Hairston Dee Alford Davison Igbinosun Cole Bishop CJ Gardner-Johnson Jordan Hancock Jalon Kilgore Kani Walker Sam Franklin Jr. I’ve gone back and forth on Damar Hamlin — he was an afterthought this offseason but has parlayed a strong camp into a solid preseason, and I do think in a perfect world, the Bills would like to keep him as veteran experience at safety behind Cole Bishop and CJ Gardner-Johnson. For this projection, he’s left off the 53-man roster with Buffalo hoping he can be stored on the practice squad, although I do think it’s very possible Hamlin vs. Franklin Jr. is the final roster decision for Beane to make. Specialists (3) Reid Ferguson Tommy Doman Jr. Tyler Bass Hard to say if there’s been a clear winner in the punter battle — as both Mitch Wishnowsky and Doman only got cracks at it in the second preseason game. This one could go down to the wire. *Phidarian Mathis will begin serving his three-game suspension at the start of the regular season so he will not originally be on the 53-man roster Week 1. *Ty Johnson and Jude Bowry begin the season on IR in this projection

title: 4 Buffalo Bills who helped their cause vs. Steelers in preseason game No. 3
summary: The Buffalo Bills ended their 2026 preseason 3-0 with a dazzling comeback win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night, and now have 53-man roster decisions to make ahead of Sunday evening. Which roster-bubble players made a final push to make the team with their performance in the preseason finale, you ask? My answers below. […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - AUGUST 22: Buffalo Bills defensive end Mike Danna (51) leaves the field following the National Football League preseason game between the Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns on August 22, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buffalo Bills ended their 2026 preseason 3-0 with a dazzling comeback win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night, and now have 53-man roster decisions to make ahead of Sunday evening. Which roster-bubble players made a final push to make the team with their performance in the preseason finale, you ask? My answers below. EDGE Mike Danna I’m a staunch advocate of Bruce Nolan’s WAWW philosophy in the preseason, and Danna played a whopping 43 snaps, most of which came in the second half and well into the fourth quarter, so the writing may be on the wall regarding his future on the Bills. But it would’ve been nearly impossible for Danna to do more with his time on task late in this trio of Bills preseason games. Danna added three tackles, two more pressures, and another tackle for loss to his stellar preseason against the Steelers. I have no idea if the Bills will have room for Danna on the 53-man roster, and he feels like a potential poaching target on the practice squad. If I was the GM, I’d very much like to have a wily, versatile, thick defensive linemen with gobs of deep playoff experience in my back pocket, and that’s precisely what the 29 year old Danna is. LB Keonta Jenkins Am I the only one who visualizes Tremaine Edmunds when watching Jenkins in the Bills No. 49? In actuality, Edmunds was a first-round pick and stood at 6’5” and 250 pounds. Jenkins was undrafted out of Virginia Tech and is only 6’2” and probably in the 220-230 pound range now. But the long hair out of the back of his helmet and the way he effortlessly glides to the football is very Edmunds-esque. Jenkins had six tackles against the Steelers, one of a which was a thudding tackle for loss and tacked on a sack in his 24 snaps. Joe Andreessen did not play defense against Pittsburgh, which hints that he’s a lock to make the 53-man roster as the primary inside linebacker contingency plan. But Jenkins put quite the emphatic stamp on a summer in which he demonstrated that his arrow is pointed decidedly upward. RB Frank Gore Jr. Gore Jr., now three years into his professional career — it seems less than that, doesn’t it? — feels like a real pro’s pro at this stage, even though we’ve almost strictly seen him in training camp and the preseason. Making cornerbacks whiff in space on catches in the flat or screens, knifing his way through small crevices between the tackles, and morphing into a small cement wall in pass protection against an A-gap blitz, for the third-straight preseason, Gore demonstrated that he does everything well that teams ask of modern-day running backs albeit not against first-teamers. And he put multiple exclamation points on film against the Steelers to prove his well-roundedness. The two long gainers on short throws from Shane Buechele, a stick on a pass-pro rep that allowed Buechele to deliver a strike on a deep over, and gritty, just-take-what’s-there runs between the tackles. It was all there from Gore Jr. in this game. On 15 touches he totaled 72 yards from scrimmage and scored a touchdown. If Buffalo wants to take the precautionary route with Ty Johnson to begin the season — see: short-term IR — I believe Gore Jr. has done enough to earn an opportunity when the games count. OG Ar’Maj Reed-Adams Reed-Adams isn’t going to make the 53-man roster. But I can’t quit him. And that’s partly due to my affinity for him as a prospect. But he was an old-school workhorse MLB pitcher this preseason — the rookie guard logged another 67 snaps in the preseason finale against the Steelers. And once again, Reed-Adams did not allow a single pressure. It capped a debut preseason for Reed-Adams without surrendering a single quarterback pressure — he did have a holding call that negated one but otherwise was not flagged. The nearly 6’6” and 315-plus pounder has absolutely done enough to secure a spot on the practice squad, and I’m incredibly into his upside as, first, a deep-depth option, and eventually, a starter at either guard position on this team.

title: NFL waiver wire explained: How it affects the Buffalo Bills in 2026
summary: The Buffalo Bills just finished their preseason schedule on Thursday night with a home win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. With that comes one of the most difficult 72 hours the organization will face all season. Like every other team, the Bills must release a large amount of players in an effort to comply with the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - SEPTEMBER 12: DeWayne Carter #90 of the Buffalo Bills rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on September 12, 2024 in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills just finished their preseason schedule on Thursday night with a home win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. With that comes one of the most difficult 72 hours the organization will face all season. Like every other team, the Bills must release a large amount of players in an effort to comply with the NFL-mandated 53-man active roster requirement by 6 p.m. EDT on Sunday, August 30. To get there, Buffalo must release at least 38 players, some of whom will be subject to waivers. Should any of these players be waived this weekend, they have the potential to be claimed by another team ahead of the Bills in the waiver priority. Buffalo currently sits at 26 in the waiver wire priority. If another team doesn’t claim waiver-eligible players released by the Bills, their contract ends and they become free agents who can return to Buffalo as part of the team’s 17-man practice squad. All claims filed for players waived during final roster reductions this weekend are processed and awarded on Monday, August 31, 2026. After that happens, NFL teams can then officially begin assembling their practice squads after the final waiver claim is completed. What will a new coaching regime decide to do with Buffalo’s roster to begin the 2026 season? A team led by quarterback Josh Allen still cannot afford to make the wrong roster moves. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook believe the Bills will make the right decisions , and currently list the Bills with the best odds of making the playoffs in the AFC (-330), and the second-best odds (+1000) of winning Super Bowl LXI. Follow along below as we break down what this all means for the Bills and the rest of the NFL. Buffalo Bills subject to 2026 NFL waiver wire The Bills have 50 players who would enter the NFL’s waiver wire system if released at any point this season. It’s a list that includes players who are unlikely to be released, as well those players fighting for a roster spot this season. That means one should not expect the team to unwisely expose the bulk of their most recent rookie class to waivers, as well as young players with significant starting roles like Cole Bishop, Ray Davis, Maxwell Hairston, Deone Walker, and others. Players at most risk for release often play depth roles on a team’s roster. WR Skyler Bell OT/OG Jude Bowry OLB Cade Denhoff P Tommy Doman Jr. CB Jordan Dunbar DL Zane Durant LB Kaleb Elarms-Orr OG Bruno Fina ILB Theron Gaines CB Davison Igbinosun S Jalon Kilgore WR Ja’Mori Maclin OLB TJ Parker CB Toriano Pride Jr. OG Ar’maj Reed-Adams WR Max Tomczak CB Kani Waler OG Da’Metrius Weatherspoon DB Te’Cory Couch RB Frank Gore Jr. WR Stephen Gosnell C Sincere Haynesworth ILB Keonta Jenkins TE Keleki Latu DL Zion Logue CB D.J. Miller WR Quentin Skinner ILB Jimmy Ciarlo DL Travis Clayton (International Player Pathway) CB Maxwell Hairston DB Jordan Hancock TE Jackson Hawes DL Landon Jackson OLB Andre Jones Jr. OT Chase Lundt S Wande Owens DL T.J. Sanders DL Deone Walker RB Ian Wheeler ILB Joe Andreessen S Cole Bishop OG Nick Broeker DL DeWayne Carter WR Keon Coleman RB Ray Davis OT/OG Tylan Grable CB Anthony Kendall ILB Otis Reese IV OLB Javon Solomon C/OG Sedrick Van Pran-Granger What is the NFL waiver wire? Every NFL franchise must make decisions to finalize their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. As discussed above, some of those players enter the waiver wire protocol, while others immediately become free agents. Players with less than four accrued seasons who are waived are subject to the waiver wire, where any team that claims them picks up their current contract. Any player claimed off the waiver wire must added to the claiming team’s active 53-man roster. If they pass through waivers unclaimed, they become free agents and are free to sign with any team’s practice squad they choose, which includes their prior team. The current waiver wire priority is set by the original 2026 NFL Draft order, that is the list excluding trades. Waiver claims are filed by teams at the same time, with the team holding the highest claim in the process successfully picking up the player. Which NFL players face waivers, who becomes a free agent? As discussed above, players with less than four years of accrued NFL experience entering 2026 enter the waiver wire protocol if released. If they pass through the system unclaimed their current contract ends, at which point they become free agents and can pick their next destination (which includes their former/most recent team’s practice squad). Players who have four or more years of NFL service immediately become unrestricted free agents if released. Their contracts end on the day of their release, opening up the opportunity for them to sign anywhere they prefer. Primarily, the group of players being waived is comprised of those who are currently ineligible for unrestricted free-agency status entering the season. They would instead be an Exclusive Rights Free Agent (less than three years of service) or a Restricted Free Agent (three years of service). What is the current NFL waiver priority order? The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order. Once every team in the league has played four games, it resets to the current NFL standings. title: Bills HC Joe Brady says Maxwell Hairston is Buffalo’s starting CB
summary: All eyes were on Buffalo Bills second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston during the team’s preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Hairston started at cornerback Thursday night, and there’s been plenty of attention paid to his missed tackle in the open field early in action. To that end, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic shared that head coach […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Maxwell Hairston #31 of the Buffalo Bills walks off the field prior to a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images All eyes were on Buffalo Bills second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston during the team’s preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Hairston started at cornerback Thursday night, and there’s been plenty of attention paid to his missed tackle in the open field early in action. To that end, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic shared that head coach Joe Brady gave a very definitive and public vote of confidence in Hairston, stating to reporters that “(h)e’s our starting corner” when asked if there’s a competition at CB2. That competition query of of course refers to the presence of rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun. Bills HC Joe Brady on Maxwell Hairston and if there’s a competition for CB2: “He’s our starting corner” — Joe Buscaglia (@JoeBuscaglia) August 28, 2026 The question now for One Bills Drive is whether or not they write Hairston’s name in pencil or permanent marker. That’s something Hairston will have to influence in his second season, and likely hold off any incursion by Igbinosun. After putting a difficult rookie year behind him that saw his first season bookended by significant injuries, it appeared as though Hairston was setting up to take off in year two. Well, at least that seemed like the plan for as long as Sean McDermott was the head coach. The trouble for Hairston may have been that McDermott’s future at One Bills Drive perished the same night of Buffalo’s playoff loss to the Denver Broncos last January. Though that could appear short-sighted when considering that the main person responsible for selecting him in the first round was still in house — Brandon Beane — and received a promotion to include president of football operations within his executive title as general manager. Those injuries to his knee and ankle now behind him, it almost seems as though Hairston’s role on defense is more confusing than ever. The new regime saw fit to select Igbinosun early in the 2026 NFL Draft. Mind you, not as early as Hairston, but it was a significant addition considering the team’s defensive needs elsewhere. It was a decision met with quite a bit of confusion and controversy in the early going. One can only imagine what Hairston thought of the move. Hairston’s potential and athletic ability are both undeniable and off the charts . To think that only a select few were in on drafting him early is foolish. Any team would be happy to have Max Hairston, but it’s possible teams that prioritize man-cover cornerbacks wouldn’t place the same premium on rostering him. Hairston spent the bulk of his college career playing zone-based coverage, and he was an observably solid fit for that scheme under McDermott. When Brady was chosen as the new head coach, he decided to go in a new direction on defense, hiring Jim Leonhard who has brought along a 3-4 base system that prioritizes attacking offenses while asking boundary corners to play press man. At least we believe that to be the crux of the situation in 2026 and beyond. It’s possible that Leonhard has a plan for Hairston that defies any limitations exposed of him in man coverage. It’s also possible that Leonhard’s defense runs an exotic hybrid that allows Hairston to shine in zone looks. All we’ve seen of the new defense to this point is as bland as a flavorless snow cone. We won’t know what’s true until Week 1 kicks off against the Houston Texans. Even then, it’s possible the team pivots based on need. Brady sounds like a straight shooter as someone who’s fairly generous with his time and effort at the podium. As such, he should be taken at his word. At least for now.
