title: Buffalo Bills trending up/down after preseason win vs. Pittsburgh Steelers
summary: The Buffalo Bills’ preseason finale home win against the Pittsburgh Steelers didn’t come easy, with late-game heroics orchestrated by quarterback Shane Buechele to claim a one-point victory. Scores matter little in preseason, at least beyond those players who help put the points on the board, that is. For as much as anyone will say these […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Frank Gore Jr. #20 of the Buffalo Bills runs after the catch during the second quarter of a preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills’ preseason finale home win against the Pittsburgh Steelers didn’t come easy, with late-game heroics orchestrated by quarterback Shane Buechele to claim a one-point victory. Scores matter little in preseason, at least beyond those players who help put the points on the board, that is. For as much as anyone will say these are meaningless games, there’s never anything more at stake for plenty of NFL hopefuls who’ve put in a long spring and summer of work — and many of whom will continue doing so season after season for several years despite the same results. So let’s put to bed the notion that scores don’t really matter in the preseason. Winning and losing doesn’t have an impact on the season (apart from the infamy that was the Detroit Lions completely winless season in 2008), but scoring sure can play a huge role in any player’s ability to stick with a team. So too, can big-time performances, the likes of which have spawned countless summer crushes. But the dog days of summer are coming to an end, and there are a few notable players and situations to account for out of Thursday’s primetime win. Let’s take a less-than-conventional-at-times look at some of those moments. So who or what stood out, both good and bad, in preseason Week 3? Read on below… Horns Up: QB Kyle Allen It’s perhaps odd to include a player who didn’t perform in the preseason finale, especially considering that Shane Buechele played admirably over a full game on Thursday night. This has more to do with Allen not playing, and after head coach Joe Brady said the plan was for both he and Buechele to take snaps in the finale. So why the horns up? Allen played really well in two preseason games, going 24-of-28 for 236 yards and one touchdown with a 113.7 QB rating. During the second quarter of play, when president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane conducted an interview in the broadcast booth, he discussed Allen’s preseason body of work, claiming it to be among the finest he’d seen by a backup quarterback during his tenure with the Bills. That sounds like a lot of reassuring language toward Kyle Allen’s job status. Unfortunately, that may prove a difficult pill to swallow when talking about Shane Buechele’s future roster spot. Horns Down (unfairly): QB Shane Buechele This feels wrong, I understand. Shane Buechele went out and did a heck of a lot behind a makeshift offensive line filled with the deepest depth possible at One Bills Drive. In a game with so much roster gymnastics, Buechele played the role of fourth-quarter comeback artist. Why, then, give Buechele a horns down? It’s all about Brady’s decision to sit Kyle Allen. As mentioned above, that move and Beane’s comments on Allen seem to imply he did all possible to win the backup job. History has told us that players who take significant snaps in the final preseason game (and late in action) are often auditioning for other featured opportunities. It’s brutal, unfair, and perhaps unnecessary if NFL owners would simply approve an expanded roster count. Buechele finished the night going 26-of-38 for 196 yards with one of the best two-point passes in preseason history. Whatever comes of Buechele moving forward, and he at least deserves a featured spot on Buffalo’s practice squad, he should point proudly to his work against these Steelers. He even withstood a nasty-looking potential injury to his left forearm on an early sack. If there’s still a decision to be made about backup quarterback, it’s due to Buechele’s never-say-die effort and moxie late in action under the primetime lights. Horns Up: WR Skyler Bell No wide receiver saw more targets against the Steelers. In fact, the next closest person to Bell’s 10 targets was Gore with five targets. It’s clear that Brady (and perhaps Josh Allen the play caller) wanted to get Bell into rhythm and plenty of snaps heading into Week 1. Bell responded well, catching seven passes for 49 yards, and adding one rush for 28 yards. It had been a fairly quiet and disappointing training camp for Bell despite any extra opportunity borne out of injuries to the wide receivers room. While taking the reality of the preseason situation into account, things may have changed to the delight of Bell against the Steelers. Bell will have an uphill battle as a rookie fighting for snaps with the likes of DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, and Joshua Palmer. Rookie wide receivers often struggle to acclimate against NFL defenses, but this performance should go a long way toward benefiting Bell’s confidence early and often. Horns Down: Anyone fighting with Skyler Bell for a roster spot Apart from Bell who caught seven passes on 10 targets, the remainder of Buffalo’s wide receivers totaled six catches on 11 targets. It’s true that Max Tomczak (2) and Trent Sherfield (1) caught every target their way, but it’s eye-opening that Bell caught one more pass on one less total target than the rest of the team’s active wideouts Thursday night. There aren’t a lot of spots open at wide receiver, perhaps just one if we consider Bell a lock (he should be a lock). That leaves a lot of questions for a bunch of players who haven’t stood out that often this summer. Who makes Buffalo’s roster as WR6 could come down almost exclusively to their contributions elsewhere. Does that make it more or less likely that someone such as Mecole Hardman Jr. or Sherfield have an inside track over a rookie like Ja’Mori Maclin and Tomczak? What about Dante Pettis’ odds after a fantastic two-point conversion to claim the winning points? We’ll find out soon enough. Horns Up: RB Frank Gore Jr. Bloodlines matter, and if the worst anyone can say about Gore is that he looks like a dependable back, you take that every time. But Gore put on a clinic early in action against Pittsburgh. He finished the night with 10 rushes for 27 yards and one touchdown, adding an impressive five receptions (5 targets) for 45 additional yards. We don’t know yet what the plan is with third-down specialist Ty Johnson, but Gore has now proven capable as a receiver, similar in mold to Ray Davis. With the third quarter dying down, Gore tore off a long gain downfield, ending it by turning inside to welcome defenders instead of running toward safety and out of bounds. That goes a really long way in proving one’s worth to an NFL team. You can be certain everyone on that sideline and in the executive suite noticed that play. Gore is the type of player who just gets better with more snaps. Horns Down (unfairly): RB Ian Wheeler Ian Wheeler should be viewed as having done nothing to dissuade the Bills from rostering him in some capacity. He may be in a no-win situation simply because of Gore’s recent play. Wheeler is a tough SOB with the ball in his hands, and there’s a ton to love about the way he runs on any down. I could find way to adding both Gore and Wheeler to the 53-man roster if there was cause to roster one less defensive tackle and no fullback. Teams should want to hold onto the best football players, regardless of position. That doesn’t mean Wheeler (or Gore) should take priority over anyone as QB2, but there may be room to take on less conventional roster measures to keep Wheeler in town. If we see Gore as a lock for the practice squad as RB4, then it’s very likely there’s little to no room for Wheeler there unless Ty Johnson’s injury keeps him out in Week 1 and beyond. By all accounts on Thursday, Johnson appeared well on his way to being fully mended. Don’t be shocked if Wheeler and Gore are a part of the Bills’ plans this season. title: Buffalo Bills vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Week 3 preseason game recap
summary: Preseason Week 3 is a wrap, and the Buffalo Bills close out the exhibition slate with a 28-27 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium. Thanks for your love in the first article of this series, and glad to be back for another one. Here’s everything I wrote down as it happened. 1st Half […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Skyler Bell #13 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball in for a touchdown during the third quarter of a preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Preseason Week 3 is a wrap, and the Buffalo Bills close out the exhibition slate with a 28-27 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium. Thanks for your love in the first article of this series, and glad to be back for another one. Here’s everything I wrote down as it happened. 1st Half Skyler Bell moves fluidly and is a huge mismatch running routes inside. The way he moves reminds me of Stefon Diggs a lot. Shane Buechele isn’t close to Kyle Allen as a passer. And Allen isn’t great. Trent Sherfield is a lock to make this roster IMO. Joe Andreessen will make the team. They wouldn’t keep him out of this game if he wasn’t part of their roster. They’d give him a chance to put up more on tape for his NFL future elsewhere. Keonta Jenkins in trouble? Maybe PS bound again. Mitch Wishnowsky is gone. A 19-yard punt when battling for his life? Oof. Ray Davis messed up with his punt return case . Better now than in week 1, I guess? It might cost the Bills a roster spot, though. The punt returner job might not be settled. Mecole Hardman hasn’t been good, Khalil Shakir is simply a guy for safety there. Maybe Keon Coleman will get another shot? I’m not very excited about any of those options. A battle for the CB2 job in week 3 of preseason? Davison Igbinosun is giving Maxwell Hairston a run for his money. I won’t be surprised to see him alongside Christian Benford in week 1. T.J. Parker reminds me of Shaq Lawson right now . I know Shaq never became what we expected from him, but that’s not a bad comp for T.J. as he starts his career. He has the potential to become better and more complete. I wouldn’t keep Damar Hamlin or Geno Stone in my 53 , going with Jordan Hancock and Jalon Kilgore as my backup safeties. I think the Bills will carry one of them, though. Hamlin’s probably getting the nod with another INT. Phidarian Mathis looks good , too bad he’s on PEDs. Kani Walker is an awesome find. Undrafted? This guy looks better than Levi Wallace, who was also undrafted, and Dane Jackson, who was a 7th-round pick. He’s young Benford-like, but Benford was a 6th round pick. Awesome find. Andre Jones Jr. giving Max Iheanachor, a 1st round pick, some trouble is a good look for somebody who’s fighting for a PS place. Rough half for the OL. 2nd Half Nice to see Bell being moved around and getting open no matter where he lined up. It’s against backups at this point or even people who won’t make the team, but we’re talking about a 4th round pick, it’s not like he’s supposed to be a stud out of the gate. His versatility will give him opportunities. I’ve heard all the talk about the new stadium , but I’ll tell you one thing: it looks gorgeous on TV, especially as the night comes. It’s just preseason , and with a lot of backups and camp bodies on the field at this point, but I’m really excited for the new defensive schemes. Jim Leonhard’s defense should be fun. Bad bad look for the Special Teams allowing that punt return for a TD. No discipline, poor angles, and even worse tackling. Teaching tape on what not to do for the guys in the final 53. That Pittsburgh PR, though. Dude is a real weapon. (Kaden Wetjen, 4th round pick). One of the best punt returners coming out of college recently (Two-time Jet Award winner, 2024-25). It’s extremely frustrating how Buechele doesn’t risk anything downfield , like, ever. Give his WRs a chance to make some plays. It’s always a check-down or scrambling. (He just gave Max Tomczak a shot as I was typing this, and guess what? It worked). I wish Ja’Mori Maclin had more chances , but, as said above, Buechele. Last drive and Buechele starts to let it fly. Gave Dante Pettis two chances and good things happened — a 1st down completion on 3rd and 14, and a long PI call setting the Bills up inside the 10. Pettis is an NFL receiver. He ate his competition alive late in the game, including on the game-winning 2-point conversion. Can he become the punt returner and make the team? I’d rather have him than Hardman, but I don’t think any of them make the team. 1 min left, 1-point game. The type of situation Sean McDermott’s D failed miserably , again and again. Not Leonhard’s though. 4 and out, game over. What’s that? Is it real life? Love to see it. Catch up on all this and more with the latest edition of Leading the Charge!

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Pittsburgh Steelers NFL Preseason Week 3 fan discussion
summary: The Buffalo Bills close out their 2026 NFL preseason schedule with a home tilt against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Head coach Joe Brady has said some starters will play this evening, but that quarterback Josh Allen will not be among that group. Despite anyone’s insistence that Allen and the offense need as many reps as reasonably […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Buffalo Bills cornerback Maxwell Hairston (31) warms up before the game between the Cleveland Browns and the Bills at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Buffalo Bills close out their 2026 NFL preseason schedule with a home tilt against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Head coach Joe Brady has said some starters will play this evening, but that quarterback Josh Allen will not be among that group. Despite anyone’s insistence that Allen and the offense need as many reps as reasonably possible, the best news is that Allen won’t be put in harm’s way on the field this evening. Instead, look for quarterback Shane Buechele taking all the offensive snaps tonight. Despite a game that’s meaningless in the box score, it’s a very important game for a lot of guys on the field of play. Who plays when and for how long tends to go a long way towards their path to a roster spot. At least that was true in prior seasons under former head coach Sean McDermott. All of Bills Mafia wants tonight’s game to come and go as quickly as possible, and with little necessary drama attached. That said, there are a lot of intriguing story lines to watch for, perhaps none bigger in this game than that of second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston. With a defensive scheme change, are Hairston’s days as a starter numbered, or can he succeed as needed in man-cover looks and hold back rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun? Tonight could tell us a lot about Hairston’s immediate future whether he doesn’t play, or plays and plays a lot of snaps. There’s a battle at running back behind James Cook III, Ty Johnson, and Ray Davis. Obviously each of that trio has a lock on starting snaps, however a pair of young running backs in Frank Gore Jr. and Ian Wheeler will do their best to earn significant consideration for the regular season and beyond. Is this Gore’s year despite the noise that Wheeler’s tracks have made? The top of the wide receiver depth chart seems fairly settled, but there are a lot of options to consider behind starting wideouts DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, and Joshua Palmer. Keep your eyes on rookies Skyler Bell, Ja’Mori Maclin, and Max Tomczak, plus veteran receivers Mecole Hardman Jr., Trent Sherfield, Stephen Gosnell, Dante Pettis, and Quentin Skinner — especially when and where each player takes snaps against the Steelers. On defense, focus on how defensive tackle Greg Gaines is deployed, and what his contributions bring to Buffalo’s trenches. Plus, is the battle at linebacker settled? Will the Bills march on with Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams as the team’s starting inside ‘backers, or will Kaleb Elarms-Orr, Joe Andreessen, Keonta Jenkins, Jimmy Ciarlo, Theron Gaines, or even Otis Reese IV give new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard pause before naming starters inside? There are a lot of guys battling for a spot at outside linebacker/edge rusher behind Greg Rousseau, Bradley Chubb, and Michael Hoecht. Will rookie EDGE players in TJ Parker and Cade Denhoff make a move up the chart this evening, or will it be Javon Solomon? What about veteran defenders like Mike Danna and Andre Jones Jr.? With that, here’s your open thread for all of tonight’s action during Bills vs. Steelers. Remember, we only have one game thread for each matchup this season so you can sit tight in this space all game long. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

RobHolland211: Hi Brian. […]
full_text: CANTON, OH - AUGUST 06: Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Reggie Virgil (82) is tackled by Carolina Panthers cornerback Corey Thornton (31) during the second quarter of the National Football League preseason game between the Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals on August 6, 2026, at the Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We have one final week of preseason to get through before its on to the final roster cut down, practice squad signings, and then game week! Let’s dive in to your final round of preseason questions! RobHolland211: Hi Brian. Based solely on what we’ve seen this preseason, do you think we win the division again this year or do you think one (or two) of our NFC South foes have a chance of overtaking us? I have a hard time basing much on the preseason. I think the Falcons are going to be dead in the water unless Michael Penix really bounces back. I do think the Buccaneers could win the NFC South, while I think the Saints will once again be competitive. But this division is still as unpredictable as ever to me. GooseCreek: Brian, you are among a group of football enthusiasts gathered to discuss NFL rules you would like to add or change. After these discussions, a list of proposals will be sent to Troy Vincent, NFL Exec. V.P. of Football Operations for evaluation and referral to Commissioner Goodell. What changes or additions are you advocating? ] I would push for an additional bye week and add more final roster spots and active GameDay roster spots. I think both of these will help increase the longevity of the rosters over the course of the ever expanding NFL season and subsequent increased travel with international games. Plus, it gives more young talents time and paychecks to develop in the NFL. Those are the only ones I am really all that passionate about, there were some really good answers to this question so share all your thoughts down below, CSR faithful. @WTMealey: We might know the answer before the other article drops but anywho How many players not currently on the roster will we claim on waivers and make the initial 53? How many of our current players that we cut will end up on some other teams initial 53? The Panthers do tend to churn the 53 man roster cuts, so I’ll go with 2 players they might add. I think maybe 2 for the Panthers to make other 53 man rosters. I don’t expect Xavier Legette to be waived so he’s not on my list. This Panthers squad is a bit deeper than seasons past. Randallpink11: Is Corey Thorton making the 53? I have seen several reports suggesting he does not. What does the mighty Brain have to say about it? I don’t have a whole lot of doubt that he does make the roster. He made it last season and played some valuable snaps as part of the regular season defense before injuries. I have 4 guys ahead of him on the depth chart (Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Chau Smith-Wade, Will Lee III). I would expect at least 5 CBs to make the roster and an additional 1 or 2 making the practice squad. Revshawn: What would be the equivalent of natural disaster it would be if Haynes King is cut on the final cut day and he’s claimed by the Atlanta Falcons? I appreciate a good bit, but its not outside of the realm of possibility the Panthers let King hit waivers and try to add him back to the practice squad. I think its more likely he sticks and Kyle Trask gets released, but I’m not staking my name to that claim just yet. But if waiving King happens, it will suck a little bit. Good_Ol_Boy: Have you been impressed by our incoming rookie class in the preseason? Do you think any of them will be cut outright and not be put on the PS? I don’t see much reason for the Panthers to waive any of their rookie draft class. I’d consider Will Lee III, Sam Hecht, and Zakee Wheatley pretty safe at this point. They may waive Jackson Kuwatch but I’d expect him to go back to the practice squad. If you’re talking UDFAs, I’m not getting into that one. SmoothC: What order so you see the NFC south finishing? I see the Bucs, Panthers, Saints, and Falcons as the order, with the top of the division once again super close in record. I could even see the Panthers slipping to 3rd or 4th by only a game or twos difference and tiebreakers. Still a real hard division to predict right now. schrodingersblackcat: What’s your favorite Dolly Parton song (or other artistic contribution)? What’s your favorite Tim Curry role? Jolene and I Will Always Love You will always be classics for me. They may be easy answers but its just not difficult to me. As a side note, check out Dollywood if you never got the chance to. For me, Tim Curry’s version of It will always be my favorite. Just a classic film in the horror genre. SnarkyComet: How do you think our RB group will look on Week 1 vs the Bears? Like what percentage do you see the usage of each RB? With Hubbard coming off injury I’m anxious to see how/who we roll out there for the run game. I know no one is 100% safe that’s not named Hubbard or Brooks so you can say 3rd RB if it helps. Or do you have a strong idea of who that third RB is? I’m not overly concerned with Chuba Hubbard, it very much seems like Carolina is playing it safe with a soft tendon issue, and they really don’t need to trot Chuba out there during the preseason when he’s nursing an injury. I think Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks will split a healthy number of carries, but if Chuba is still hampered I don’t see any reason they won’t use Trevor Etienne. I’m way more worried about other positions than running back right now. JakeNCVA: I’m all out of questions; other than ones that will have to wait until the regular season gets underway to get answers. Great final comment to end the preseason mailbag, I’m exhausted with trying to project this and am just excited to see the real thing. That’s all for this week, Panthers fans. Enjoy the preseason game!

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 16 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - JANUARY 07: Jonathan Stewart #28 of the Carolina Panthers runs the ball against the New Orleans Saints during the first half of the NFC Wild Card playoff game at the Mercedes-Benz Superdome on January 7, 2018 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Layne Murdoch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #16. Jonathan Stewart If there’s one position group that’s always been a strength of the Carolina Panthers, it’s running back. That’s in large part due to the fact that the franchise has historically over-invested in the position, but at least they’ve gotten strong returns for those investments. A quintessential example of that is Jonathan Stewart, who comes in as the highest ranked running back on our list. The Panthers used a first round pick (13th overall) on Stewart despite having used a first round pick on current starter DeAngelo Williams just two years prior. While the allocation of resources was definitely not the most efficient, it did create one of if not the most memorable player duo in the team’s history. He and Williams combined to form Double Trouble. Stewart racked up 836 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie despite splitting time with Williams. In Stewart’s second season, Williams missed a couple games due to injury, and that allowed both to top 1,100 rushing yards for the season. It remains the only time that’s been done in the history of the NFL, and I’d venture to guess that record is pretty safe for the foreseeable future. Stewart would continue to split carries with Williams until the latter was let go by Dave Gettleman in one of many high-animosity moves. That finally gave Stewart the backfield mostly to himself for the first time in his career, and he responded with two seasons in which he would have been well on pace to top 1,000 yards had he not missed a couple games each season due to injury. The Panthers continued their trend of over-investing in the position by drafting McCaffrey in the first round of the 2017 draft after those two seasons from Stewart. Stewart served as the veteran battering ram while the shifty McCaffrey got up to speed with the NFL. Stewart was let go after the 2018 season due to his diminishing play and role along with some cap relief. He went on to sign for the Giants, but he only carried the ball six times before a foot injury ended his season and ultimately his career. Jonathan Stewart has maintained a central figure around the Panthers since his retirement. He’s often involved in promotional material from the team and is all over the place on social media and in local events talking about the team. While he didn’t have some of the peaks that DeAngelo Williams and Christian McCaffrey had, his longevity and tight bond with the organization earn him the highest ranking among running backs and the number 16 spot on the top 100 Panthers of all time.

title: Is it fair at this point to question Kyler Gordon?
summary: Over the years as a sports fan, I have certainly questioned a player or two about their desire to get back on the football field. But over the years I’ve learned that’s not a good idea. I will admit, I originally questioned Jay Cutler in the moment during the NFC Championship game when we had […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 18: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL divisional playoff game against the Los Angeles Rams at Soldier Field on January 18, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the years as a sports fan, I have certainly questioned a player or two about their desire to get back on the football field. But over the years I’ve learned that’s not a good idea. I will admit, I originally questioned Jay Cutler in the moment during the NFC Championship game when we had the Caleb Haine experience. In hindsight, that was stupid. It took me a long time to question Nate Davis. Let’s not forget, the summer Nate Davis arrived in Chicago, his mother died. It’s impossible to know how that’s going to affect someone’s professional life, and to this day, we still really don’t know how that impacted him. Kyler Gordon is entering his fifth season in Chicago. And while he’s never played a full season, before last year, he never missed more than 4 games in a season. Last year, Gordon missed 14. This year, Gordon basically hasn’t been on the field at all. If the Bears were coming out and talking about Gordon’s injury and how his rehab is going and a projected timeline, we would be classifying this as an unfortunate injury, but that’s not what the Bears are saying. Both Ben Johnson and Ryan Poles have been pretty flippant talking about Gordon during the spring and summer and certainly seemed agitated about his lack of progress and lack of participation. They also seem to be missing details about what his status is. The Bears have plenty of injured players. You don’t hear Johnson or Poles talking about any other injured players like that. We just heard Ben Johnson say that “ALMOST every player” that is injured is trying hard to get back on the field. That certainly seems like a shot at Gordon. At this point, with the Bears clearly frustrated, is it time to question Gordon’s motivation to get back on the field? Like I said at the top, questioning an injury with a player is almost always bad business. I think 19 times out of 20 (maybe more), you find out that you didn’t have all the information and the player was more hurt than anyone realized (sometimes coaching staffs included). But let’s go back to Nate Davis. And now, I am not saying Gordon is Davis. But Davis clearly didn’t want to play football. Davis got through his rookie contract, signed a contract that earned him $20 million guaranteed with the Bears, and at that point, decided to do the bare minimum to fulfil his contract so he could collect his money. At this point, we know Davis was released in November of 2024, and he hasn’t even sniffed a tryout with another team. Davis is a good enough player that teams would absolutely bring him in for a tryout if he was interested. He clearly is not. Is that Gordon’s situation? I have a hard time believing that. Gordon has played hard in plenty of football games and has never come across that way. But Gordon was paid in August of 2025, and since then, not only has he barely played, he’s barely practiced. Ryan Poles is frustrated. Ben Johnson is frustrated. Chicago Bears fans are frustrated. Is it fair to question Gordon’s motivations and wonder if he’s lost his drive to play now that he has a contract that guarantees him $31 million? We’ve seen more and more players retire at younger ages once they get the guaranteed money from their second contract. Heck, Drew Dalman only got through one of his two guaranteed years before he decided to hang it up. Has Kyler Gordon quietly quit? I certainly hope not, and I’m not there yet, but I have to admit, the thought is now creeping into my mind. I don’t like that it has, but it’s almost impossible at this point not to start thinking it’s a possibility. For now, we wait. We see if Gordon gets on the field in the regular season, and we see how hard he’s playing and how effective he is. If this dance continues throughout the season, every Bears fan is going to have the same thought. If Gordon gets on the field and plays 12 or 13 games and looks good in the process, we are all going to put this behind us. To me, I’m starting to wonder if this is similar to the Derrick Rose situation with the Bulls. Rose, post injury, was very honest about how he approached injuries and how he wasn’t willing to punish his body if it meant the possibility that his body breaks down in the future when he’s in his 50s and 60s. That frustrated Bulls fans, but when Rose was on the court, he was 100% committed to being on the court. It was how he approached his recovery that was frustrating. Is Gordon the same? Only time will tell, but as for now, I’m just wondering if it’s time to question Kyler Gordon?

title: Chicago Bears Question of the Day: Which Historical Roster Cut Stung the Most?
summary: Chicago Bears fans are some of the most loyal fans you will ever find. We love our players, and that includes backups, undrafted free agents, practice squad players, and even former players (we miss you, DJ!) But one thing I have noticed about emotions is that the highs are matched by the lows. No better […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - AUGUST 26: Trevis Gipson #99 of the Chicago Bears celebrates with Terrell Lewis #52 after forcing a fumble against the Buffalo Bills during the first half of a preseason game at Soldier Field on August 26, 2023 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears fans are some of the most loyal fans you will ever find. We love our players, and that includes backups, undrafted free agents, practice squad players, and even former players (we miss you, DJ!) But one thing I have noticed about emotions is that the highs are matched by the lows. No better reminder of that than roster cuts. Right?! With teams required to make cuts to get down to 53-man rosters this Sunday at 5:00 pm CST, it got me thinking about which players I hope make the cut. Then my mind went to which cut stands out above the rest over the years, which is my question to you all! Since you have been a fan of the Bears, which roster cut was the hardest one to witness? A few camp legends come to mind. Devin Aromashadu, who eventually made the team at WR, as did another camp hero, Dane Sanzenbacher, but others like OLB James Vaughters were not so lucky. Terrell Lewis is another whom I thought earned his roster spot, only to get released at cutdown day, with Trevis Gipson soon to follow. Tanner Gentry, Daniel Braverman, MyCole Pruitt, Armanti Edwards, Tom Zbikowski, Harvey Unga, Josh Beekman, Brandon Rideau, and even our own Ryan Poles were also notable cuts at the end of camp. But the hardest one for me to stomach was Terrell Lewis in 2023. We entered that year with a glaring hole at edge rusher despite signing free-agent Yannick Ngakoue that offseason to a 1-year, $10.5 million deal and eventually trading a future 2nd-round pick for Montez Sweat. But why cut Lewis? He was on fire that pre-season and led the league in sacks and forced fumbles. He would go on to practice for the Eagles but not play another down professionally, so clearly Chicago wasn’t the only one to deem him unworthy of a roster spot, but man – he was looking good for us all camp. What about you? Who comes to mind as far as one of the most difficult roster cuts of all time?

title: Final Chicago Bears 53-man roster prediction
summary: The Bears’ initial 53-man roster will be announced in just a few days, and trying to project this one is rather difficult. Most of the main positions are mostly settled, but there are several players dealing with injuries, so trying to figure out how the Bears plan to maneuver those players so they can get […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: The Chicago Bears offense huddles during the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Bears’ initial 53-man roster will be announced in just a few days, and trying to project this one is rather difficult. Most of the main positions are mostly settled, but there are several players dealing with injuries, so trying to figure out how the Bears plan to maneuver those players so they can get everyone to their designated injury list is a bit more challenging. Here’s my best guess as to how the 53-man roster looks on Sunday (* are explained in the comments for each group) Quarterback (3): Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum Why burn words on the most straightforward group at any position on the team? Running Back (4): D’Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, Salvon Ahmed, Roschon Johnson I think most projections here will be three running backs. I’m going to go with four thanks to Ozzy Trapilo (more on that later). I think Ahmed makes the team as the third running back and Roschon finishes out his contract playing largely on special teams. Wide Receiver (6): Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, Kalif Raymond, Jahdae Walker, Zavion Thomas, Kaden Davis Based on how the Bears have signed multiple veteran wide receivers, I get the idea they want to keep 6 on the roster. I think the top 5 are pretty straightforward, and I think with a strong camp, Kaden Davis makes the roster this year and the Bears see if Davis has finally found a home after being quite the nomad to start his career. Tight End (3): Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, Sam Roush This one is about as straightforward as the QB room. Offensive Line (9): Braxton Jones, Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, Jonah Jackson, Darnell Wright, Logan Jones, Luke Newman, Jordan McFadden, Theo Benedet Alright, so with this one, you’ll see that Ozzy Trapilo is missing. The Bears are allowed to move two players directly to IR without playing the “put them on the original 53, and then move them to IR the next day and bring back someone you just cut” game. I say they do that with Trapilo. I think based on the struggles of Amegadjie and Wills, it’s just time to let them go and use Benedet as the swing tackle until Trapilo can return. When Trapilo gets back, if the offense is fully healthy, that’s when I would look at Roschon Johnson potentially getting released, but odds are, there will be more injuries to the team because, well, it’s the NFL. Special Teams (3): Cairo Santos, Tory Taylor, Beau Gardner With Luke Elkin gone, this room is already set. Defensive Ends (6/5): Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Daniel Hardy, Marcus Davenport, Jamree Kromah, Shemar Turner* The defense is certainly trickier than the offense, but let’s take a shot. With this group, I think Turner is moved to the injured list but not with one of those two initial spots, which means he’s going to have to be placed on the 53 and moved the next day. I think the Bears initially keep 6 here with the idea that it’s actually a 5-person room. Sweat and Austin, of course, are here. Hardy is a great special teamer and has been getting rotations with the 1s. Kromah has flashed enough that I think they give him a shot, and I can’t see the Bears bringing in Davenport just to let him go before the season starts. Defensive Tackles (5): Grady Jarrett, Gervon Dexter, Dayo Odeyingbo, Neville Gallimore, Jordan van den Berg For this exercise, we’ve moved Odeyingbo inside. The Bears really seem to want to try him as an interior pass rusher, so we will call him that for this purpose. I don’t know if Dexter is on the block or if the agent is just trying to drum up interest to try and get his client a bigger payday, but I think he’s here still on Sunday. Gallimore, of course, makes it, as does van den Berg. It does mean there is no room for Kentavius Street. Linebackers (5): Devin Bush, TJ Edwards, D’Marco Jackson, Keyshaun Elliott, Ruben Hyppolite I think this room is pretty straightforward. Noah Sewell is in the final year of his contract and hasn’t been on the field, and I just don’t see a spot for Jack Sanborn. Hyppolite could be gone, but I doubt the Bears go another direction after just one season. I think he gets another year to show improvement. The other four aren’t going anywhere. Cornerbacks (5/6): Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad, Josh Blackwell, Jaylon Jones, Dontae Manning* Here we see Kyler Gordon missing because I think he, like Trapilo, gets moved immediately to IR when the initial 53 comes out. I think Manning is initially released but is brought back as the 6th CB once they can move Turner over to the injured list. I think Terell Smith misses making the team this year after countless years struggling to stay healthy. Safeties (4): Dillon Thieneman, Cam Lewis, Xavier Woods, Elijah Hicks*, Skyler Thomas* No Coby Bryant here, and a banged-up Elijah Hicks makes this an interesting group. I think the Bears initially keep Hicks on the 53 and release Thomas, but swap them 24 hours later, with Hicks moving to the injured list and Thomas coming back onto the 53. IR/PUP (4): Kyler Gordon, Ozzy Trapilo, Shemar Turner* , Elijah Hicks* With this group, as I’ve mentioned in previous paragraphs, Gordon and Trapilo immediately move to IR, and Turner and Hicks get transferred to the injured list after initial cuts.

title: A Chippy Joint Practice Between the Chicago Bears and Tennessee Titans
summary: The Chicago Bears held their second joint practice of training camp, closing out the camp season, with the Tennessee Titans Thursday at Vanderbilt Health Football Center, a roughly two-hour, padded session against Robert Saleh’s Titans two days before Saturday’s preseason finale at Nissan Stadium (5 p.m. CT).  It was hot, physical, and chippy. From the […]
full_text: LAKE FOREST, ILLINOIS - JULY 29: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears looks on during Chicago Bears Training Camp at Halas Hall on July 29, 2026 in Lake Forest, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears held their second joint practice of training camp, closing out the camp season, with the Tennessee Titans Thursday at Vanderbilt Health Football Center, a roughly two-hour, padded session against Robert Saleh’s Titans two days before Saturday’s preseason finale at Nissan Stadium (5 p.m. CT). It was hot, physical, and chippy. From the Bears’ side, the day split cleanly: the offense — especially Caleb Williams and the tight ends — won the first half; Tennessee’s defense and first-round receiver Carnell Tate won the second after Chicago lost both starting corners for stretches. Ben Johnson framed the week as “another controlled test” against an “attacking front” designed to meet the Bears at the line of scrimmage — a different problem than Joe Burrow and the Bengals. This is the last chance for the Bears to evaluate position battles and get both the offense and defense ready for a season that will kick off in less than two weeks, when the Bears will face their first test against the Carolina Panthers. On a very hot day in Nashville, Caleb Williams got off to a hot start, according to CHGO’s Adam Hoge , noting that Caleb had six straight completions and was 9 of 11 overall for that period. Hoge also reported that Caleb spread the ball around to eight different receivers. Caleb Williams on 🔥 to start practice vs Titans. Six straight completions and 9 of 11 overall. The incompletions were a throwaway and a drop. Ball being spread around. Eight different receivers have caught a pass from Caleb. — Adam Hoge (@AdamHoge) August 27, 2026 Ben Arthur (FOX, covering the Titans) described the tape: Williams hit Rome Odunze in stride off an RPO, stepped up and found Cole Kmet on a shuffle pass, and ripped a dart into a tight window outside the numbers. Red-zone work was even better for Chicago. The Tennessean’s live blog had the Bears scoring six touchdowns in 12 combined red-zone snaps across first, second, and third units. Caleb threw two red-zone scores in one period, including an out to rookie WR Zavion Thomas and a play-action shot to a wide-open Kmet. D’Andre Swift scored in the red zone and was part of a trick play: handoff, pitch back to Williams, downfield to Kmet. Johnson had said before practice that Swift looked as good as he has at this point of any year — vision, bounce, cut-up timing. That showed up today in the practice with the Titans. The tight-end room was the most consistent Bears’ weapon of the day. Colston Loveland drew praise from Titans reporters on the other sideline (“looks legit”; “big, tall, fast, and very good”). He had a highlight after a Swift-to-Williams lateral and a YAC spin for a chunk gain. Rookie Sam Roush, working later units with Case Keenum, caught a deep ball and an end-zone score for “big plays,” according to Nick Moreano of REKAP, in the 11-on-11 period, and agreed that Johnson’s pre-practice line on Roush still applied after the session: flashes that get a staff excited, consistency not there yet, which is expected for a rookie tight end. Tight ends had themselves a day 🔥 pic.twitter.com/QRjMTzurzz — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) August 27, 2026 In the second half of the practice, the Bears were taught to remember the Titans (you come here for the news and coverage, you stay for the Dad jokes). Adam Hoge noted the “good response” by the Titans defense during a long team period in which they were better in coverage and got more pressure on Caleb. Also said that the Titans did not like Tyson Bagent going to make a tackle on an interception. Williams finished a two-minute drive around the 20 with 12 seconds left and threw an interception to Tony Adams intended for Loveland. Titans 1s also sacked him and forced incompletions in the period after the break. Good response by the Titans defense in a long 28-play team period. Tightened up coverage and got a lot more pressure, making things more difficult for Caleb. Would say the Titans definitely won that period. Things got chippy too, especially after Tyson Bagent went to make a… — Adam Hoge (@AdamHoge) August 27, 2026 Chicago arrived today in Nashville short on the defensive line. Dan Wiederer of the Athletic reported that Gervon Dexter (hamstring or trade negotiations – hard to say which) and Austin Booker (groin) did not travel. Then both starting corners left early. Jaylon Johnson hurt his right arm on a run play in 11-on-11, lost his helmet and pads, stayed on the sideline next to DBs coach Al Harris, and kept chirping. Tyrique Stevenson favored his right leg after a collision with Tate / a red-zone breakup, left with trainer Andre Tucker, then returned with the starters. While Johnson took off his pads and did not return to the field, he stayed on the sidelines. Cam Lewis gave the defense its best moment: an interception of Cam Ward on a throw behind TE Gunnar Helm. Malik Muhammad broke up one would-be Tate touchdown. Otherwise, with Johnson out and Stevenson in and out, Tate feasted. Luther Burden III traveled and did individual work only while still easing back from a groin injury; he stayed vocal on the sideline. A hit on Titans WR Wan’Dale Robinson, later identified as having been delivered by Xavier Woods, was called “cheap” by Saleh in the post-practice interview . It cleared both benches and sent Robinson off for a concussion evaluation. There seemed to be a consensus among both Bears and Titans beat reporters that the Bears had the advantage early in practice but that the Titans got the best of the Bears in the later period. Jim Wyatt , senior writer for the Tennessee Titans, thought that the Titans “held their own” against a “good football team” in the Chicago Bears at practice today. He also thought that former Chicago Bear, now Titans backup, Mitch Trubisky had a solid day with a 19-26 performance. AtoZ’s Kole Noble said it most directly from the Chicago beat: the Titans “seemingly won the day,” with plenty of Bears positives still on the field. Chris Kwiecinski and Devan Kaney of FOX 32 sounded the most Bears-optimistic voice among the reporters covering the practice, writing that Williams was the catalyst and that “the Bears’ offense was winning the day over the Titans” – but that assessment was before the practice break. All in all, while the Titans seemed to get the best of the Bears in the second half of the practice, both teams seem to have come away with positives, despite the jawing and occasional fisticuffs, and despite the scare with the injuries to Johnson and Stephenson, and the hit on Robinson, both teams seem to have come away relatively healthy. Some other news of note, nuggets, if you will: Patrick Finley of the Sun-Times remarked that Zavion Thomas was ready to fight any and every Titan on the field: Zavion Thomas just tried to fight half the Titans defense, — Patrick Finley (@patrickfinley) August 27, 2026 In the same vein, Brad Biggs of the Tribune observed that the Bears were very vocal with the Titans throughout practice today: Some players came together after last series for starters in team drills. Luther Burden, who is not doing team drills, got into some jawing with Jeffery Simmons and Jermaine Johnson. Size advantage: Titans. — Brad Biggs (@BradBiggs) August 27, 2026 Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that Sean McDermott, the former Buffalo Bills head coach, was at practice and consulting with Ben Johnson: Former Bills HC Sean McDermott is at today’s Titans-Bears joint practice and is spending time with Chicago HC Ben Johnson. pic.twitter.com/7VE2vmnOJA — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 27, 2026 And a few videos from the day. Caleb being Caleb with a busted pocket pic.twitter.com/62CfUPySRt — Ball Noir (@EnEfEl_Football) August 27, 2026 Loveland makin plays @creamsleeve…

full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Austin Booker #94 of the Chicago Bears lines up before the snap during an NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson met the media earlier today before their joint practice with the Tennessee Titans, and he provided a few injury updates. Defensive end Austin Booker has missed the last few days, and per Johnson, he’s dealing with a groin issue and is week-to-week. Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr., who was mentioned in a trade rumor a couple of days ago, tweaked his hamstring that same day and did not travel to Nashville. Right tackle Darnell Wright, who was back at practice yesterday after leaving on Tuesday, re-aggravated his elbow injury that he suffered last year, but it’s not expected to sideline him. Johnson said he’d practice today. Defensive end Marcus Davenport, who was signed 10 days ago, hasn’t practiced because he’s been doing training and conditioning work as they ramp him up. Johnson also asked about players returning from injury, and if you read between the lines, you may have a similar thought that many fans do… “We have almost the entire roster fighting their tails off to get back out on the field. They do not like missing time. …. They want to be out there with their teammates, and to me, that’s the sign that we’re moving in the right direction.” We’ll have more from the joint practice later this afternoon.

title: Bengals 53-man roster projection ahead of preseason finale vs. Eagles
summary: The final preseason gameday is here for the Cincinnati Bengals, who will take on the Philadelphia Eagles tonight at Lincoln Financial Field, where many players are getting their final chance to prove they belong on a 53-man roster. With that in mind, here is our latest Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster projection! Quarterback: Joe Burrow, Joe […]
full_text: The final preseason gameday is here for the Cincinnati Bengals, who will take on the Philadelphia Eagles tonight at Lincoln Financial Field, where many players are getting their final chance to prove they belong on a 53-man roster. With that in mind, here is our latest Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster projection! Quarterback: Joe Burrow, Joe Flacco (2) Completely straightforward with the two players who will make the Bengals’ initial 53-man roster here. The only question is whether the Bengals will keep both Josh Johnson and Sean Clifford on the 16-player practice squad. If not, which one do they end up keeping there? Running Back: Chase Brown, Samaje Perine, Tahj Brooks (3) The biggest question of this trio is Tahj Brooks. While he hasn’t really stood out running the football through two games, his blocking and receiving skills look to be improved. For now, Brooks makes the initial 53-man roster, but this could be a spot where the Bengals make a waiver claim. Tahj Brooks is penciled in as the third running back on the roster for now. While we would all like to see more explosive runs from him, I do think other areas of his game are coming along. Do you think he sticks on the 53-man roster, or will the Bengals potentially make a waiver… pic.twitter.com/pSXtD8bcaA — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 26, 2026 Wide Receiver: Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Andrei Iosivas, Colbie Young, Dohnte Meyers, Mitch Tinsley (6) The biggest question mark is the last spot at the position. They could decide to keep Charlie Jones as the primary returner. They could opt for Ke’Shawn Williams in that spot, and potentially float Jones out as a trade candidate for a late-round pick swap. Or they could go with Tinsley as I did here. I don’t think he has had a major standout performance like last preseason, but Burrow knows he has made plays for him in the past, and that could ultimately help him claim the final spot. In this scenario, Meyers is the primary returner. Tight End: Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All Jr., Tanner Hudson, Jack Endries (5) The Bengals kept five tight ends last year, and I think they will do the same again this year. If it comes down to keeping just four, both Hudson and Endries have made cases for earning that final spot. They could opt for the proven veteran or the young rookie with upside. Ultimately, I think they keep both. Offensive Line: Orlando Brown Jr., Dylan Fairchild, Ted Karras, Dalton Risner, Amarius Mims, Brian Parker II, Connor Lew, Jalen Rivers, Javon Foster (9) The uncertainty at the swing tackle position could force them to keep both Rivers and Foster for now. If that happens, Jacob Bayer is the biggest snub for making the 53-man roster. He has been really impressive during the preseason. He can play both guard and center for the Bengals, and would be a prime candidate to sign back to the practice squad if he goes unclaimed on waivers. Defensive Line: Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, Dexter Lawrence, Myles Murphy, Cashius Howell, BJ Hill, Shemar Stewart, TJ Slaton, Kris Jenkins, Cedric Johnson, Landon Robinson (11) Unless there is a Kris Jenkins trade, the Bengals will go heavy with 11 defensive linemen. Landon Robinson has earned his spot on the roster and should be active on game days. My biggest question is whether they decide to put Shemar Stewart on IR to start the season. If that happens, it would open the door for Isaiah Foskey to make the 53-man roster. Landon Robinson with another standout performance on Saturday night. pic.twitter.com/4bOMXTp9RU — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 23, 2026 Linebacker: Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., Swayze Bozeman, Oren Burks (4) Going heavy at tight end and defensive line would mean another position would have to go light. The position could end up being at linebacker. I have Joe Giles-Harris just missing the 53-man roster in this projection. If they keep five linebackers, he is on it. They could also start him on the practice squad and call him up early in the season. He has been an integral member of our special teams units. There are other good practice squad candidates at the position, including Liam Anderson and Jack Dingle. Cornerback: DJ Turner, Dax Hill, Jalen Davis, Tacario Davis, DJ Ivey, Ja’Sir Taylor (6) I could make an argument for Bralyn Lux or Josh Newton to nab the final cornerback spot, but the Bengals feel strongly about Taylor as the backup slot corner behind Jalen Davis. Taylor played solid during preseason game two, and likely solidified his spot on the Bengals’ 53-man roster. Safety: Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle, Kyle Dugger, PJ Jules (4) While Jules has had some struggles with coverage, he is making this 53-man roster for his special-teams ability. He will likely be the leader of that unit this season, and the Bengals had him serve as a captain during the game against the Bears. Russ Yeast will likely start the season on the practice squad behind these four players. PJ Jules has had some struggles in coverage, but what he provides on special teams is why he should be on this roster. pic.twitter.com/kSqFypt3Op — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 23, 2026 Specialists: P Ryan Rehkow, K Evan McPherson, LS William Wagner (3) No decisions to be made here. These spots are locked up for the foreseeable future.

summary: Tonight marks the Cincinnati Bengals’ final preseason game, as they’re set to take on the Eagles in Philly. We already know the starters won’t play, but plenty of young guys and roster-bubble players will be putting their blood, sweat, and tears into this game. Many of the guys who will play in this game for […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Landon Robinson (96) walks off the field at the end of the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tonight marks the Cincinnati Bengals’ final preseason game, as they’re set to take on the Eagles in Philly. We already know the starters won’t play, but plenty of young guys and roster-bubble players will be putting their blood, sweat, and tears into this game. Many of the guys who will play in this game for both sides will have serious job uncertainty by Sunday evening (6 PM ET), when teams officially have to cut down to 53 men. Then comes the flurry of calls for practice squads or possibly spots on other teams’ rosters. The most stressful game of musical chairs, where if you are left without a seat, you likely have to focus on staying in football shape, hoping to get a call, or call it quits on your dream. People will diminish this game, but truthfully, it will be the last time so many guys in the NFL suit up and get a shot until next offseason, if at all. Players like wide receiver Dohntae Meyers and defensive tackle Landon Robinson going off and showing they belong on an NFL roster is what this time of year is all about. However, as one story rises, we often see the end of another. Someone like Charlie Jones or Mitchell Tinsley — who was a preseason darling himself last year with some highlights during the regular season— could find themselves on a different roster or sitting on the practice squad. It is a numbers game at the end of the day. You can only keep so many wide receivers, tight ends or defensive tackles. And players know the harsh truth that this is a business at the end of the day. It is just one of those times to remember that the players who aren’t the Joe Burrows or Ja’Marr Chases of the NFL are closer to their dream being over at the drop of a hat than many of us realize. Who was the player you were rooting for the most this offseason, or who do you think is going to be the most surprising cut come Sunday? Bengals News What to Watch For | Bengals at Eagles Preseason Week 3 Some other young O-lineman have made a strong impression on Taylor and the coaching staff through training camp, including fourth-round draft pick Connor Lew, who spent the early portion of camp recovering from a knee injury but started at center against the Bears. According to Taylor, Lew has made up for the valuable time lost while finishing his rehab. Another strong vote of confidence in Lew from the head coach. There is no question this guy will likely be the first man up if something happens at guard. Marvin Lewis says ‘Mike Brown doesn’t give a (expletive) about money’ “His words trigger action,” Lewis said. “No question in my mind, they trigger action, because (Brown) loves quarterbacks and he wants to win in the worst way.” Well worth a listen to the interview. It feels like Lewis has not really talked in depth about his experience with the Bengals. Him talking about Burrow’s word triggering actions is interesting in particular. One Bengals Offseason Acquisition Itching to Start 2026 Season “I’m buzzing with a lot of excitement right now,” Cook said when talking about taking the field for the first time as a member of his hometown team this season. Safe to say most Bengals fans are also buzzing with excitement. Hopefully replacing Geno Stone with Cook offers a better result on the back end of the defense. NFL News NFL Network: Seahawks, DT Leonard Williams agree to three-year, $90M extension Somewhere down the line Dexter Lawrence is going to need paid. Whether the team is willing to go that high for someone entering their 30’s will remain to be seen, but this is a bit of a look into the future as the defensive tackle market isn’t rising as rapidly as some other positions. 2026 NFL fantasy football draft tips: 18 must-know Do’s and Don’ts Some quick advice going into your fantasy drafts. My advice, start an auction league. It is way more fun and takes more skill than simply drafting players typically. There is nothing wrong with regular drafts, but give auction a try. Packers star RB Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors Ignoring the obvious terrible human being implications of this to focus on the football side of things to keep things short… Jacobs is probably hoping whatever video doesn’t come out. We have seen that it has (unfortunately) taken videos coming out for the public to show a real outcry about this kind of stuff.

full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 27: Dylan Fairchild #63 of the Cincinnati Bengals drops back to block during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 27, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bengals’ offensive line is a unique combination of youth and experience. It’s also a combination of free agent acquisitions and draft picks. As far as breakout candidates go, third-year right tackle Amarius Mims has gotten several picks to be just that for the Bengals this season. However, in Pro Football Focus’ breakout candidate for all 32 NFL teams , they listed a different offensive lineman: Second-year left guard Dylan Fairchild. Here is what PFF’s Gordon McGuiness had to say about the Bengals’ third-round pick out of Georgia in the 2025 NFL Draft: The Bengals drafted guard Dylan Fairchild with the 81st overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, and the former Georgia Bulldog started 15 games as a rookie. Over the final eight games of the season, his 74.3 PFF pass-blocking grade ranked first among rookie guards and fourth among all rookie offensive linemen. He is capable of developing into the Bengals’ best offensive lineman by the end of the 2026 season. Fairchild proved right away he belongs and can play at a high level in the NFL. Expectations are high for the promising left guard, as he looks to continue to validate his candidacy to be the Bengals’ long-term left guard. If Fairchild can make a big jump this season along with Mims, this offensive line could really surprise people and potentially become a top-10 unit.

He can't wait for week one and told us he's "ready to go." #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/OwKzkiu3lx — Jeremy Rauch (@FOX19Jeremy) August 25, 2026 When asked about preparing for Week 1, Cook had some fun comments. “It feels phenomenal. I’m ready for that first chance to actually put on the uniform.” Cook comes in with fantastic experience and leadership, something that the Bengals defense has desperately lacked since the departure of Jessie Bates a few years ago. Having Cook running the show in the secondary should drastically improve a defense that was the worst I have ever seen.

title: Marvin Lewis shares insight on Mike Brown and Bengals ownership
summary: As a small-market team, the Cincinnati Bengals have always been a franchise the national media picks on and spins narratives about each and every year. The front office has built a reputation over the past several decades but has slowly changed its ‘ways’ to help build a successful team around Joe Burrow. The Bengals extended […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OH - DECEMBER 23, 2018: Head coach Marvin Lewis of the Cincinnati Bengals on the field prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns on December 23, 2018 at FirstEnergy Stadium in Cleveland, Ohio. Cleveland won 26-18. (Photo by: 2018 Nick Cammett/Diamond Images/Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images As a small-market team, the Cincinnati Bengals have always been a franchise the national media picks on and spins narratives about each and every year. The front office has built a reputation over the past several decades but has slowly changed its ‘ways’ to help build a successful team around Joe Burrow. The Bengals extended Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, something every media outlet claimed would never happen. The Bengals traded their first-round pick for superstar defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence, something the franchise has never done and everyone assumed would never happen. The Bengals have invested in the offensive line and have all five starters from last season returning to protect Burrow, something the media gripes on every single day. The Bengals spent roughly $125 million on defensive free agents to help bolster a defense that needed serious help, yet the media says the front office doesn’t spend money. The bottom line is the Bengals front office has changed their ways right in front of our eyes, and former head coach Marvin Lewis shared some interesting insight this week on how the front office operates, specifically Mike Brown. “Let’s talk about the Brown family,” Lewis said in an appearance on the Inside Football podcast . “Mike Brown doesn’t give a shit about money. Don’t waste it. All his money goes to that football team. The man has no outside habits other than reading big ass thick books that I used to just look at on his desk or beside me on the plane. He just wants to win football games the way he wants to win.” Lewis continued, “He doesn’t want to mortgage the franchise on one year and one player. He sees a 3 or 4 year projection and that is different than how some organizations work.” The former head coach went on to give examples of free agents the Bengals front office lost, and that forced them to pivot and figure out another option. He also shared his thoughts on Burrow being the voice for ownership… What Burrow wants, ownership wants to make happen. “I am telling ya, his (Burrow’s) words trigger action, ain’t no question in my mind because that man (Mike Brown) loves quarterbacks and wants to win in the worst way,” Lewis stated. It is neat to hear this perspective from Lewis because he was in the Bengals building every day for years and years.
author: Patrick Carey

title: Browns 53-man roster prediction: Last 4 in, last 4 out
summary: The Cleveland Browns finished their 2026 exhibition schedule on a high note by having their second-and third-string guys demolish the New England Patriots. The contest gave both coaching staffs an idea of who to cut and who to keep. None of the projected starters played, with the exception of the special teams guys. RELATED: BROWNS […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 10: Michael Burton #34 of the Cleveland Browns catches a pass during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 10, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns finished their 2026 exhibition schedule on a high note by having their second-and third-string guys demolish the New England Patriots . The contest gave both coaching staffs an idea of who to cut and who to keep. None of the projected starters played, with the exception of the special teams guys. RELATED: BROWNS CUT TRACKER Now for the difficult part of being an NFL head coach: cutting players. Training camp involves 90 players. On August 30, that roster has to be pared down to 53 guys. It used to be in increments. On the first cut, the roster was down to 75. The cut to 62, and then finally to 53. It made for a lot of drama. But now? That’s a lot of athletes calling their agent to see if some other team put in a waiver claim for them. Who to release, and who to retain? There are rumors that the Browns coaching staff wants to keep all four of their quarterbacks . That is highly unusual because only one plays in every game. After the starter, Deshaun Watson, the remainder in the room are all developmental first-and second-year guys. Yikes. No wily, seasoned veteran to lean on, like when Baker Mayfield had Casey Keenum, or when Deshaun Watson was on suspension, the roster had Jacoby Brissett. By keeping four QBs, this means the roster will release a tight end, a cornerback, or a defensive line player instead. A larger yikes. Every Browns media outlet will give their list of what the final 53 will look like, as DBN did . Today, we are just going to predict who the final four guys the coaching staff will keep, and the four last bubble guys they bumped off. Last four in FB Michael Burton Burton was used in the preseason more as another tight end/H-back than a traditional fullback, although he did line up occasionally in the backfield. He is strictly a blocker, but was thrown to a few times in the Patriots preseason game. Head coach Todd Monken likes having a fullback. The team was expected to draft one but didn’t, so Burton signed. By keeping him, the tight end room can become three players instead of four. WR Luke Floriea This one was tight. Floriea had a great preseason. So did Malachi Corley and Greg Larvadain. Maybe the coaching staff sees Floriea as their very own Wes Welker who will take some slot reps. Hard to tell, but the short white receiver played well when his number was called, and is a good blocker downfield. S Donovan McMillon McMillon is a missile on special teams on kickoff and punt coverage teams. And he does get defensive snaps as well. He is a willing tackler. His special teams play was commendable, which is enough to earn a roster spot in that role with potential upside defensively. CB Michael Coats, Jr. He was signed with a $100,000 guarantee and showed he can ball out as an undrafted rookie. Runs a 4.41. He has had an ankle injury during the first preseason game, and now a second leg injury has arisen. But he has shown quite a bit in training camp. If he can remain healthy, the coaching staff could believe that Coats can provide good depth plus value on special teams. He may not play right away, but once he heals, he should become an asset. Last four out TE Joe Royer Yeah, the coaching staff had high hopes for Royer. He hasn’t been placed on any list – yet. He could end up on the final roster, and then be added to some sort of list, and then get back one guy they wanted to keep. It has happened before. Nobody but the front office seems to know what personal issues Royer is dealing with. WR Malachi Corley Just a numbers game, and Floriea had three to none. That is three touchdown catches to zero for Corley. If he clears waivers, the Browns will get him back to the practice squad and perhaps bring him up as a returner. The coaching staff really likes this guy. Plus, Greg Larvadain has offered more as a returner. S Daniel Thomas The question concerning the fourth safety was: is it going to be Chris Edmonds or Donovan McMillon? Edmonds is already gone, and there is no competition for Thomas to beat out McMillon. Too many players in the room, which most likely sends him to the practice squad. If the coaching staff retains five safeties, then Thomas would become that choice. DE Sam Kamara The Browns keep going back to Kamara like a security blanket since 2022, in that he can play outside or slide into the middle. He has been on the practice squad six times, released five times, and promoted to the roster on six different stints. This will even out all numbers to six with his release once again. Who do you think are the last 4 in/out on the Browns initial 53-man roster? Join the conversation! title: Browns QB room: Patriots game enough to secure roster spots?
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ final preseason game against the New England Patriots allowed both Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green to make their case for a spot on the initial 53-man roster. Gabriel brings experience to the table, having played at multiple college programs and appeared in several games during the 2025 season. Green is coming in as […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns’ final preseason game against the New England Patriots allowed both Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green to make their case for a spot on the initial 53-man roster . Gabriel brings experience to the table, having played at multiple college programs and appeared in several games during the 2025 season. Green is coming in as the rookie looking to show that there are enough tools there that could develop into a competent NFL quarterback. Gabriel started in this matchup and put up a solid performance. He completed 12 of his 15 passes for 186 yards with three touchdowns. Green took over at quarterback in the second half and completed five passes for 27 yards. Additionally, he had eight rushes for 66 yards. Both quarterbacks impressed in different ways and made an argument for why they deserve a spot on this roster. Although Gabriel is clearly the more impressive quarterback of the two, it is more likely that the rookie Green will end up getting a roster spot. Gabriel has the higher floor of the two quarterbacks, but Green is younger and possesses the physical tools that could make him an intriguing player for the team to develop. When looking at the third quarterback on the roster, it is better to look at who has higher upside and could develop into something really valuable for the team in the future. full_text: The Cleveland Browns have until Sunday at 6:00 PM ET to make roster cuts and announce their initial 53-man roster. Some of those cuts or rumors about roster moves might leak early, though. The Browns may also announce them in waves — for example, some cuts may be announced Friday, some on Saturday, etc. All players who are released with less than four years of service must go through waivers and are eligible to be claimed by any other team until 1:00 PM ET on Monday . After that, any unclaimed player can be signed and teams will begin to fill out their 16-man practice squads. Veterans with more than four years of service can sign immediately after being released. You can also use the comments section to discuss cuts around the NFL that may be of interest to Cleveland. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 225/1 odds to win the Super Bowl, heading into final roster cuts. Browns Roster Cuts Live Blog Friday (August 28, 2026) 3:36 PM: By my count, the Browns are now down to 73 players, meaning they have 20 moves remaining to get down to 53 players by Sunday at 6:00 pm ET. I’m not sure if there will be any more moves today, but my current guess is that the remaining moves will be announced tomorrow. What you might start hearing, before that official news release, are player’s agents leaking that “so and so has been informed that they have made the 53 man roster,” or some sources indicating that a particular player has been notified that they’ll be cut. Going back to the first batch of cuts below, none of them are a surprise. Avery was a guy on my 53-man roster, but he was meant to be a temporary placeholder due to injury concerns; I did not expect him to be a long-term player on the roster. 3:25 PM: We have our first batch of Browns cuts: 16 moves in total (4 contracts terminated, 12 players waived). The terminated players are TE Jack Stoll (from IR), OT Tyre Phillips , CB Tre Avery , and CB Tyler Hall . The players waived are WR Ben Patterson , TE Jermaine Terry II , TE Drew Biber , OT Jeremiah Byers , OT Izavion Miller , DT Coziah Izzard , DT Patrick Jenkins , DE Jamil Muhammad , CB Jeremiah McClendon , CB Nate Evans , S Christopher Edmonds , and P Nik Constantinou . 1:24 PM: Not a reportable rumor as I don’t have a second source, but enough to at least share here as a keep-your-eyes-out kinda thing. I’ve heard that the Falcons and Chargers at least discussed a Tua trade, which could open up a spot for Dillon Gabriel in Atlanta (just as everyone joked/expected when Kevin Stefanski was hired there). – Jared 10:15 AM: Regarding the timing of the Browns’ roster cuts, Jared Mueller made a good point on one of our site’s internal communications. Head coach Todd Monken is scheduled to talk to the media at 11:00 AM ET on Saturday, with practice to follow at 12:15 PM on Saturday. It seems highly likely that the Browns will have their 53-man roster decided by then. I’ve never heard of a case where the team keeps players around for one more practice in between making their final roster cuts. 10:02 AM: Good morning, everyone! I posted my 53-man roster projection this morning. There were plenty of tough decisions at quarterback, wide receiver, tight end, and cornerback. With these potential roster cuts, news could literally hit any time between now and Sunday evening. Typically, Andrew Berry does not wait through the deadline to make cuts. We’ll keep you posted on any Browns-related news that comes in, as well as other cuts around the league. One thing to keep in mind is that the final preseason games in general takes place today, as only a few games took place Thursday evening. In general, you likely won’t see league-wide news about roster cuts until Saturday. 12:00 AM: The Browns just finished their third and final preseason game, beating the New England Patriots by a score of 37-13 . We already heard about one big roster cut on Thursday morning, as reports indicated that Cleveland was waiving WR Cedric Tillman . Tillman was going to be a cut on my 53-man roster projection anyway, due to the way things have unfolded in camp this year and the impressive nature of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston .
