title: Browns 53-man roster: Expect creative moves with a few vets, QB room
summary: It is quite impressive how quickly things need to turn from the Cleveland Browns final preseason game to the initial 53-man roster decisions. As we shared in our roster tracker piece, the Browns planned schedule tells us that most of their moves will be made a full 24 hours plus before the NFL’s mandate. As […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Tylan Wallace (16) and Cleveland Browns running back Dylan Sampson (22) run through drills during the first day of training camp, July 29, 2026, at the Cross Country Mortgage Campus in Berea, Ohio. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It is quite impressive how quickly things need to turn from the Cleveland Browns final preseason game to the initial 53-man roster decisions . As we shared in our roster tracker piece , the Browns planned schedule tells us that most of their moves will be made a full 24 hours plus before the NFL’s mandate. As always with the NFL, the details are very important when it comes to the 53-man roster. The waiver process and order can lead teams to make a myriad of decisions differently than they would. As can having veterans on one-year contracts and the flexibility that it can provide the team. Cleveland fans will remember the team doing this with OT Greg Robinson , who was the Browns starting left tackle heading into the 2019 season. Robinson was cut from the initial 53-man roster before being re-signed just a day later. The reason for the Robinson process (to get a player onto IR but not lose them for the season) is no longer a problem, but if GM Andrew Berry and HC Todd Monken want to try to keep all four quarterbacks, releasing a veteran like newly signed DE Derek Barnett , WR Tylan Wallace , and /or FB Michael Burton could be in the cards. The scenario is simple: It is rare that waived players get claimed (no matter the preseason hubbub), but those that do get claimed are generally at high-value positions like QB, OT, CB, DL, and WR. If the Browns hope to keep all four quarterbacks, waiving Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green at the initial cutdown day could lead to a claim. Doing so a day or two later, when they would re-sign a vet they cut, like Barnett, Wallace, or Burton, would make it less likely that another team would claim them. Then Gabriel or Green could have an easier time getting to Cleveland’s practice squad. Teams don’t like claiming a player only to waive them a day later because a more important player became available. It is seen as bad business with agents and even within the team itself. A move of this sort is not certain and would not be limited to just the quarterback position. As long as the player, their agent, and the Browns are on the same page, veterans will often go along with the process and earn slightly more ($100,000 or so) when they return to the team a day or two later.

title: Making a case for the Browns to keep WR Luke Floriea
summary: The worst position group for the Cleveland Browns last year was arguably the wide receiver group. GM Andrew Berry took on the assignment to improve this group and get them out of the hole of being ranked #32 last year. In case you are scoring at home, that is dead last.   In the April […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Wide receiver Luke Floriea #81 of the Cleveland Browns scores a touchdown against cornerback Kindle Vildor #28 of the New England Patriots in the first quarter of a preseason game at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The worst position group for the Cleveland Browns last year was arguably the wide receiver group. GM Andrew Berry took on the assignment to improve this group and get them out of the hole of being ranked #32 last year. In case you are scoring at home, that is dead last. In the April draft, Berry selected KC Concepcion of Texas A&M in Round 1, and then with his very next pick he chose Washington’s Denzel Boston. RELATED: 2026 GAVE FANS WHAT THEY WANT Each NFL club usually retains five or six receivers. For the Browns, Jerry Jeudy and the two rookies are a lock. The coaching staff really likes the development of Isaiah Bond. That leaves two spots. Berry signed Tylan Wallace from the Baltimore Ravens , who is a receiver but was inked for his return skills. But still, he would count as one of the six spots. That leaves one. The competition is between Cedric Tillman, Larvadain, Luke Floriea, Malachi Corley, and undrafted rookie Ben Patterson. Tillman was released before “The Turk” shows up on August 30. That means the one roster spot is down to one guy. Floriea was signed to a reserve/futures deal in January. Jamari Thrash and Corley were tendered in March. Wallace came to Cleveland during the free agency period. Undrafted rookies Aaron Anderson and Kole Wilson were inked right after the draft. Anderson and Thrash ended up injured and were waived with an injury designation. Undrafted rookie Ben Patterson was then signed to fill the void. The Ohio kid Back to Floriea, which is pronounced as “Flo-REE-uh.” He is an Ohio player. He grew up in Mentor, Ohio, and attended Mentor High School, where he played basketball and football despite only being 5’-8” tall and weighing 179 pounds. Floriea was an exceptional basketball player, playing 101 contests and averaging 11.5 points a game, 2.7 rebounds, 2.0 steals, and 4.4 assists. 22 times in his final three seasons, he was named the “Player of the Game.” In football, he played receiver and ran a 4.48 in the 40 with a vertical leap of 32”. As a senior, he had 52 receptions for 939 yards and 14 touchdowns. He was named Second Team All-Ohio, First Team All-District, and First Team All-County. He was listed as a three-star recruit. Athletics run in the family, as his sister Paige was a track star. He had plenty of offers, but chose Kent State. His career totals are 48 games played, 100 receptions for 1,321 yards, 12 TDs, a 13.2 yards-per-reception average, and four rushes for 23 yards with a single score. Floriea was also a return man with seven kickoffs for a 17.8 yards-per-return average, plus 21 punt returns with an average of 7.6 yards per return. After his junior and senior seasons, Floriea was named First Team All-MAC and received a Hula Bowl invite. As a senior, he caught 44 receptions for 699 yards with seven touchdowns. He ranked fifth in the conference in yards per catch (15.9). The sixth and final receiver spot on the Browns’ roster is up for grabs. Last year, Floriea was a bubble guy as well, was waived, and then spent the year on Cleveland’s practice squad. Versus the Patriots Going into the final preseason game with the New England Patriots, it was made known that the starters weren’t going to play, and this contest was for the bottom third of the roster to prove that they deserved a roster spot. Like Floriea. Against New England, Floriea was lined up with the second team. The final catch of the first drive impressed. Cleveland had driven down to New England’s seven-yard line with a first-and-goal. Rocket Sanders had gotten most of the yardage to finally get the offense down close. With Dillon Gabriel at quarterback, he found Floriea who had come from the left slot to the right flats, alone at the 9-yard line. He then headed to the right pylon despite three defenders bearing down on him. Staying in-bounds by inches, he fought his way to the pylon for the game’s first touchdown with CB Kindle Vildor and S John Saunders all over him. Luke powering it in for 6! #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/b8BAvwthgP — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 It wasn’t the crossing route, or getting wide open, or his decision to turn upfield, or his speed. It was the fight to get into the end zone for points that was the most impressive. Make that two touchdowns in two weeks. On the next possession, the pass was to WR Greg Larvadain with 7:31 left in the first quarter. Larvadain caught the ball while Floriea then walled off his man, which gave the receiver an extra six yards on the completed pass. It’s plays like this that don’t show up on the stat sheet. Let’s discuss his second touchdown of the game. The Browns drove down to New England’s fourteen-yard line. Dillon in shotgun, with Floriea now as the right slot receiver. He did a right juke, then immediately cut to the inside and headed towards the left center of the end zone. He pretty much shrugged off his man, CB Marcellas Dial, but still had a safety man deep. The pass hit him perfectly at the seven-yard line with two steps now on Dial. His speed got him to the three as S Dell Pettus approached, Floriea gave him a right-turn head bob. This caused Pettus to pause, which gave Floriea a millisecond. Then the two met at the one with a fight to cross the goal line. DG + Luke = TD 🙌 #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/mYVj4n5MnH — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 Yes, both scores were against the Patriots’ second-team defense. We get that. However, receivers have the job of catching passes and trying to score. Floriea is doing both. He doesn’t drop balls. He doesn’t throw his arms up when he doesn’t make a contested catch. He accepts incompletions. He runs crisp routes. He sells his fakes. He does his job. This year, it just seems different for Floriea. His routes have more meaning. He is giving extra deception and is selling it more. I’ll be completely honest: What you saw from Luke Floriea tonight is what we see every day in practice. He consistently gets open, makes plays, works hard and is a great teammate. This isn’t a feel-good story anymore. I talked about him last year, and he continues to produce.… https://t.co/yL72FhBOJm — Lance Reisland (Coach Riz) (@LanceReisland) August 28, 2026 Take Floriea’s touchdown-not-touchdown in the second quarter. The throw was bad and died heading towards the ground. Yet Floriea made the effort with both hands and was one inch away from his third touchdown of the game. In fact, the initial call was touchdown, but the replay showed a small skip off the turf. Is it enough? Patterson did some good things in the Patriots game, including the 52-yard gain and leading all receivers. He seems destined for the practice squad. Larvadain has had a roller coaster in training camp as well as in preseason games. That might become two down. Sources: Former #Jets WR Malachi Corley is signing with the #Browns . I’m told Corley had multiple opportunities on the open market, and ultimately chose Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/bHXDWo8MGn — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) August 27, 2025 Corley is a guy who failed to wow anybody in preseason, but the coaching staff loves him. He offered more as a complete player last year, even though that was with another staff. But he has a lot of potential, has genuine juice, and came from a college program that was on full throttle every game on offense. He is a weapon once he catches the ball and is an above-average kickoff returner, adding to his versatility. The last receivers on the depth chart usually have to also play on punt and kick coverage units as well, something Corley has experience with. Preseason Comparison: vs. Chicago Bears Corley: 2 targets, 0 receptions,…

This projection is based on the weeks of training camp […]
full_text: It is time for my 53-man roster projection for the Cleveland Browns . Head coach Todd Monken will get together and consult with General Manager Andrew Berry , as they work together to trim the roster to 53 players by 6:00 PM ET on Sunday, August 30. This projection is based on the weeks of training camp reports, the preseason games to date, and my general instincts. color: black; } .dbn tr td:first-child { text-align:center; font-weight:bold; } Reserve/PUP: LB Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah NFI: N/A The list above contains 53 players that I kept. Because practice squads are so big (16 players), I have created a specific column for those players too — although I did not fully fill it. Listed below would be just the 53-man roster, if I was correct on everything. 53-Man Roster Depth Chart (Projected) Position Starter(s) Backup(s) QB – 3 Deshaun Watson Shedeur Sanders, Taylen Green RB – 4 Quinshon Judkins Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders, Michael Burton WR – 6 Jerry Jeudy, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston Isaiah Bond, Luke Floriea, Tylan Wallace TE – 4 Harold Fannin Blake Whiteheart, Carsen Ryan, Joe Royer OT – 4 Spencer Fano, Tytus Howard Dawand Jones, Austin Barber Guard – 3 Zion Johnson, Teven Jenkins KT Leveston Center – 2 Elgton Jenkins Parker Brailsford DE – 4 Jared Verse, Isaiah McGuire Derek Barnett, Julian Okwara DT – 5 Mason Graham, Maliek Collins Mike Hall, Sam Kamara, Adin Huntington LB – 5 Carson Schwesinger, Quincy Williams Winston Reid, Nathaniel Watson, Justin Jefferson CB – 6 Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell Myles Harden, Michael Coats, Tre Avery, Mekhi Blackmon Safety – 4 Ronnie Hickman, Grant Delpit, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren Donovan McMillon Kicker – 1 Andre Szymt Punter – 1 Corey Bojorquez LS – 1 Rex Sunahara General Roster Projection Notes On my first pass through coming up with a 53-man roster, I had 52 players on my list, meaning there was only one player who I needed to add. I debated what to do, but I ultimately threw TE Joe Royer on the roster, not knowing what his status is since he’s missed camp for personal reasons. After the final preseason game, I made one change to my 53-man roster: I removed WR Gage Larvadain and added WR Luke Floriea . I have 10 players listed on my practice squad (16 players can make it). QB: The biggest decision here is to keep three quarterbacks vs. four quarterbacks. Based on what I’ve seen from Dillon Gabriel , I don’t see him cutting it out as a starter. I liked what I saw in the final preseason game, but that was also a very basic defense that he thrived against. We’ve seen him against starting defenses, and things fall apart because teams know what to expect from him. Could he be a decent backup? Maybe. But Shedeur Sanders won that role, and Taylen Green was drafted. I’m forecasting Gabriel being dealt somewhere for a minimal draft pick. RB: The competition at running back is supposed to be Ahmani Marshall vs. Raheim Sanders . I like Sanders, and think he would be the team’s best blocking back too for pass protection, so I picked Sanders. I also threw veteran fullback Michael Burton on the roster, even though he’s missed most of camp. Todd Monken uses fullbacks, and Burton can be leveraged there while Carsen Ryan floats over to tight end. WR: The first four are locked in for sure: Jerry Jeudy , KC Concepcion , Denzel Boston , and Isaiah Bond . After that, determining the remaining two spots is difficult. On one hand, I wanted to pick Gage Larvadain and Luke Floriea , but then I’m thinking, “Is Tylan Wallace going to return punts, and why isn’t Malachi Corley being given more consideration?” I could easily see any combination of the four making it. Initially, I rolled with Larvadain and Wallace. I made the switch after the final preseason game to put Floriea on instead of Larvadain. Unfortunately, Larvadain has shown a bit of a knack of trying to make something out of nothing at times, both at receiver and on punt returns. Floriea has done everything one could ask of a receiver this camp, he gets open, he wins match-ups, and he catches everything. I think either one could clear waivers and get to the practice squad, but I think there’s a slight chance Floriea catches people’s attention, whereas Larvadain more easily gets to the practice squad. TE: The depth here appears thin or inexperienced, and with Jack Stoll on IR, the team lost their potential blocking back. I think they’ll look closely at the waiver wire for a blocker. OL: I don’t think I have anything too surprising here, except whether to keep Zak Zinter or not. I think he and Luke Wypler can slip to the practice squad. DL: Same thing on the defensive trench — I think it seems pretty obvious who will be kept, the question is more so will they keep an extra (tenth) guy. LB: Rinse-and-repeat, there wasn’t a whole lot of debating at linebacker. Although if Carson Schwesinger is to miss any regular season action, they’d need an extra guy temporarily. CB: This is challenging. Michael Coats earned a spot as an undrafted player, but now he’s hurt, and we don’t know how long. I’m hoping it’s just a small ankle injury that maybe warrants short-term IR. New this year, teams can designate two players to go directly to IR without having to “put them on the roster, cut someone else, and then put the player on IR.” Myles Bryant could also make it here over Tre Avery , but I just don’t know his health. And I know very little about Mekhi Blackmon , but Cleveland claimed him on Thursday, so I assume he’s making the initial 53-man roster. S: Considering the top three safeties are basically starters, it might be necessary to have two backups here. For now, I just have one. ST: It’d be a stunner if this differed at all. Note: I have the option to update my 53-man projection if injury-related or other news comes out by Saturday, as far as counting my accuracy goes. I always try to aim for at least 49/53! What Do You Think? Feel free to share your roster projections here, or some changes you would make to mine.

Whether or not a player enters the waiver wire of becomes a free agent depends on a player’s NFL service time. Players with at least four years of accrued NFL service time are outright released. For example, if Deshaun Watson was released, he would immediately become a free agent. He would be eligible to sign with any team, with no waiting period involved. However, if a player has less than four years of service time, they are waived and subject to waiver wire claims. Any player who is not claimed after being waived is eligible to sign wherever they’d like, including their former team’s practice squad. What is the NFL waiver order right now? The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order. After Week 3, the order resets to the current NFL standings. Will the Browns’ Super Bowl odds improve by the time that time rolls around? According to FanDuel , the Browns are 225/1 odds to win the Super Bowl, heading into final roster cuts. If they start winning early, by Week 4, maybe their waiver wire priority will be near the bottom of the pack. The first batch of waiver claims will be due by 1:00 pm ET on Monday, August 31. The Raiders will have first waiver claim priority for cutdowns to 53-man rosters, while the Browns will be sixth in line. title: Browns vs Patriots: 8 takeaways as Dillon Gabriel, Taylen Green each show something
summary: The third preseason game for the Cleveland Browns and New England Patriots did not include a lot of players who will play a lot of snaps in Week 1, but it did include a lot of roster bubble guys. The amazing Browns fans were planning to tune in, with QBs Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green […]
full_text: Aug 27, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel (6) runs the ball against the New England Patriots during the first half at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The third preseason game for the Cleveland Browns and New England Patriots did not include a lot of players who will play a lot of snaps in Week 1, but it did include a lot of roster bubble guys . The amazing Browns fans were planning to tune in, with QBs Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green taking the snaps this week: The biggest stories coming out of the game will be any injuries and how those bubble players perform with the chances that they are given. Some of the evaluation is tougher given the level of talent on the other side of the field, with the Patriots also not playing their top guys. Take everything within that perspective. A few takeaways from Thursday Night Football off the shores of Lake Erie: Rocket Sanders looks good Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson have locked up the top of the depth chart, but Raheim Sanders still has to secure his spot as the third guy. A few carries in the first few series looked like Sanders, nicknamed “Rocket,” is on his way to having that role. Luke Floriea trying to make Browns roster decision tough One of Shedeur Sanders ’ favorite targets, Floriea just keeps making plays, including this touchdown from Gabriel: Luke powering it in for 6! #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/b8BAvwthgP — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 And again! DG + Luke = TD 🙌 #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/mYVj4n5MnH — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 Defensive questions CB D’Angelo Ross is a special teams star and looked totally out of place getting beat for a touchdown throw where he wasn’t anywhere near the receiver while looking into the backfield. Overall, the defense made a couple of big plays, but seemed to benefit from the bad New England offense more than making stops themselves. Dillon Gabriel shows talent, value As noted above, level of competition is a key reference point, but Gabriel showed out in the first half. Not only with the stats, but the long-term college starter looked under control, was rarely rattled, and was smooth with his decisions and delivery of passes. As much as Monken values “operation,” Gabriel was pretty clean throughout. As for the stats, this is Preseason Performance Hall of Fame level: 12 for 15 186 yards 3 touchdowns 4 rushes, 3 yards 157.9 rating There were some very good throws, as well as his receivers making plays and Patriots defenders not making the plays they needed to. For example, the text of this tweet is… interesting… given the play being made by RB Ahmani Marshall after a simple Gabriel pass, but a touchdown is a touchdown: Dillon Gabriel is DEALING. That's 3 TDs in the first half 🔥 NEvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uI7eJFz5WW — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 QB run going to be a big piece of the offense Both Gabriel and Green ran some zone read and other quarterback run-oriented plays. Green’s QB sweep was really well designed and put defenders in difficult positions. It is one reason I believe Watson won the starting QB job and think the QB run will be a huge part of this Al Michaels just saying whatever was funny Michaels made a number of mistakes, railed on the refs, the virtual measurement, and more. Perhaps too much celebration of his 60th wedding anniversary (seriously, that is amazing). Given that the game didn’t matter, Michaels being a little less professional, and showing a little chest hair, was kind of appropriate. Taylen Green’s legs a weapon, a few good passes too As noted above, the QB run game was shown more in this game, but Green’s legs were useful as a scrambler as well. Defenders have to be ready for the run from Green, which can open up lanes for the running backs in option oriented palys and even receivers in some passing concepts. Green finished with eight rushes for 66 yards. Not everything was perfect, of course, but Green hit a few passes as well, including a key checkdown to Floreia to keep a drive going. Social media and our game chat were full of ideas to have a package for Green or to use him on sneaks, the problem there is that Cleveland would have to keep three quarterbacks on their active game-day roster, instead of two and an emergency third QB. Seems unlikely unless injuries require it. Green is only likely to be active if/when he’s the backup QB (or starter). 4 running backs? Davon Booth and Marshall both made plays in the third preseason game. Will the Browns keep four running backs and rely on a tight end to take the fullback role? Veteran FB Michael Burton hasn’t practiced during training camp, while Rocket Sanders, Booth, and Marshall have all made a case for making the roster as well. Perhaps Monken gets creative with his usage, including Sanders taking some snaps at fullback. What were your takeaways from Browns vs Patriots? Join the conversation! summary: Third preseason games don’t matter, but it’s still fun to watch the Cleveland Browns dominate a game and pile on some stats for guys trying to get plays on tape. It was all Cleveland against the Patriots in a 37-13 victory. Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Patriots The […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Dillon Gabriel #6 of the Cleveland Browns calls a play during the first quarter of a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Third preseason games don’t matter, but it’s still fun to watch the Cleveland Browns dominate a game and pile on some stats for guys trying to get plays on tape. It was all Cleveland against the Patriots in a 37-13 victory. Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Patriots The Browns received the opening kickoff, as QB Dillon Gabriel came on to the field. He orchestrated an opening-drive touchdown, finishing it with a playaction pass to WR Luke Floriea , who stayed in bounds along the boundary for the 6-yard touchdown to put Cleveland up 7-0. Dillon Gabriel ➡️ Luke Floriea for a Browns TD! NEvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fZE1gP0gTz — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 The Patriots gave the start to QB Tommy DeVito , and he found WR Kyle Williams open down the left sideline for a 45-yard touchdown, as CB D’Angelo Ross appeared to lose track of the ball. That tied the game up at 7-7. . @tommydevito007 to @k_mmoneyyyy DIME 🎯 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/wtuNHzpYIa — New England Patriots (@Patriots) August 28, 2026 The action continued on the next drive. Gabriel hit WR Gage Larvadain over the middle for 21 yards, and later WR Ben Patterson for 19 yards. On 2nd-and-6 from the 14 yard line, Gabriel found Floriea again in stride for 14 yards and another touchdown to make it a 14-7 game. DG + Luke = TD 🙌 #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/mYVj4n5MnH — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 The Patriots went three-and-out on their next drive, and then Gabriel started the next drive by rolling to his left and finding Patterson, who caught the defensive back flat-footed for a catch-and-run of 52 yards. That helped set up a 35-yard field goal by K Andre Szmyt to put the Browns up 17-7. QB Behren Morton came on for the Patriots. On his first pass, he tried to hit a tight end who was busy blocking, so it hit the back of his leg and bounced in the air. LB Easton Mascarenas-Arnold tipped it in the air and came down with the interception to wrap up the opening quarter. we'll take that thank youuu #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/T8dDqriLHP — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 2nd Quarter – Browns vs. Patriots Gabriel went three-and-out for the first time on the day, but the Browns were still in field goal range. Szmyt hit from 47 yards out to put the Browns up 20-7. After Morton’s first series lasted one play, his second one lasted 14 plays and 7:13 of clock. DE Khordae Sydnor registered his third sack of the preseason in the red zone, though, which helped force New England into a 26-yard field goal to cut the Browns’ lead to 20-10. . @KhordaeS got him good 😮‍💨 #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/wJumJHlc3k — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 On Gabriel’s next drive, he moved the ball again, and nearly gave Floriea the hat trick for what was initially ruled a 16-yard touchdown pass. However, replay review showed that the throw was low and just barely touched the ground for an incomplete pass. A few plays later, Gabriel still found RB Ahmani Marshall for a 7-yard touchdown for a 27-10 lead. TD no. 3 on the day for Dillon! #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/IUuwDLPDYL — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 S Donovan McMillian came up with an interception after the two-minute warning, but the official threw a flag for pass interference on him. Replays showed that it was a bad call and the interception should have counted. The defense still held tight to close out the half, holding New England to a 33-yard field goal to make it a 27-13 game. 3rd Quarter – Browns vs. Patriots The Patriots began the half, but could only get to midfield before having to punt. That punt was run backward by Larvadain, back to the 2 yard line, for QB Taylen Green’s first drive. Green’s only chance to do anything was on 3rd-and-long, and his scramble fell just short of a first down. The Browns punted, and then New England punted right back to Cleveland, with the drive starting at the 2 yard line again. Green really got to show off his legs on the drive, including running around in his own end zone and then taking off for 30 yards. Between that, and a mix of short passes, Cleveland finished the third quarter near a goal-to-go situation. a runner and a track star 🏃💨 #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/XjzMkQH92H — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 4th Quarter – Browns vs. Patriots A few plays into the quarter, RB Davon Booth got the handoff and executed a spin move to dodge a defender and walk into the end zone for the 8 yard touchdown and a 34-13 lead. put the spin cycle on him 🔄 #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/wdVUCVET1g — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 On Green’s next drive, he got into New England territory again, but had his first incompletion on a third down pass that sailed over the receiver, leading to a punt. The Patriots went for it on 4th-and-2 in their own territory, and Morton was picked off by LB Justin Jefferson , returned to the 12 yard line. a big pick and a big return for JJ! #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/K0vvxx3lE2 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 It only led to a field goal for Cleveland, making it 37-13. The Patriots ran out the clock from there. Quick Hitters QB Dillon Gabriel: 12-of 15 for 186 yards, 3 TD. QB Taylen Green: 5-of-7 for 27 yards. 8 carries, 66 yards. WR Luke Floriea: 3 catches, 29 yards, 2 TD. Next up, the Browns will trim their roster to 53 players and get ready for the regular season.

title: 3 roster issues to settle in the Cowboys preseason finale
summary: The famous saying “blink and you’ll miss it” could not be more true. After an offseason that felt like an eternity, the Cowboys are just two weeks away from the start of their regular season. With their third and final preseason game on Friday night, the Cowboys have multiple roster spots up for grabs that […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Jaishawn Barham #55 of the Dallas Cowboys gets ready to make a play during a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The famous saying “blink and you’ll miss it” could not be more true. After an offseason that felt like an eternity, the Cowboys are just two weeks away from the start of their regular season. With their third and final preseason game on Friday night, the Cowboys have multiple roster spots up for grabs that can be decided against the New Orleans Saints. Today we will look at three burning questions the Cowboys will need to answer before the start of their 2026 season. 3. Who will win the starting linebacker job? One of the major questions coming into training camp was the Cowboys situation at the linebacker spot. With DeMarvion Overshown’s injury history and Dee Winters having limited starting experience, most Cowboy fans had 2025 PTSD about what the linebacker position could look like. With two weeks before the start of the season, the linebacker position was one of the many positive developments in training camp and throughout two preseason games. Rookie LB Jaishawn Barham has stormed onto the scene. Despite missing some time with a groin injury, you can make the argument Barham has been one the Cowboys five best players so far this offseason. Along with Barham’s charge, Winters has also had a nice camp and has brought a calming sense to the Cowboys linebacker room alongside Overshown. Just a year ago, the Cowboys struggled to put a single capable linebacker on the field, but now it sure seems like they have three, maybe even four with Shemar James making positive strides in year two. Whether it’s Barham or Winters on the field alongside Overshown when the season kicks off against the New York Giants, the Cowboys have two solid options to pick from, which is a huge upgrade from where they were in 2025. 2. Will Camden Brown earn his star? Speaking of top five performers in training camp, Camden Brown was one of the biggest stars of training camp and preseason action for the Cowboys. After signing with the team as a UDFA, not many people expected Brown to push for a roster spot this offseason, but boy did he do that. Brown has shown more than enough to make the Cowboys final 53-man roster, but given the Cowboys numbers at the wide receiver position, Jonathan Mingo’s offseason development, and the need for roster spots on the defensive side of the ball, it seems to be a 50/50 chance if Brown will make the final roster, or look to clear waivers and head to the practice squad. 1. Will the Cowboys add a veteran CB? It has been rumored for a few weeks now that the Cowboys have been hunting veteran cornerbacks before the start of the regular season. With DaRon Bland, Cobie Durant, Shavon Revel Jr., and Caleb Downs expected to play most of the snaps at cornerback, Bland’s injury history and Revel’s lack of experience has many concerned that the depth behind those four could be improved. Adoree Jackson’s name was tied to the Cowboys recently given his relationship with Christian Parker. Whether it be Jackson or another veteran option on the market, it sure doesn’t sound like the Cowboys are set at the cornerback position as of today.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 16
summary: It is Day 16 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: It is Day 16 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Strap in for Day 16 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the afternoon the Cowboys’ 1990s dynasty first began to feel possible. Dallas went into Soldier Field with a young roster, a backup quarterback and no playoff victory since the 1982 season. But Jimmy Johnson’s team delivered the postseason breakthrough that opened the door to everything that followed. Sunday, December 29, 1991 — 12:30 p.m. ET Soldier Field, Chicago, Illinois Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 17, Chicago Bears 13 The Cowboys, having finished 11-5, returned to the playoffs for the first time since 1985. However, Troy Aikman was still recovering from a knee injury, leaving Steve Beuerlein to start against an experienced Chicago team that had also gone 11-5. Despite the Bears producing more yardage throughout the afternoon, Dallas protected the football, created takeaways, and repeatedly stood firm near their own goal line. Bill Bates helped create the opening points by forcing Jim Harbaugh to fumble on Chicago’s first possession. Defensive end Tony Hill recovered near midfield, and Ken Willis eventually converted a 27-yard field goal to give Dallas a 3-0 lead. Special teams then presented another opportunity. Darrick Brownlow blocked a Bears’ punt, and Ken Norton Jr. recovered at the Chicago 10-yard line. Four plays later, Emmitt Smith scored from one yard out, extending the Cowboys’ advantage to 10-0 during the first quarter. Chicago moved the ball effectively, but struggled to convert drives. During the second quarter, they reached the Dallas two-yard line, but Jack Del Rio and Tony Tolbert stopped consecutive rushing attempts, forcing a turnover on downs. Chicago later returned to the two-yard line but settled for Kevin Butler’s 19-yard field goal just before halftime, leaving Dallas ahead 10-3. Butler added a 43-yard field goal during the third quarter to reduce the margin to four. Dallas answered with its most important offensive possession of the game, travelling 75 yards in 14 plays. Beuerlein kept the drive alive with two 22-yard completions to Michael Irvin before finding Jay Novacek for a three-yard touchdown on third-and-goal. The methodical response restored a 17-6 lead. The Bears continued their relentless pressure in the fourth quarter. Another drive reached the Dallas seven, but Harbaugh’s fourth-down pass fell incomplete. However, Chicago eventually scored when Harbaugh connected with Tom Waddle for a six-yard touchdown, cutting the score to 17-13. This gave the Bears one final opportunity to secure the victory. Mike Saxon’s 52-yard punt pinned Chicago at its own four-yard line with 1:50 remaining. Three plays later, Bates intercepted Harbaugh at the Bears’ 16, allowing Dallas to run out the clock. The veteran who connected the Landry era to Johnson’s rebuilding project had made the first and final defensive plays that shaped the victory. This game belongs on the countdown because it was the moment Dallas’ young core gained postseason credibility. The Cowboys lost heavily at Detroit in the Divisional Round the following week, but the victory in Chicago proved the rebuilding process had reached a new stage. #Cowboys vs #Bears 1991 NFC Wild Card Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 17, Chicago Bears 13 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/9QIktvIth3 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 28, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The victory was Dallas’ first postseason win since defeating Green Bay in the 1982 NFC playoffs. title: Questions facing the Cowboys entering the final preseason game
summary: For most of the offseason, the Dallas Cowboys have operated with fewer distractions than usual, keeping them under the radar. Then, after two strong performances in the first two preseason games, Dallas became a focus of sports talk television, raising the question, “Is this finally the year they do it?” Before jumping too far ahead […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Nate Thomas #71 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the second quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images For most of the offseason, the Dallas Cowboys have operated with fewer distractions than usual, keeping them under the radar. Then, after two strong performances in the first two preseason games, Dallas became a focus of sports talk television, raising the question, “Is this finally the year they do it?” Before jumping too far ahead in that conversation, the Cowboys have one more preseason game to play at home against the New Orleans Saints. The top end of the roster is almost set for the season opener, but questions remain about what to do with the final spots and who will win certain competitions. Who sits and who plays on Friday night will tell us a lot to begin with, but here are four remaining questions Dallas needs answers to by the end of the preseason finale. Can Dallas keep three quarterbacks? Joe Milton has performed exceptionally well in his second season as a backup to Dak Prescott. When Dallas signed Sam Howell, it “pissed off” Milton , but it also brought out the best in him and pushed him to become a proficient commander of the offense. Milton has the fourth most passing yards in the preseason (286), leads quarterbacks in passing touchdowns (3) and passer rating (142.9) for any quarterback who has had 20 percent of the total dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus . Sam Howell has made a case for himself to stay on the roster as well. His first preseason game was better than the second, but Brian Schottenheimer continues to praise him and what he’s brought to the quarterback room. If Howell does nothing more than continue to keep that fire under Milton lit the entire season and grow as a player, does that justify keeping Howell in the building on the 53? If the Cowboys cut either quarterback, it might not be as easy to claim them back on the practice squad, since good backup play is hard to come by in the NFL. Dallas has kept three quarterbacks in the past. This roster makes it much harder to find a scenario where that’s possible. Does Dallas keep five or six wide receivers? Over the last week, there’s been chatter on social media about Camden Brown’s flaws. He can’t separate; he doesn’t have the finishing speed; Dallas could find another developmental wide receiver. And then Brown makes another highlight play in training camp practice that makes everyone remember how consistent he’s been all offseason, forcing his way onto the 53-man roster. Camden Brown continuing to make athletic grabs (🎥: @dallascowboys , @CBSNewsTexas ) pic.twitter.com/3qsK5TyChI — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 27, 2026 Jonathan Mingo has also played extremely well in training camp and in the preseason games. He has four catches on five targets, 82 receiving yards, one touchdown, and a 90.5 PFF grade, which is fifth-best among all wide receivers in the preseason . Add that on top of him becoming a special teams player for Dallas, and it makes it hard to cut a player like Mingo, too, who Dallas has invested a ton of time in and has been patient. If Dallas decides to go with five wideouts, which player would be unlikely to return to the practice squad and get claimed by another team? The way Brown has flashed and has been showcased in games could catch the eye of another team looking to bring on a developmental player who’s ahead of the curve as a rookie. Mingo gives another team a pro-ready player who elevates the back end of a wide receiver room, with the potential to be a high-end WR3 for a team like the Miami Dolphins. The best-case scenario is that both players make the 53, and Dallas goes short at another position. It shouldn’t be an either-or conversation because both players deserve to be on the final roster. Do the Cowboys have their backup tackles? Nick Leverett, Ajani Cornelius, and Trevor Keegan have played really well in the interior of the offensive line. With T.J. Bass already locked in as the sixth offensive lineman, Dallas might only be able to keep two of the three. That’s a small potato question (if you know, you know). The big potato question is what Dallas should do about their backup offensive tackles? Nate Thomas was supposed to push Tyler Guyton at left tackle for a starting job. Guyton quickly ended that battle, pushing Thomas down to backup. Throughout training camp and the preseason, things haven’t always looked great for the former seventh-round pick. The team has tried him at left and right tackle to practice position flex, but his development seems to be taking a step back instead of forward. For a player who has started four games in the NFL, Dallas was hoping for more. Drew Shelton will need more time to grow as an NFL tackle. The 2026 fourth-round pick has not been great and has given up the second-most pressures (seven) of any offensive lineman in the preseason. Like Thomas, the coaching staff has tried to move him from right to left so he can learn to be a swing tackle and find the best role for him. Dallas might not feel great about where either player is in their development, and with Cornelius moving to offensive guard, the Cowboys might have to find their swing tackle on the open market. If the front office has to pick either Thomas or Shelton to make the initial 53-man roster, the tie would probably go to Shelton, considering he’s the most recent draft pick and Dallas doesn’t usually give up on fourth-round picks this early. Sam Williams or Marist Liufau? After the Cowboys signed Von Miller, it took away a roster spot from James Houston, Sam Williams, and Marist Liufau. Instead of all three making the team, the competition could come down to two. All three can play on special teams and have been really good at it, so who makes the roster might be decided by who can show the most as a pass rusher. Houston was a surprise for Dallas last year, getting 3.5 sacks in the first five games as a rotational player. He’s also continued that production in the preseason. Houston is the one Dallas might be most confident in out of the three. Williams re-signed with Dallas on a one-year deal after testing the waters of free agency and getting nothing on the open market. The transition to a 3-4 defense could benefit him at stand-up outside linebacker. Williams has done a lot on special teams during the regular season, but has hurt the Cowboys at times with costly penalties. Do the Cowboys still believe the same player exists who had 8.5 sacks over the first two seasons of his career? After two seasons at off-ball linebacker, Liufau made the switch to outside linebacker in the new scheme in what feels like a last-ditch effort to make the cut. Liufau has received praise from Schottenheimer for the way he’s attacked the transition and played with effort. Watching the preseason games, it looks like he may be too small to consistently go up against offensive tackles and blocking tight ends. Despite being the most recent draft pick of the three players listed, he might not fit the scheme anymore. The final preseason game will be a chance for all three to make their final mark, with Williams and Liufau being at the center of it.

title: Camden Brown represents strong Cowboys tradition
summary: Who is the most likely undrafted free agent to make this year’s Dallas Cowboys roster? The answer is Camden Brown. It is certainly possible that another could find his way there, but right now, Brown is the leader in the clubhouse if there is one. Given that we are talking about the Cowboys, we can […]
full_text: FRISCO, TEXAS - AUGUST 25: Camden Brown #6 of the Dallas Cowboys runs during practice at The Star in Frisco on August 25, 2026 in Frisco, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images Who is the most likely undrafted free agent to make this year’s Dallas Cowboys roster? The answer is Camden Brown. It is certainly possible that another could find his way there, but right now, Brown is the leader in the clubhouse if there is one. Given that we are talking about the Cowboys, we can almost set our watches by the fact that one UDFA will make the team. There has been at least one on the final roster for the last four years running. Things go way beyond that, though. The Cowboys have noted in their public messaging that they have seen at least one UDFA make the initial 53-man roster in 10 of the last 11 seasons. 2021 is the only outlier. The last five, per the team’s records: 2020: Terence Steele 2022: Markquese Bell, T.J. Bass, Juanyeh Thomas 2023: Hunter Luepke, Tyrus Wheat 2024: Brevyn Spann-Ford 2025: Zion Childress When you think of the Cowboys and UDFA history your mind generally goes to the likes of Tony Romo, Miles Austin, and/or Dan Bailey. They are certainly among the more successful. It is hardly a team tradition to carry an undrafted guy, and if there isn’t one qualified then the Cowboys shouldn’t force the issue for the sake of some sort of streak or data point; however, Camden has certainly proven he is worthy. In fact, there aren’t many fans who wouldn’t put him on their own personal 53 right now. If he does make it though it will be the latest example of the legacy that the Cowboys are building through this particular method of roster management. What’s your call BTB? Will Camden Brown make the 53? Will another UDFA?

title: Cowboys news: Jobs are up for grabs in the Cowboys preseason finale
summary: Dallas Cowboys’ Toughest 53-Man Roster Decisions With Cutdown Day Looming – Mike Moraitis, SI.com The Cowboys final preseason game is tonight. There are still multiple big decisions to be made for the final 53-man roster. What will the toughest decisions be? Jonathan Mingo vs. Camden Brown As disappointing as he has been during his career, […]
full_text: FRISCO, TEXAS - AUGUST 25: Camden Brown #6 of the Dallas Cowboys runs during practice at The Star in Frisco on August 25, 2026 in Frisco, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dallas Cowboys’ Toughest 53-Man Roster Decisions With Cutdown Day Looming – Mike Moraitis, SI.com The Cowboys final preseason game is tonight. There are still multiple big decisions to be made for the final 53-man roster. What will the toughest decisions be? Jonathan Mingo vs. Camden Brown As disappointing as he has been during his career, Mingo has more experience than Brown, but the rookie has had a fantastic camp and preseason and looks the part of an NFL-caliber wide receiver. With what the Cowboys have invested in Mingo following their head-scratching trade with the Carolina Panthers in 2024, and with Mingo managing to have a solid offseason , we think Dallas keeps him for another year. That leaves the Cowboys with a tough decision because they do not need six wide receivers thanks to a loaded group that includes CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy, and KaVontae Turpin is locked in, also. Why Cowboys fans shouldn’t fret if Dallas waives their favorite WR on the roster bubble – Joseph Hoyt, The Dallas Morning News One of the Cowboys best training camp battles showcased Johnathan Mingo vs Camden Brown. Will Brown earn his way onto the roster or will the Cowboys bite their nails while waiting to see if he clears waivers? With expectations on the rise, it’s easy to forget the Cowboys nearly lost Flournoy a year ago. Dallas waived Flournoy during the roster shuffle after the cutdown deadline. Any team could’ve claimed a receiver who eventually grew into the team’s unquestioned third option behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but they didn’t. Flournoy cleared waivers and returned to the team’s practice squad. Game analysis, roster moves and key developments on the Cowboys, from AT&T Stadium to The Star.Email “There was a lot of anxiety,” Schottenheimer said about potentially losing Flournoy on waivers. The Cowboys remain Jerry’s world, but Stephen Jones will engineer ‘a different path’ – Zack Keefer, The Athletic How will the Cowboys operate post Jerry Jones? Even though we know who will be taking over, here’s an in-depth look at what might look different. Stephen ditched the oil business, moved to Dallas and heeded his father’s advice. He started from the bottom. He was a gofer, a sales rep, an understudy. He learned how to brand the Cowboys and how to sell the Cowboys. He learned to negotiate. “No one’s gonna care about our money like we will,” Jerry used to tell him. He’d fume when his father was criticized in the newspapers, which, back then, was all the time. He became a buffer, smoothing over some of the tensions between Jerry and the first coach he brought to town. “I could work with Stephen Jones anytime,” Jimmy Johnson has said over the years. A decade later, Jerry brags, Bill Parcells would echo the sentiment. 3 position battles to watch in the Cowboys preseason finale – LP Cruz, Blogging the Boys It’s unlikely we will see any regular season starters in the final preseason game, but there are still roster battles to keep our eyes on. Which one will you have your focus on? The Cowboys have a good mix of veteran and young talent to lead their pass rush group. Adding Rashan Gary and Von Miller, who has plenty left in the tank, provides the team with excellent experience. Along with them are Malachi Lawrence and Donovan Ezeiruaku, who have the talent to explode for double-digit sacks. The bottom of the pecking order is left to fight for a roster spot and reps, and that has created a heated battle with Marist Liufau and Sam Williams, who are clinging to a possible spot on the team. Sam Williams has put together a nice camp for himself and has shown up in the first two games. Williams recorded a sack against the Arizona Cardinals last week. Cowboys’ leadership council is taking pressure off Prescott The Cowboys have lacked true leadership in the locker room for quite some time. But like many other aspects of the 2026 Cowboys, it sounds like that is changing. In his second year, Schottenheimer, with the recommendations of his coordinators, put together an 11-player leadership council. In his first season, Schottenheimer wanted a “one voice” approach — his — although he would often meet with players to get the pulse of what the locker room was feeling. The 11 players on the 2026 leadership council are Prescott, CeeDee Lamb , Tyler Smith , Tyler Booker , Jake Ferguson , Javonte Williams , Bryan Anger , Quinnen Williams , Kenny Clark , Rashan Gary , and Jalen Thompson . The council meets about every two weeks to discuss things that have happened and what might happen down the road. Could Cowboys Cut a Rookie Picked in the Top 120? Why Dallas might be facing a tough decision ahead of roster cutdown day – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys have multiple 2026 draft picks fighting for roster spots heading into the preseason finale. The Cowboys picked Drew Shelton with pick No. 112 in the fourth round. The expectation set on him right away was for him to be depth early on in his career and maybe even compete for a swing tackle role. But so far, he’s looked struggled much more than expected. At this point, he simply doesn’t look like a viable NFL tackle. I don’t mean to pile on the player, as he could still develop into a solid lineman with time. But Shelton’s struggles have been very apparent in the preseason, to the point of landing a 3.0 pass-blocking grade from PFF in Week 2 of the preseason. Daily discussion question: What do you most want to see tonight?

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Predicting the 53-man roster
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jess Haynie, Sean Martin, and Tom Ryle.  Time to predict the 53-man roster. On offense, who do you predict to be the running backs on the final […]
full_text: FRISCO, TEXAS - AUGUST 25: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys lines up under center during practice at The Star in Frisco on August 25, 2026 in Frisco, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jess Haynie, Sean Martin, and Tom Ryle. Time to predict the 53-man roster. On offense, who do you predict to be the running backs on the final roster, the wide receiver corps, and the tight ends? MIKE: At running back, I’d keep Javonte Williams, Malik Davis, Jaydon Blue and Hunter Luepke. Williams is locked in as the lead back, Davis feels like the safest RB2 because of consistency and reliability, Blue gives them the change-of-pace element, and Luepke’s fullback and special teams value makes him hard to cut. At wide receiver, I’d go with CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, KaVontae Turpin, Jonathan Mingo and Camden Brown, this one seems easy to predict. At tight end, the keepers will be Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker. Ferguson is TE1, Spann-Ford should be TE2 and has the momentum to take a bigger role, while Schoonmaker probably sticks because of draft investment, experience and the fact Dallas has treated him like a safe veteran during preseason. Michael Trigg is the tempting upside choice, but Trigg’s injury makes that harder for me unless Dallas is willing to gamble. JESS : At RB I have Williams, Davis, Blue, and Luepke. At this point, Mafah and/or Abanikanda feel practice squad bound. WRs are Lamb, Pickens, Flournoy, Turpin, Brown and Mingo. I think they go long there with six because they can now stash Trigg on IR, which means they’ll only keep Ferguson, Spann-Ford, and Schoonmaker on the 53. TOM: I’ll second Jess on both RB and TE, but I’ll throw a curveball on WR. It’s obvious that Lamb, Pickens, and Flournoy are the top three weapons, with Turpin, primarily a return specialist, counting as part of the group. But I think they will dangle one or both of Brown and Mingo as trade bait. There are some receiver hungry teams out there that might be willing to part with a decent pick. With other options to stash on the PS, I think Jerry and his brain trust would close a deal. (If you force me, I’m guessing Brown would go because of how cheap he is. This is not an endorsement of a trade on my part, just something that popped into my warped mind.) SEAN : Designating Hunter Luepke as a running back for this, I’d have him along with Javonte Williams, Jaydon Blue, and Malik Davis. I like what Phil Mafah brings, but unfortunately for him I also don’t see anything he does remarkably better than Williams or Davis in the ground-and-pound game, or Blue in the pass game. At wide receiver, the locks are obviously CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, KaVontae Turpin, and like Jess I’m also going to keep both Camden Brown and Jonathan Mingo. Leaving just Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford, and Luke Schoonmaker at tight end. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s interest in Zack Kuntz is notable here, but he hasn’t done enough or nearly have the time remaining before cuts to make enough of an impact to beat out any of the other three here. On defense, name the final defensive line players you predict to make the roster. MIKE: Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Otito Ogbonnia, Jonathan Bullard and L.T. Overton inside, with Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Von Miller, Malachi Lawrence, James Houston and Marist Liufau on the edge. The interior feels mostly settled, but the tougher call is the edge group. Gary, Ezeiruaku, Miller and Lawrence feel safe, then I’d keep Houston as the pass-rush specialist and Liufau over Sam Williams because of position flexibility and special teams value. JESS : I’m struggling with Jonathan Bullard right now. He’s missed almost the entire summer, and it seems like L.T. Overton is stepping up and capable of playing the same role. If they keep Bullard, it may just be those two, Williams, Clark, and Ogbonnia. If they cut Bullard, it’ll be for either Tommy Dunn or Jay Toia. It’ll also be one of those two guys if they keep a sixth DL. TOM: Wait, what about the OLBs? I don’t see them in any of Jess’ projections. And I’m not at all certain how many will be carried at any of the positions. But here’s my choice for the guys that get their hands down: I will say they keep both Overton and Bullard to go with the obvious ones of Williams, Clark, and Ogbonnia. I think they have to have at least six. SEAN : Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, Otito Ogbonnia, Jay Toia, LT Overton, and Jonathan Bullard would be my six. Again, I agree with Jess about being up in the air about Bullard, but at the end of the day veterans with pass rush juice don’t get cut from teams looking to make some real noise (see: the Von Miller signing). Toia was super impressive against the Cardinals in the preseason game and worthy of his spot as well. Name the linebackers you predict to be on the final 53-man roster. MIKE: DeMarvion Overshown is the clear leader and green-dot defender, Dee Winters is obviously locked in after Dallas invested in him, and Jaishawn Barham is too intriguing as a rookie weapon to leave off the roster. Shemar James sticks because of athletic upside and development, while Barron gets the final spot because of his versatility and special teams value. JESS : This one’s easy: Overshown, Winters, Barham, James, and Barron. If they keep six, throw in Curtis Robinson. But the pecking order at that spot feels pretty clear. TOM: Inside, I concur on the top five. Now you have to figure out the OLBs. Gary, Ezeiruaku, Miller, and Lawrnece seem the four locks. I think they’ll keep at least five to keep throwing outside rushers at the opponents. I’ll give Houston the nod over Williams, but wouldn’t be surprised if they go the other way. SEAN: Ah, the position that’s been turned on its head the most by the latest scheme and coaching change on defense. Starting with the pass rushers, we go Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence, James Houston, Tyrus Wheat, Von Miller, and Donovan Ezeiruaku. For the rest of the group, it’s Dee Winters, DeMarvion Overshown, Jaishawn Barham, and Shemar James for me. For the obvious absentee here, It feels like Marsit Liufau is not only caught behind other more natural pass rushers on the edge, but the fact Dallas has some intriguing safeties that can play as hybrid coverage linebackers, while Liufau is also a liability in coverage, does not help him at all. Give one name that you think will be a surprise player to make the 53-man roster. MIKE: The surprise name I’d go with is Phil Mafah. Carrying five players at running back sounds heavy, but it could make sense for Dallas because Mafah brings something different from the rest of the room. He has more of that downhill, physical runner profile, and when he has been given chances, he hasn’t looked out of place. With the RB2 spot still carrying a small question mark, keeping Mafah gives the Cowboys another option if they want more size, short-yardage ability, and insurance behind Javonte Williams. It may come down to numbers elsewhere on the roster, but if Dallas decides the run game needs depth and variety, Mafah is exactly the kind of surprise player who could sneak onto the 53. JESS : I can’t say this guy “will be” a surprise, but he could be. And that’s Marist Liufau. He provides versatile depth with his ILB experience and now learning at OLB. Not saying he’s great at either, but a strong special teamer who can be a body at two positions is not a crazy path to the roster. TOM : This one is hard, but could the Cowboys go deep at QB and keep Sam Howell on the 53? I think they might not want to put him at risk of being signed away. If he has a good game against the Saints, that could become a real concern. SEAN: I truly have no idea if this is a surprise or not, but my pick is safety Alijah…

We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Here’s it is, Day 17 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the defensive masterpiece that sent Dallas to a second consecutive Super Bowl. After playing nearly three quarters without scoring, the Cowboys forced one mistake after another and transformed a tense NFC Championship Game into a complete dismantling of the Los Angeles Rams. Sunday, January 7, 1979 — 5:00 p.m. ET Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, California Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 28, Los Angeles Rams 0 The matchup was steeped in history and filled with hostility. Both teams had finished 12-4, but Los Angeles held the home-field advantage and had defeated Dallas 27-14 at the Coliseum earlier that season. The Rams were determined to overcome years of postseason frustration, while the defending champion Cowboys sought their fifth Super Bowl appearance. The opening half was a defensive struggle, with Dallas unable to find a consistent rhythm against the Rams’ talented front. Meanwhile, Los Angeles squandered its best chances when Frank Corral missed two field goals. As a result, the teams entered halftime tied 0-0, leaving the conference championship undecided. The Doomsday Defense turned the tide of the game midway through the third quarter. Charlie Waters intercepted Pat Haden and returned the ball to the Los Angeles 10-yard line. Five plays later, Tony Dorsett scored on a five-yard run, giving Dallas the first points of the afternoon. After Jackie Wallace’s punt return gave them possession at the Dallas 23, the Rams immediately threatened to respond. Los Angeles reached fourth-and-short at the 14, but Randy White and Larry Bethea stopped Jim Jodat before he could score. This pivotal stand preserved the lead and denied the Rams their best scoring opportunity to that point. Waters struck again near the end of the third quarter, intercepting another Haden pass and returning it to the Rams’ 20-yard line. During the play, Haden injured his throwing hand on Randy White’s helmet and left with a broken thumb. Just 58 seconds into the fourth quarter, Roger Staubach found Scott Laidlaw for a four-yard touchdown, extending the lead to 14-0. Vince Ferragamo, the backup quarterback, briefly gave Los Angeles hope by connecting with Willie Miller for 65 yards to the Dallas 10. However, Cullen Bryant mishandled the handoff on the following play, and Harvey Martin recovered the fumble at the 11. The Rams had moved within sight of the end zone, only to leave without points once again. Dallas’s next drive sealed the game. Dorsett burst through for 53 yards on the first play, amassing 70 yards in the ensuing 89-yard possession. Staubach capitalized with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Billy Joe DuPree, securing a commanding 21-0 lead for the Cowboys. Thomas “Hollywood” Henderson supplied the final exclamation point. After spending the week openly questioning whether the Rams could handle the moment, Henderson intercepted Ferragamo and returned the ball 68 yards for a touchdown with 1:19 remaining. His score completed the shutout and turned his pregame talk into one of the defining stories of the game. This game belongs on the countdown because it demonstrated the ruthless postseason quality of Landry’s Cowboys. Dallas absorbed everything the Rams offered during a difficult first half, remained patient and then punished every mistake after halftime. What began as a close defensive contest ended as one of the most decisive conference-title victories in franchise history. #Cowboys vs #Rams 1979 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 28, Los Angeles Rams 0 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/n7AL2AG2q8 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 27, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Dallas wore its royal-blue jerseys, making this the franchise’s last playoff victory in a blue uniform until its Wild Card win at Tampa Bay following the 2022 season. title: 3 position battles to watch in the Cowboys preseason finale
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have to trim the roster from 90 to 53 players by this Sunday at 6 PM. It won’t be easy. The Cowboys have a lot of players on the bottom of the depth chart who could contribute for other teams either on the active roster or the practice squad. When Dallas plays […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Marist Liufau #35 of the Dallas Cowboys pass rushes during a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have to trim the roster from 90 to 53 players by this Sunday at 6 PM. It won’t be easy. The Cowboys have a lot of players on the bottom of the depth chart who could contribute for other teams either on the active roster or the practice squad. When Dallas plays on Friday against the New Orleans Saints, there will be high stakes. For who? Who are locked in for one last audition to prove they belong on the team or deserve actual reps, and who are those players up against on their team? Here are some key position battles to watch in tomorrow’s game. Marist Liufau vs. Sam Williams The Cowboys have a good mix of veteran and young talent to lead their pass rush group. Adding Rashan Gary and Von Miller, who has plenty left in the tank, provides the team with excellent experience. Along with them are Malachi Lawrence and Donovan Ezeiruaku, who have the talent to explode for double-digit sacks. The bottom of the pecking order is left to fight for a roster spot and reps, and that has created a heated battle with Marist Liufau and Sam Williams, who are clinging to a possible spot on the team. Sam Williams has put together a nice camp for himself and has shown up in the first two games. Williams recorded a sack against the Arizona Cardinals last week. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau hasn’t recorded a sack officially in the preseason, but he has been able to create some pressure with his speed off the edge, and contributes greatly on special teams. Williams doesn’t have the same versatility as Liufau to drop back in coverage or play inside if needed. Yet, Liufau doesn’t have the natural pass rush arsenal that Williams has since Liufau has recently moved to the position. Both players are competing with James Houston for a roster spot, who has also been consistent as a pass rusher. Look for Williams and Liufau to have extended snaps to show us who is the best man to earn a spot on the team. Malik Davis vs. Jaydon Blue for RB2 & Israel Abanikanda vs. Phil Mafah for the roster It was all good just a little while ago. When training camp started, it was Jaydon Blue who had the leg up on the primary job to back up Javonte Williams. In fact, Malik Davis was behind both second-year players Blue and Phil Mafah. Fast forward to the present, and Davis hasn’t gone away quietly and has pushed to earn the second running back spot outright. After the first preseason game, Malik Davis looked to have surpassed Blue, and then he showed more of the same with a good performance against the Cardinals. Blue answered back with multiple highlight plays showcasing his agility and speed. Blue led the team in rushing, with both runners playing to a proverbial stalemate last Saturday. That’s only one running back battle to check out this week. Let’s assume the Cowboys go heavy at running back and keep four along with Hunter Leupke; who would win the last spot? Phil Mafah or Israel Abanikanda? Phil Mafah had only one carry last week, but he made the most of it, avoiding a sure tackle for loss, changing direction, and racing past the Cardinals defense for a late score. Phil Mafah zooms in for a Cowboys TD 👏 DALvsAZ on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gUktkzSGVo — NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026 As for Abanikanda, he too has had a good training camp and has shown not only his speed in practices but the strength to keep the chains moving with his power and willingness to finish runs. Abanikanda and Mafah could split reps in the second half for a final push to make the team in the game’s dwindling moments. Joe Milton vs. Sam Howell Up to this point, Joe Milton should feel like he’s comfortably ahead in the race for QB2. Through two games, he has been stellar. He has completed 75% of his passes for 286 yards and three touchdowns for a passer rating of 142.8. He has made tremendous strides to improve his timing and touch on his throws. As of now, this is his job to lose. Milton can’t afford to regress against the Saints or allow doubt to creep back into the mind of the decision-makers. Howell played well in the preseason opener, posting stats almost identical to Milton. Joe Milton LAUNCHES it for a 53-yard TD pass to Jonathan Mingo 🚀 DALvsAZ on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3LgWRZrsii — NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026 With Milton ahead in the race, don’t be surprised if the team gives him a brief appearance for about a quarter and leaves Howell to finish the rest of the way. The offensive line also has a lot to prove as the team sorts out the offensive line rotation. Expect the best out of that group as well as receivers Jonathan Mingo and Anthony Smith, who need to deliver for Howell. Mingo and Smith also have an opportunity to make the team. Still, let’s be transparent: For Howell, he’s in the bottom of the ninth and needs a grand slam just to tie the game with Milton. He has to have a huge game this week.

title: Broncos vs. Vikings: 3 storylines to watch for in Week 3 of NFL preseason
summary: Tue Denver Broncos host the Minnesota tonight for their preseason finale. Coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers last week, the Broncos have a lot of issues to work out. Here are several storylines to watch this evening in Denver’s last gridiron battle before the regular season kicks off in a […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on in the second half of a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field At Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Clarkson Creative/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tue Denver Broncos host the Minnesota tonight for their preseason finale. Coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers last week, the Broncos have a lot of issues to work out. Here are several storylines to watch this evening in Denver’s last gridiron battle before the regular season kicks off in a few weeks against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football . Can the Broncos play disciplined and dial back the penalties? The Broncos have experienced an impressive turnaround with Head Coach Sean Payton leading the way. Despite incurring a historic amount of dead cap by moving on from Russell Wilson several seasons ago, Denver has assembled one of the best rosters in the NFL. Moreover, General Manager George Paton has done a tremendous job inking the team’s best players to long-term contracts that have aged well as the market continues to explode at premium positions. Coming off their first AFC title in a decade and 14-win season, the Broncos are in the best spot they have been in ages. However, they have one of the toughest schedules for the upcoming 2026 season. They face a gauntlet in the first half of the season—going head-to-head against a lot of playoff teams and potential Super Bowl contenders. It’ll be tough to win those games, especially if they continue their poor trend of drawing flags. Last season, the Broncos were the fourth-most flagged team in football. A lot of offensive drives were stalled due to them, and many drives for the opposition were extended due to consistent defensive holding, pass interference, or roughing the passer penalties. So far this preseason they have had 18 called against them. That’s a nine per game average which is absolutely alarming. This is a well-coached team, but the miscues and penalty issues that have plagued them for the past several seasons needs to be addressed. Payton was visibly upset with their lack of discipline after their loss to the Packers and mentioned it has to be rectified. That’s one of the major things I’m looking forward to seeing. Will the Broncos’ rushing attack bounce back? One of the reasons why the Broncos were able to trounce the Atlanta Falcons in the preseason opener was because of their ground game. They rushed for over 160 yards. By doing so, they set the pace of the game and controlled the clock. Against the Packers last week, they had less than half of that and barely averaged three yards per carry. That isn’t going to cut the mustard when it matters most. The Vikings have a well-coached defense led by Brian Flores who has a penchant for being aggressive and blitzing. Sometimes, that can backfire on them, and they were in the bottom half of the NFL last season with respect to run defense. I want to see Denver take advantage of that and have a strong rushing performance this evening. Having a solid ground attack will make a huge difference for the Broncos this season. Fans across Broncos Country saw what happened in the second half of the season without J.K. Dobbins. I’m hoping to see Denver deploy a formidable rushing attack against Minnesota and would like Dobbins, alongside RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman, to show what kind of trio they can be in the regular season. What players make the strongest case to make the final 53-man roster? Continuity was a major theme for the Broncos this offseason. Outside of trading for Jaylen Waddle and their 2026 NFL Draft class, Denver didn’t opt to bring in a lot of outside players to their roster. It’s a team loaded with quality starters and solid backups at most positions. Truth be told, there aren’t a lot of positions up for grabs. The preseason finale against the Vikings will be the last chance for fringe roster players to make a case to earn a spot on the roster. The spots I’m looking at the most are who impresses the most at safety. With Taylor Rapp in the fold alongside Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga, those three will be locks for the final roster. The last two spots, if Denver opts to keep five safeties like last season, will come down to Devon Key, Tycen Anderson, J.L. Skinner, and Miles Scott. Key, given his prowess as an All-Pro special team’s player seems likely. Whichever player flashes the most in their defensive reps, in my opinion, will be the one to make the squad. Outside of safety, the battle for two depth spots behind Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad looms large. Karene Reid has played well in both preseason games and seems like a good bet to make the squad. The last spot will come down to Red Murdock, Taurean York, and Jordan Turner. My gut tells me Murdock has the inside track for this one given the praise he has received from Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph throughout training camp. Last but not least, I’ll be keeping a close eye on the offensive trenches. The Broncos have been banged up at center and most all the reserve lineman struggled immensely last week against the Packers. While I’m confident in the team’s starters to play at a high level, finding the right combination of depth players behind them will be crucial. There have been far too many offensive line penalties and blown blocks the past two weeks. What about you, Broncos Country? What things are you keeping a close eye on in the preseason finale against the Vikings? Sound off in the comments section and let me know what you think.
