title: Denver Broncos 53-man roster projection: Hart’s prediction
summary: The Denver Broncos play their final preseason game this evening against the Minnesota Vikings. They have until Sunday, August 30th to finalize their 53-man roster. I usually don’t do predictions like this but thought I’d throw my hat in the ring alongside Scotty Payne and give my best guess on who makes the team. I’ll […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 14: A detail view of the Denver Broncos logo on September 14, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos play their final preseason game this evening against the Minnesota Vikings. They have until Sunday, August 30th to finalize their 53-man roster. I usually don’t do predictions like this but thought I’d throw my hat in the ring alongside Scotty Payne and give my best guess on who makes the team. I’ll forego guessing on who makes the team’s 16-man practice squad. Predicting the Broncos’ 2026 Offense: 24 Players Quarterbacks — (2) Bo Nix Jarrett Stidham Nix and Stidham are the only quarterbacks the Broncos need to carry on their roster. I don’t see the need to carry three. I’d just stash Sam Ehlinger on the practice squad. Running Backs — (4) JK Dobbins RJ Harvey Jonah Coleman Adam Prentice Dobbins, Harvey, and Coleman will be the Broncos’ trio of running backs this season. Adam Prentice, who has seen a lot of preseason action, will be the team’s fullback. Wide Receiver — (5) Courtland Sutton Jaylen Waddle Marvin Mims Jr. Troy Franklin Pat Bryant Sutton, Waddle, Mims Jr., Franklin, and Bryant make a deep five. I don’t think they need to carry more than this. However, it wouldn’t surprise me if Lil’Jordan Humphrey wound up making it six. He knows Payton’s offense but could very well just be a practice squad player who gets elevated. Tight End — (4) Adam Trautman Evan Engram Nate Adkins Justin Joly Trautman is the veteran ‘Y’ tight end and Engram is the Broncos’ ‘F’ or move tight end. Nate Adkins is a versatile player who can line up in a few positions, while Joly has the talent and abilities to eventually replace Engram in 2027. I think we will see Caleb Lohner and Dallen Bentley wind up on the practice squad. Offensive Line — (9) Garett Bolles Ben Powers Luke Wattenberg Quinn Meinerz Mike McGlinchey Alex Palczewski Kage Casey Alex Forsyth Frank Crum There isn’t a big difference here than last year. The exception being Kage Casey in the mix as a versatile backup, with Matt Peart losing his spot to Frank Crum. Though I’ll admit I think Peart has played better than Crum has during the preseason. Predicting the Broncos’ 2026 Defense: 26 Players Defensive Line — (6) Zach Allen D.J. Jones Malcolm Roach Eyioma Uwazurike Sai’vion Jones Tyler Onyedim This one was a hard projection. Quite frankly, I thought Jordan Jackson and Jordan Miller outperformed Jones and Onyedim in the preseason. That being said, I have a hard time envisioning the Broncos moving on from Jones, who was a third-round draft selection in the 2025 NFL Draft. However, this also means that Jones or Onyedim will be a game day inactive. Not necessarily ideal for third-round picks, but it is what it is. Edge Rusher — (5) Nik Bonitto Jonathon Cooper Jonah Elliss Dondrea Tillman Que Robinson The Broncos’ edge rusher room will remain as it was in 2025. The big variable is the future of Jonathon Cooper. At some point in time, he could receive a suspension from the NFL for his off the field violations of the league’s domestic violence policy. In the event Cooper would be served one prior to the regular season, perhaps the Broncos kick the tires on Haason Reddick. He is a veteran player who spent two years playing for Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph with the Arizona Cardinals. Inside Linebacker — (5) Alex Singleton Justin Strnad Karene Reid Red Murdock Waiver Wire Addition / Veteran Trade This position was sort of tough for me. Singleton and Strnad are the starters, while Reid and Murdock have shown enough in the preseason to beat out Jordan Turner and Taurean York. That being said, I honestly have some concerns with the depth. Does the Broncos’ coaching staff feel confident that Reid or Murdock can perform well enough if tasked to start? I don’t have the answer to that. Not many teams carry five inside linebackers, though feel that this may be a position Denver pursues a waiver wire addition or potential trade for an established veteran with more experience. I’d place a higher value on that as opposed to an additional receiver, running back, tight end, or other depth piece on the roster. Cornerback — (5) Patrick Surtain II Riley Moss Ja’Quan McMillian Jahdae Barron Kris Abrams-Draine I expect Denver’s group of cornerbacks to be the same as last year. There is no doubt in my mind Denver’s five cornerbacks are the best group in the NFL. Safety — (5) Brandon Jones Talanoa Hufanga Devon Key J.L. Skinner Waive Wire Addition Jones and Hufanga are the starters this season. After that? It’s anybody’s best guess. With Taylor Rapp being released the other day, the competition for the third spot on the depth chart is open. Key was an All-Pro special team’s player last season, and Skinner has been a critical piece of Denver’s coverage units the past two seasons. Maybe Denver’s coaching staff thinks one of them is poised to take a leap this year. Though I could see Denver hitting the waiver wire to add a fifth player. If not? I’d give Miles Scott the nod over Tycen Anderson. Predicting the Broncos’ 2026 Special Teams: 3 Players Will Lutz — Kicker Jeremy Crawshaw — Punter Mitchell Fabroni — Long Snapper No surprises here, these are Denver’s trio of special teamers for the 2026 season. Final Thoughts: Honestly, I don’t think we will see too many curveballs here. Most of the roster’s key starters and depth spots have already been established. There are only a few position groups with true battles up for grabs. All things considered, I do think an outside addition is likely. There are a few areas of the team where I wouldn’t be surprised if a better player becomes availabel than what is currently on the roster.

title: The Broncos offensive line has become a model of continuity
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! One of the popular phrases in the world of football and sports is continuity. No matter the level of play, this is the rare gem every unit and team craves to unearth. In professional sports, that’s made even more difficult with free agency. It’s difficult to keep players, and thus even […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - AUGUST 7: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos fist bumps offensive tackle Garett Bolles (72) during practice on Friday, August. 7, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colo.(Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! One of the popular phrases in the world of football and sports is continuity. No matter the level of play, this is the rare gem every unit and team craves to unearth. In professional sports, that’s made even more difficult with free agency. It’s difficult to keep players, and thus even tougher to maintain continuity. The Denver Broncos are one of the rare exceptions, and that speaks to the culture that head coach Sean Payton has developed in his three years in Denver. It doesn’t hurt to have one of the best ownership groups in the NFL and a general manager in George Paton, who has a great rapport with Payton and the franchise. Just look at the lack of turnover from the team that was just in the AFC Championship Game. The Broncos lost one starter on defense, kept the offense intact, and added Jaylen Waddle in the process. But the unit that highlights continuity is Denver’s offensive line. As offensive coordinator Davis Webb said to the media earlier this week: “I’ve never been around somewhere that’s been about to be four straight years of basically the same offensive line. It’s such a blessing because they’re good dudes, they’re coached well, they’re nasty, they take things personal. I think pass block-wise, they’ve been pretty consistent over the last few years, and run-game-wise, I think we’re trying to build on that consistency. “Not saying it’s been bad, but we can definitely be more consistent. That’s a goal that we’ve tried to address this offseason. We’re just very blessed in all of our rooms that the offensive line’s been the most stationary. They’re the strength of our offense.” As the Broncos look to take the next step this season, continuity along the offensive line and within the team will play a massive role in making that happen. title: Best Lions content of the week: Goff, St. Brown discuss their telepathy
summary: The connection between a quarterback and wide receiver is one of the more storied partnerships in all of sports, and for good reason. full_text: The connection between a quarterback and wide receiver is one of the more storied partnerships in all of sports, and for good reason. So many details go into the artistry that occurs between the two positions on gameday. And if you are looking for proof, just ask one of the best duos in NFL—Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. “When you watch Goff and St. Brown on the field, you can see they’re finishing each other’s sentences — if every sentence was punctuated with a first down,” wrote Henry McKenna of Fox Sports in his recent feature on the pair. “It’s not normal. They can make changes mid-play without even having to look at each other. It goes beyond coaching.” If you have been watching the Lions for the last several years, then chances are you know exactly what McKenna is talking about. “I think we’ve been playing for so long together that he understands my body language when I’m running routes,” St. Brown told McKenna. “That he can anticipate throws before I’m even out of the break. He kind of knows, ‘Oh, that’s how it looks when he’s about to break down.’ So he already knows. He can anticipate the throw.” The article dives into what makes the relationship between the two pros so special, including frequent visits to St. Brown’s favorite sushi restaurant near their Los Angeles area offseason homes. You can read the entire article from McKenna right here . And now onto the rest of the best Lions content from this week. If you didn’t already see, Chris Long and The Greenlight Podcast were in Allen Park recently, and they got some excellent interviews in with St. Brown, Goff, and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. title: What will you be looking for in the Lions’ preseason finale against the Colts?
summary: Just like that, Detroit Lions training camp is officially complete. After about four weeks of practices, the last hurdles standing between the team and the regular season are the final preseason season game against the Indianapolis Colts on Saturday, and cut-down day on Sunday where coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes will be […]
full_text: Just like that, Detroit Lions training camp is officially complete. After about four weeks of practices, the last hurdles standing between the team and the regular season are the final preseason season game against the Indianapolis Colts on Saturday, and cut-down day on Sunday where coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes will be faced with some difficult decisions in regards to who is going to make the final roster. And while we can expect the majority of the Lions’ starters to be in street clothes for the preseason finale in Indiana, there are still several hotly-contested competitions taking place, starting at the quarterback position. Can rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer do enough to unseat the battle-tested veteran Josh Dobbs? Staying on the offensive side of the ball, there are still things to sort out concerning the running back and wide receiver positions, too. Defensively, there are potentially even more tough decisions to make. Along the defensive line, there is a bit of a logjam at defensive tackle between the likes of Skyler Gill-Howard, Chris Smith, and Mekhi Wingo. Moving into the secondary and there may be even more questions than the defensive line. That brings us to today’s question of the day: What will you be watching for in the Lions’ final preseason game against the Colts? My answer: As usual, my eyes will be fixed on the trenches. On the offensive line, who gets the most work at center? Will Juice Scruggs see any reps, or will he also be in street clothes? If he isn’t dressed, will Seth McLaughlin see the majority of the opportunities? On the other side of the ball, will the last preseason game help the coaching staff figure out which direction they want to go in as far as the active roster is concerned? What about you? What will you be watching for in Saturday’s game against the Colts? Join our community and share your answer in the comment section. Join the conversation! title: Detroit Lions backup quarterback race highlights preseason finale
summary: The Detroit Lions enter their final preseason game with likely most of their roster spots decided, but one that may still be up in the air is the backup quarterback job. Entering training camp, there likely wasn’t going to be much drama at the position. However, Teddy Bridgewater’s abrupt retirement midway through camp forced the […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16), and center Cade Mays (64), left, practice next to offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (70), and quarterback Luke Altmyer (2) during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions enter their final preseason game with likely most of their roster spots decided, but one that may still be up in the air is the backup quarterback job. Entering training camp, there likely wasn’t going to be much drama at the position. However, Teddy Bridgewater’s abrupt retirement midway through camp forced the Lions to pivot. While undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer has been with the team all offseason, suddenly thrusting a 23-year-old into the backup position wasn’t something the Lions were willing to do unopposed. So they quickly added nine-year veteran Josh Dobbs to the room. But thus far in camp, Altmyer has continued to get the bulk of the backup reps. And what seemed like a far-fetched approach—letting Altmyer be the backup to veteran Jared Goff—now seems closer to reality than ever. On Thursday, Lions coach Dan Campbell asked what he needs to see from Altmyer to have the confidence that he can handle such a critical role. “Consistency. Just play good smart football,” Campbell said. “We don’t need some wild throws, whatever. Be able to run the offense, be efficient, make smart decisions, even if that means that you’re punting the ball. That’ll be the most important thing. We don’t want the wild plays and then there’s an ill-advised throw across the middle for an intercept—those won’t get it done. So just be smart, take what’s there, run the offense and that’ll go a long way.” It hardly seems like a coincidence that Campbell would bring up the example of an ill-advised pass over the middle that was intercepted. That could be fresh in his mind because Altmyer’s competition, Josh Dobbs, did exactly that in the team’s second preseason game last week . But under Dan Campbell, the Lions have seemingly preferred to have a veteran set of eyes behind Goff. Be it Bridgewater, David Blough, or Kyle Allen, the Lions almost always wanted a seasoned player among the quarterback reserves, with the lone exception being 2024 (Hendon Hooker, Jake Fromm). Campbell admitted they prefer to have experienced players at quarterback, but that won’t trump overall talent when it comes to cut-down day. “I mean, you would like that because those guys have played, there are real reps. They’ve been under real fire in real football games and that is important. But that’s not the end all be all, either,” Campbell said. “If you think there’s somebody to work with here and that he’s shown enough progress and he’s only going to get better, then we don’t close our eyes to that either.” Further complicating the Lions’ decision is the amount of roster gymnastics they could try to perform to keep both players around. Because Dobbs is a veteran, the Lions could opt to cut him, not subject him to waivers, and bring him back later either on the practice squad or 53-man roster. But at the same time, how likely is it that Altmyer would get claimed on waivers if Detroit opted to cut him? Last year, there were only 27 total waiver claims after initial NFL roster cuts , and just one of them (Tommy Devito) was a quarterback. So the Lions could keep Dobbs on the roster, and bring back Altmyer assuming he clears waivers. Regardless, the Lions won’t make that decision until after Saturday’s preseason finale against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s unclear how the Lions will share the load between Altmyer and Dobbs on gameday, but their performance could be the tipping point for a difficult decision.

title: Dan Campbell delivers an awesome message to high school football players
summary: Thursday night, high school football teams around the state kicked off their 2026 season. For some kids, it’s the last “opening week” of football they’ll ever play at an organized level. Several hours before football kicked off in the state of Michigan, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell delivered an awesome message to the high school […]
full_text: Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell addresses the media prior to Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Thursday night, high school football teams around the state kicked off their 2026 season. For some kids, it’s the last “opening week” of football they’ll ever play at an organized level. Several hours before football kicked off in the state of Michigan, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell delivered an awesome message to the high school kids out there ready to strap their helmets on. “Make the most of it,” Campbell said. “Because you’re not guaranteed to be able to get another chance to play and be with those guys that you grew up with and enjoy the game at that level and the wins and the sacrifice and the hard work and the blood and the sweat and the tears, It’s a special time, enjoy it.” Campbell is obviously one of the lucky ones to make a career out of football, both as a player and a coach. But despite playing for 10 seasons, participating in a Super Bowl, coaching for nearly another two decades, and being a part of endless classic NFL games, he still remembers both the sting and the wonder of his last game in high school—a loss, as he’s quick to point out. “We lost, and it wasn’t good. Yeah, we weren’t going to the playoffs, I remember that,” Campbell said. “But I remember being with that group of guys that I knew and I grew up with and I was with for a long time. And it is, you don’t forget those, you just don’t. You just don’t forget and it is a special time. And you’re going to look back and wish, ‘Man, I wish I could do that one more time. I wish I could go back and play that game one more time or play with those guys one more time.’” While Campbell pleaded to high school seniors appreciate the moment and give it all you’ve got so you don’t have any regrets, he also had a message for the underclassmen. “If you’re a young guy, man, I’m a freshman, I’m a sophomore, you owe it to the seniors because this may be the last time that—you get one more shot, they don’t,” Campbell said. “So, give them everything you have got and make it a special year for them because next year is your year and you’re going to want those young guys to help you. So, man, enjoy it. It doesn’t last and you’ll remember it the rest of your life.” It’s one thing to read Campbell’s words. It’s another to experience them. So do yourself a favor and watch his answer to the question below, and share it with any high school football player you know. "Make the most of it" – Coach Campbell on high school football season starting pic.twitter.com/7pZYz1VYXf — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 27, 2026

title: Detroit Lions training camp injury news: Very shorthanded at center
summary: The Detroit Lions have had some bad luck at center, and that may continue moving forward. It started when Cade Mays suffered a fractured wrist and backup Juice Scruggs missed time with his own injury. Scruggs is thankfully back and set to be the starter. But, now, with training camp concluded on Thursday, the Lions […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Luke Altmyer (2) lines up behind center Seth McLaughlin (65) in the second quarter against the Washington Commanders at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions have had some bad luck at center, and that may continue moving forward. It started when Cade Mays suffered a fractured wrist and backup Juice Scruggs missed time with his own injury. Scruggs is thankfully back and set to be the starter. But, now, with training camp concluded on Thursday, the Lions are dealing with more center issues. Let’s get into it in our daily training camp injury report. Returned to practice: OL Miles Frazier (undisclosed) EDGE Ahmed Hassanein (unknown) Frazier technically returned to practice on Wednesday, but he was limited to individual drills. On Thursday, he was with the second-team offense, serving as the right guard. While that has normally been Mason Miller’s job, Miller had to play as the second-team center due to Seth McLaughlin’s absence (more on that in a bit). Despite Dan Campbell saying that Hassanein was going to sit out another practice, he was participating on Thursday and even got some team action during the scrimmage. Not practicing: RB Isiah Pacheco (knee) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) C Cade Mays (wrist) C Seth McLaughlin (unknown) G Michael Niese (leg) EDGE Payton Turner (back) — placed on IR after practice EDGE Derrick Moore (unknown) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) LB Trevor Nowaske (leg) S Thomas Harper (ankle) S Christian Izien (undisclosed) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) McLaughlin was missing from practice, leaving the Lions extremely shorthanded at center. Detroit came into camp with Cade Mays, Scruggs, McLaughlin, and Michael Niese as their four centers, in that order. Now Mays, McLaughlin, and Niese are sidelined. At this point, we don’t have any idea if McLaughlin’s absence is injury-related, but this could leave the Lions in a tight spot for Saturday’s preseason finale. They likely don’t want to play Scruggs, as he’s projected to start in Week 1. But they may only have one healthy center on the roster: Gus Hartwig, who was signed earlier this week. That said, maybe they just roll with Mason Miller at center with the starters, and Hartwig the rest of the way. Though, it’s worth noting Miller and quarterback Luke Altmyer had several botched snaps during Thursday’s practice, and Miller did not play a lick of center in college. On Thursday evening, the Lions placed Payton Turner on injured reserve . Either his season is over, or the Lions will release him with an injury settlement. Regardless, it’s a disappointing end for Turner, who just can’t seem to shake the injury bug. Campbell provided an update on Moore prior to practice, noting that the rookie defensive end will miss a little time, but they hope to get him back sometime next week before the start of the season. Injured during practice S Avonte Maddox (unknown) We didn’t get an update from the team after practice, but on the very last play of practice, Maddox went down and was tended to by trainers. They appeared to be working on his upper body, and he walked to the locker room with trainers when practice had officially concluded. We’ll see if Campbell offers an update after the final preseason game. Otherwise, we may not hear for a while. Hopefully, given Detroit’s numerous injuries at safety, it’s nothing.

title: Detroit Lions sign CB, place EDGE on IR
summary: The Detroit Lions are holding their final training camp practice of the 2026 offseason on Thursday, but that doesn’t mean the front office is done trying to find solutions for the roster. The Lions still have one preseason game remaining, and with a few injuries in the secondary, they’ve signed corner Eric Scott Jr. to […]
full_text: Jul 22, 2025; St. Joseph, MO, USA; Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Eric Scott Jr. (45) walks down the hill to the practice fields during training camp at Missouri Western State University. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions are holding their final training camp practice of the 2026 offseason on Thursday, but that doesn’t mean the front office is done trying to find solutions for the roster. The Lions still have one preseason game remaining, and with a few injuries in the secondary, they’ve signed corner Eric Scott Jr. to their 90-man roster. To make room for Scott, they have placed veteran defensive end Payton Turner on injured reserve. Scott started his college career at Illinois State and worked his way up through Butler Community College to Southern Mississippi. He started the next two and a half seasons for the Golden Eagles and was selected by the Dallas Cowboys, who traded up into the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft to secure him. He made the roster as a rookie, but didn’t see the field as he was declared inactive each game. In 2024, the Cowboys waived Scott near the end of training camp, and the Kansas City Chiefs claimed him off waivers (ironically, the team the Cowboys traded with to draft Scott). Scott ended up on the Chiefs’ practice squad that season; then, the following training camp, he suffered an injury that forced him to injured reserve and cost him the 2025 season. Ahead of the Lions’ final training camp practice, coach Dan Campbell noted that he’s not sure if he’ll play his starters in the final preseason game (it’d be surprising if he did), and with a couple of injuries in the secondary—most notably Nick Whiteside at corner—adding a player like Scott could give the Lions the depth they need to close out the preseason. While the road to a spot on the roster is steep for Scott, there’s a chance for him to get some extended playing time and put some things on tape for the Lions and 31 other NFL teams. If he shows well, a spot on a team’s practice squad could be in his future. As for Turner, his season will be over, unless the Lions opt to release him with an injury settlement. The oft-injured defensive end practiced just once before being sidelined for the entirety of camp with a back injury.

title: Packers fans should be watching Pierre Strong in the preseason finale
summary: Pierre Strong was drafted by the New England Patriots in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL draft after an incredible final season at South Dakota State, when he carried the football 240 times for 1686 yards and 18 touchdowns. In his draft guide, The Beast, Dane Brugler had him as a likely fifth rounder […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: Que Robinson #51 of the Denver Broncos tackles Pierre Strong Jr. #22 of the Green Bay Packers during a preseason game at Empower Field At Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Clarkson Creative/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pierre Strong was drafted by the New England Patriots in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL draft after an incredible final season at South Dakota State, when he carried the football 240 times for 1686 yards and 18 touchdowns. In his draft guide, The Beast , Dane Brugler had him as a likely fifth rounder praising his vision and speed , though Brugler emphasized his lack of size and an issue with fumbling (partially due to small-ish hands). Strong was traded to the Browns after his first season, and his his workload slightly increased from 10 carries as a rookie to 63. During his Cleveland stint, Strong mostly served as a passing downs specialist while averaging a respectable 4.5 yards per carry and 8 yards per reception, and there’s definitely some big play ability and elite agility in his repertoire. This was on display in last week’s preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and Denver Broncos; while wearing green and gold, Strong averaged 4.6 yards per carry on eight carries and ripped off a 68-yard kickoff return. I actually like Strong better than Marshawn Lloyd as both represent the potential “lightning” to Josh Jacobs’ thunder, and while Lloyd is quite a bit larger, Strong is the better athlete, and despite his small size, he’s been more durable. The Josh Jacobs problem Matt LaFleur may be a very successful offensive football coach, but I still think he runs the ball too much. I don’t mind running the ball, and in 2024 when Josh Jacobs was ripping off 4.4 yards per carry and scoring 15 touchdowns, it was mostly fine. Unfortunately, since that time the Packers’ offensive line has declined as a run-blocking unit, and it’s possible that seven years of physical punishment has started to wear on Jacobs. And now, with Jacobs charged with assault and a pretty nasty video tape of the incident allegedly out there, there is an opportunity for the team to move on from Jacobs before he falls off a cliff (and also to get an alleged abuser off the team). Back in 2022 Josh Jacobs led the league in rushing yards with 1653 , and was also elite in exceeding his expected rushing total. The NFL’s NextGenStats page has a series of metrics which tracks how many more yards a back gains than expected based on the blocking on the play, the quality of the opponent, and several other factors. (This advanced metric was born out of the NFL’s Big Data Bowl contest in 2020 ) Jacobs gained 0.47 yards over expected per attempt that year, which ranked 11 th among qualifiers. That may not sound overly impressive, but maintaining that level of production of his robust total of 340 carries is impressive. Of the ten backs that ranked higher, only Cleveland’s Nick Chubb was even in the ballpark with 302 carries. Jacobs plummeted the following year due to injuries that caused him to miss four games, but he rebounded nicely in 2024 in his inaugural Packer season with 0.73 yards over expected per attempt, which tied him in tenth with teammate Emanuel Wilson . In 2025 Jacobs also suffered some injuries, and once again fell to -0.03 yards over expected . It’s possible that this is just a matter of health, and that after an offseason of rest and recovery he would be back to his old self again. But, running back is a young man’s game, Jacobs is expensive for a running back, and Jacobs turned 28 in February. He also uses a punishing running style and he has exceeded 200 carries in every season of his career (and 300 twice). He is not a great bet to age gracefully, and weird, bad offseasons don’t help. Committee Time While I’m not a huge fan of Marshawn Lloyd, a committee of Strong, Lloyd, and Chris Brooks would probably be fine. Brooks is an outstanding blocking back and a good enough receiver. He’s very useful and he’s capable of rattling off 5 yards a carry against light boxes while keeping your QB upright. I love Chris Brooks as a player, just not at 200 carries. In the unlikely event the Packers did move on from Jacobs, I could see the case for bringing in another power back, but even if they didn’t, they could probably get by with Lloyd/Strong/Brooks just fine, and with one additional hidden benefit. Matt LaFleur would be somewhat likely to run less without a proven workhorse, and so the number of passes the team throws would likely increase. Given that Jacobs isn’t what he once was anyway, this could actually provide a massive benefit to the team. Jacobs is one of Matt’s favorite toys, but it’s not working so well anymore. The remaining running backs have enough combined skills to make up for most of what Jacobs does at this point in his career. I don’t think they will move on, but if there really is a video out there , they’re playing with fire for no good reason. Use tonight’s game to check out the backups.
author: Paul Noonan

title: Packers Film Room, Preseason Week 2: Emptying the Notebook on the Offense
summary: During the season, I tend to dig into either specific plays or look at some of the bigger picture takeaways. Scheme and gameplan and blah blah blah. The preseason is different because those things don’t really matter. I’m more concerned with how individual players looked. So I watch a ton of players, taking notes and […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 21: Green Bay Packers tight end Drake Dabney (49) runs after a catch in the first quarter during a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images During the season, I tend to dig into either specific plays or look at some of the bigger picture takeaways. Scheme and gameplan and blah blah blah. The preseason is different because those things don’t really matter. I’m more concerned with how individual players looked. So I watch a ton of players, taking notes and gathering clips, then look up and realize I don’t have time to write about them all. What a fool I’ve been! The week is almost over! This week I got a chance to write about Jordan Love and Trey Smack , but then it all went south on me. So, today, we’re just doing a bit of a data dump. I’ll write about some of the players I watched on offense, throw out some notes and clips and we’ll all move on with our days. Let’s go. Offense Isaiah Neyor (80) Week 1 saw Neyor as a possession receiver. A lot of stuff close to the line. He has speed (ran a 4.4 40 at the Combine), but we didn’t get a chance to see him open it up last week. He had a few snaps running deep this week. I’ll say that it didn’t look quite as explosive as Sturdivant, but his speed was on display more than we saw in week 1. He shows a solid ability to stack the corner when he gets over the top, as well. One issue I had in Week 1 was Neyor’s blocking. He showed both a willingness to block and an understanding of where to be, but every single block attempt involved him wrapping his arms around his target. We saw some better form in that regard this week. In the shorter area, he shows some really nice snap at the top of his routes to create separation. Week 1 saw him working primarily outside. This week saw him in the slot a bit more, and he looked good when put there. If he’s able to improve his blocking form, working as a blocker out of the slot could be a nice spot for him. We didn’t necessarily get a ton of flashes this week, but he continues to show a well-rounded skillset. J. Michael Sturdivant (87) Unlike Neyor, we pretty much only got go routes from Sturdivant in Week 1. His explosion/speed was on full display, but we didn’t see much more than that. This week we got a little more, with Sturdivant showing good, sharp breaks at the top of his shorter routes. This is something that could really serve him well with more room to work: threaten with his speed, then break off a route. In this next clip, you can see him attacking the outside shoulder of the defender before snapping back inside. Unfortunately, this is the play he was injured on, so there were limited snaps for Sturdivant this week. We did get to see a bit of blocking, and the process looked much better than we had previously seen. In Week 1, he was tentative and didn’t always seem to know where he was supposed to be as the play unfolded. This week he attacked the blocking much better. Drake Dabney (49) I thought Dabney looked much more comfortable this week. Locked down some of his blocking assignments, and was at the very least a general nuisance when he wasn’t locking up. He knew where to be and wasn’t shy about engaging. Has a little movement as a receiver as well. Not necessarily a field-stretching type of guy, but there might be a little more here than I had previously thought. McCallan Castles (47) Looked a lot like Dabney in terms of his approach, but didn’t work quite as well as a receiver. Of the two, I’d certainly prefer Dabney at this point, but Castles showed some nice things as a blocker. Jager Burton (52) I didn’t get a chance to highlight Burton on all of these clips. Apologies. If you’ve seen one clip of Burton this week, it’s this one. And it’s a good one. He’s working as left guard, going against Zach Allen. Burton has good drive off the line, controls the rep and ends up burying Allen. Tremendous rep. I’m also a sucker for a young guy who is always looking for work. As the rep goes on Burton doesn’t have anyone to block, so he puts a shoulder into #96. You can also see his strength as he drives as part of a double team. He keeps driving through the whistle, which is always something I like to see. Unfortunately, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows. We saw him win against Zach Allen earlier. Here, he very much does not do that. Allen gets into Burton’s body and easily sheds the block attempt to hit Lloyd. Down in the low red zone, he fires off and gets out over his skis quickly, allowing #98 to control the rep and easily shed the block. Burton has showed some really nice stuff that makes me believe he will be a good player, but it doesn’t seem like he’s ready just yet. There are too many reps of him getting overpowered or controlled through the entire rep. Other times it seems like he’s fine, but the defensive lineman is just holding him in place until he needs to shed. Burton also got beat multiple times by an inside swim move. His recovery move was to turn and lunge with his arms wide, which feels like offensive holding waiting to happen. title: Tyrod Taylor vs. Kyle McCord: The Case Against Each Packers QB
summary: A few days ago, I tried with all my might to make the case for why each of Tyrod Taylor and Kyle McCord are worthy of being the Green Bay Packers QB2. Dear reader, there was a reason that article was like 300 words long. With one preseason game left for the Packers, the team […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Tyrod Taylor #6 of the Green Bay Packers throws a pass during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images A few days ago, I tried with all my might to make the case for why each of Tyrod Taylor and Kyle McCord are worthy of being the Green Bay Packers QB2. Dear reader, there was a reason that article was like 300 words long. With one preseason game left for the Packers, the team will soon have to decide who they want stepping in if they find themselves without Jordan Love. Here’s what’s wrong with both of their candidates. The Case Against Tyrod Taylor A career journeyman, Taylor has spent time with 8 different teams since being drafted in 2011. The experience is there, but the ride has been bumpy. Taylor has started 63 career games, but has just one playoff start to show for it, way back in 2017 with the Buffalo Bills. AKA: When Tyrod is your long-term starter, your season is probably lost. To be fair—this can be said about most backup quarterbacks, and some starters! There’s a reason Taylor has lasted 15 years in the NFL. He’s been pretty serviceable, and has been somewhat of a dual threat with his legs over the years. The problem is, I’m worried he doesn’t have it in him anymore. Through two preseason games, the 37-year-old has completed 8 of 16 passes for 38 yards and 1 TD, and has rushed 3 times for 11 yards. Yes, this is preseason, and head coach Matt LaFleur isn’t pulling all of his regular season tricks out of the bag just yet, but I’m having a hard time envisioning a potential Taylor start going as well as what we saw with Malik Willis. The Case Against Kyle McCord And then we have…the baby! Kyle McCord has seen zero regular season action as an NFL player since being drafted in 2025 by the Philadelphia Eagles. So, we don’t exactly know what we’re working with, outside of what we’ve seen this preseason. Through two games, McCord has 24 completions on 35 attempts for 220 yards. He’s not considered much of a threat on his legs, which is a stark shift from one of the things that made Malik Willis so fun for Matt LaFleur in Green Bay. Now, I’m not here to judge a quarterback by his lack of explosiveness in the run game, but I can’t really judge Kyle McCord by much, can I? Therein lies the problem. The Verdict Personally, I think McCord gets cut, simply due to inexperience. There’s something there that should keep him on the practice squad, unless something uncouth happens during Friday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals. I think the Packers are looking for a guy who can lead a locker room if needed, and we’ve seen that Tyrod Taylor can at least do that. One thing is for sure: the Packers backup in 2026 is going to be either a guy who was drafted 180th overall 15 years ago, or a guy who was drafted 181st overall 1 year ago. Buckle up. The team’s final preseason game is at home against Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals on Friday at 7 PM local time.

full_text: The opportunities to impress this coaching staff have dwindled with one preseason game left before the 53-man roster cutdowns. Friday’s game against the Carolina Panthers represents the final opportunity for players to put compelling tape together and earn a spot on this roster. Given the number of injuries this training camp, there are more roster spots available than anticipated. Notably, the fourth defensive end, third and fourth running back, fifth and sixth receiver, and multiple linebacker spots are up for grabs. Below, you’ll find the eight players who are on the outside looking in of the roster who can secure their spot with a good performance. He’s looked stout against inside runs and play actions, but has struggled against outside zone where he loses contain. A big performance against the Panthers can seal a roster spot for him. British Brooks, FB/RB The veteran fullback has out with an injured wrist all training camp. The offense has fully adapted without his presence and TE Cade Stover has assumed the role. He must demonstrate him impact on the entire offense by proving the run game is incrementally better with him than without. Fans have been dying to see the 17-pound weight loss’ affect on British Brooks’ mobility and power. Anther special teams ace who provides versatility to the offense. Jared Wayne, WR Wayne watched as Nick Caserio did his thing and added three wide receivers to the room. He was a rising star this offseason, making plays in training camp and rising up the depth chart. However, Caserio wouldn’t of added veterans Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones if he had the utmost confidence in Wayne. It’s unclear where Wayne ranks on the depth chart now and he needs to win on the field and through his knowledge of the offense. Alijah Huzzie, CB Huzzie is in contention for the final defensive back spot alongside injured Collin Wright and veteran Tremon Smith. Huzzie has been competing for reps throughout camp and has played significant snaps in the preseason. He is a smaller corner who plays primarily in the slot, but doesn’t have the safety versatility to completely match Pitre’s role. title: Anthony Richardson included in latest quarterback trade rumors
summary: Anthony Richardson’s future with the Indianapolis Colts continues to feel uncertain. Benjamin Allbright reported Wednesday that multiple quarterbacks could be on the move in the next few weeks, listing Tua Tagovailoa, Dillon Gabriel, J.J. McCarthy and Richardson as names who have had calls placed on them to “varying degrees of interest.” That does not mean […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - AUGUST 22: Anthony Richardson Sr. #5 of the Indianapolis Colts looks to pass during the preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons at Lucas Oil Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Anthony Richardson’s future with the Indianapolis Colts continues to feel uncertain. Could see multiple QBs on the move in the next few weeks. -Tua -Gabriel -McCarthy -Richardson All have had calls placed on them to varying degrees of interest. — Benjamin Allbright (@AllbrightNFL) August 27, 2026 Benjamin Allbright reported Wednesday that multiple quarterbacks could be on the move in the next few weeks, listing Tua Tagovailoa, Dillon Gabriel, J.J. McCarthy and Richardson as names who have had calls placed on them to “varying degrees of interest.” That does not mean Richardson is definitely being traded, and it does not even necessarily mean the Colts are actively shopping him. There is a big difference between teams calling about a player and a team being ready to move him. Still, Richardson’s inclusion is notable because of where things stand in Indianapolis. The Colts have already made their quarterback situation clear at the top. Daniel Jones is the starter, and Richardson is competing with rookie Riley Leonard for the backup job. Indianapolis has publicly backed Richardson throughout the offseason and training camp, and the team has said it plans to keep three quarterbacks. On the surface, that would suggest Richardson is not going anywhere. The problem is that the NFL can change quickly, especially at quarterback. Richardson remains one of the most interesting backup quarterbacks in the league because of his age, draft pedigree and physical tools. He was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, and even after a frustrating start to his career, there will always be teams willing to talk themselves into the upside. Quarterbacks with his size, arm strength and athletic ability do not become available often, even when the production or play have not matched the traits. For the Colts, the decision would come down to value. Moving Richardson just to move him would make little sense, especially if the return is minimal. He still gives Indianapolis a high-upside backup behind Jones, and with Leonard also on the roster, the Colts have more quarterback depth than most teams. Trading Richardson would only be logical if another team made an offer strong enough to justify giving up on the remaining upside. For now, this is more smoke than fire. Calls being placed does not guarantee movement, and the Colts do not have to force anything. However, Richardson’s name appearing in quarterback trade chatter is another reminder of how quickly his situation has changed. Two years ago, he was supposed to be the future of the franchise. Now, teams are at least checking to see if Indianapolis would consider moving him.

full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - DECEMBER 28: Rigoberto Sanchez #8 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday, the Indianapolis Colts announced that they have re-signed longtime punter Rigoberto Sanchez to a contract extension that will currently make him one of the top five highest paid punters in the NFL: Two-year extension for #Colts P Rigoberto Sanchez that makes him a top-5 paid punter at age 32. https://t.co/LH5DjvMr6U — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 27, 2026 Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, it’s confirmed to be a 2-year contract extension, which will keep the otherwise pending free agent punter, in Indianapolis through the 2028 campaign. Originally signed by the Colts as an undrafted rookie in 2017 out of Hawaii, the 9-year veteran has become one the league’s better punters, if not arguably among the best players at his position. While Sanchez may not have quite the booming leg of some of elite punting peers, he makes up for it with his elite accuracy and ball placement off his leg, as 50% of his punts were pinned with the 20-yard line last season (which was a career high). His punting skill-set plays really well with half his games inside a roof under Lucas Oil Stadium, where he can play the home turf to his punting advantage. Last season, he had 44 punts for the Colts, averaging 48.8 yards per punt (*8th most in the NFL in 2025), as well as handled a few kickoffs (9) in relief for Indianapolis’ special teams units. Per PFF, he was their 9th best graded punter with a +76.7 overall grade. Even though Sanchez surprisingly hasn’t made a Pro Bowl yet, it’s good to see that the Colts will be keeping one of their longstanding special teams standouts in Indianapolis for at least three more seasons.

Jacobs then allegedly took her phone from her while she was on the ground. The woman lay on the ground for a while and then struggled to walk back into the house. A responding officer reported that he observed redness on the woman’s face and neck and felt the bump on the back of her head. She also said her second phone, which she had grabbed inside, was damaged in the incident. Investigator Dan Van Lanen of the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department said in the report that content from a video surveillance system inside Jacobs’ garage corroborates the altercation the woman described. Kubiak mum on Raiders starter as Fernando Mendoza struggles | ESPN “I still don’t think we need to name anybody,” Kubiak said after Las Vegas’ 18-12 loss at Allegiant Stadium. “We have a lot to talk about at a lot of positions, so we want to watch the film and talk about everything as a staff.” While Kubiak continues to keep his decision close to the vest, his utilization of each quarterback once again hinted at Cousins being the team’s starter for the Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins on Sept. 13. Seahawks, DT Leonard Williams agree to three-year, $90 million extension | NFL.com Seattle Seahawks defensive tackle Leonard Williams has agreed to a three-year, $90 million extension, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported on Thursday, per sources. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the deal includes $56 million guaranteed. The team has since officially announced extending Williams. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride 4) Turnover Differential It might have felt as though the Chiefs were committing turnovers left and right, but that wasn’t the case. The offense just found a way to commit the most back-breaking turnovers possible. Kansas City was actually tied for seventh in the NFL last year while Mahomes was healthy for fewest offensive turnovers in the league (13). Unfortunately, the defense forced just 11 turnovers over that same stretch. Only the New York Jets, Washington Commanders and New York Giants forced fewer turnovers through week 15. title: Chiefs-Seahawks: 5 things to watch in the preseason finale
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will take on the Seattle Seahawks Friday night at Arrowhead Stadium to end the preseason and send both teams into Week 1. The game will kick off at 7:00 P.M. Arrowhead time and be broadcast on KSHB 41 for local viewers. The Chiefs lost their second preseason game 16-15 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Quarterback Garrett Nussmeier #14 of the Kansas City Chiefs passes during the preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will take on the Seattle Seahawks Friday night at Arrowhead Stadium to end the preseason and send both teams into Week 1. The game will kick off at 7:00 P.M. Arrowhead time and be broadcast on KSHB 41 for local viewers. The Chiefs lost their second preseason game 16-15 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , dropping the preseason record to 0-2 this year. There will be plenty to observe, as this game is the last chance for many young players to show what they can do and for roster-bubble players to prove themselves one more time. Here are five things to watch. 1. Garrett Nussmeier One of the biggest camp and preseason storylines for the Chiefs has been the emergence of the seventh-round rookie quarterback. With solid performances in training camp and the first two weeks of the preseason, Kansas City will get an extended look at Nussmeier on Friday night, when the team announced him as a starter . With Chris Oladokun in concussion protocol, Nussmeier could play the entire game. Nussmeier has the potential to become the long-term backup quarterback option for the Chiefs, and a solid game on Friday night would help propel him further in his career. 2. Will Rice and Worthy suit up? Neither of the Chiefs’ top two wide receivers has suited up at all during the preseason, and both have missed time in camp with injury. Rashee Rice is coming off of a knee cleanup surgery, and while he has been taking snaps in camp, we have yet to see him at full speed in a game situation. Xavier Worthy missed large portions of camp with a shoulder injury — which is notable because a shoulder injury limited what he was capable of doing on the field in 2025. On Wednesday, head coach Andy Reid could not confirm whether either would play in the preseason finale, so it will be worth monitoring if either makes their debut on Friday. 3. Can Felix Anudike-Uzomah continue to build momentum? Headed into camp and the preseason, defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah was down and out. The injury had cost him all of 2025, and the team had declined his fifth-year option, setting him up for free agency after this coming season. 2026 is realistically his last chance to salvage a career, but the former first-round pick has come out, competed, and worked to earn his job in St. Joseph and so far in the team’s first two preseason games. Looking bigger and stronger, he has competed both off the edge and as an inside rusher so far through camp and the preseason. A big sack last weekend highlighted a strong preseason, but he must keep building momentum this week and carry that early success into the regular season. 4. Right tackle and swing tackle battle The Chiefs offensive tackle struggled a week ago in Tampa, and the entire unit needs a bounceback effort this week. With Trey Smith back in the lineup at right guard, this will allow Jaylon Moore to slide to right tackle, while rookie Kahlil Benson will be tested on the left edge because of the absence of starting left tackle Josh Simmons (Back). Both Benson and Moore struggled, giving up multiple pressures in preseason Week 2; Benson surrendered a strip sack. In the live action, Benson looked to be playing a tick slower than those around him, and it cost him. Moore looked rusty and did not play the way he is capable of, but as of now he is the team’s best bet to start at right tackle once Simmons is back on the left side. The “backup” tackles did not look much better, as Esa Pole struggled throughout the course of the game. Ethan Driskell played well and will likely earn another look and multiple snaps this week with the second team. The depth issues across the offensive line triggered a trade on Wednesday, when the team traded for Josh Ezeudu from the New York Giants . Ezeudu will bring the versatility to play guard or tackle, and likely take a roster spot since he is not expected to compete on Friday. This will add to the intrigue as the Chiefs wrap up the preseason. 5. Bubble watch The fight for the final 53-man roster is on. Here are a few bubble players on the edge of making the active roster or being released. Interior offensive lineman Hunter Nourzad Tight end Jake Briningstool Offensive tackle Ethan Driskell Wide receiver Nikko Remigio Running back Emari Demeracdo Defensive tackle Marcus Harris Defensive end Tyreke Smith Linebacker Cam Jones Linebacker Cole Christensen Safety Xavier Nwankpa Cornerback Zelmar Vedder Cornerback Kevin Knowles Most of these players will be great candidates to make the practice squad or land elsewhere, but for some, it could be the end of the road. Even with solid performances, some could still be on the outside looking in. When roster cuts occur league-wide, that opens the door for teams to snag cut candidates and add to the roster. This season, the Chiefs will have a prime spot in the waiver order to claim talent, so the front office will be looking both internally and externally to maximize the roster.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Greg Desrosiers Jr. #31 of the Los Angeles Chargers carries the ball during a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. Offense Best WR Quentin Johnston – 95.0 RB Greg DesRosiers Jr. – 92.4 TE Charlie Kolar – 86.5 WR Gary Jennings – 80.1 C Josh Kaltenberger – 75.9 DesRosiers ran rampant with 118 carries on 118 yards on nine carries while adding another reception foro eight yards. He looked like a man possessed on his 34-yard touchdown run and it seemed like magic happened every time he touched the ball. Undrafted rookie free agent Greg Desrosiers Jr. balled out tonight: Nine Carries 118 yards, 1 TD “At the end of the day, they’re going to have a big decision to make and my job was to make it hard for them.” – he said pic.twitter.com/7SZAdrikA8 — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) August 28, 2026 Jennings led the Chargers with three receptions against the Rams and finished with 44 yards. Worst OT Laekin Vakalahi – 27.0 OG/T Alex Harkey – 44.6 QB Trey Lance – 47.1 QB Justin Herbert – 49.8 TE Oronde Gadsden II – 51.1 Vakalahi allowed the strip sack on D.J. Uiagalelei and finished with a literal 0.0 grade in pass blocking. It should be a near-impossibility to receive that grade while actively trying to block people, but here we are. Tuipulotu had one of the best pass rushes of the night when he bull-rushed a left tackle into the lap of Ty Simpson to force an incompletion. Worst DT Jacob Guillory II – 34.4 CB Nikko Reed – 38.3 EDGE Nadame Tucker – 45.3 CB Cam Hart – 53.1 LB Emany Johnson – 54.5 Reed’s grade was killed by allowing a touchdown pass to wideout Brennan Presley. His 44.7 was second worst on the team behind Emany Johnson’s 39.7. Tucker was flagged for offsides and his tackling grade of 24.6 was the worst on the defense. title: Chargers-Rams Game Recap: D.J. Uiagalelei, Greg DesRosiers Jr. lead inspired effort in loss
summary: The Chargers fell 20-18 to the Rams in a back-and-forth matchup inside SoFi Stadium. Justin Herbert and the majority of the starters got four plays on the night, headlined by a 65-yard touchdown pass to Quentin Johnston. The stars of the night for the Chargers were third-string quarterback D.J. Uiagalelei and running back Greg DesRosiers […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 20: Tight end Jerand Bradley #36 of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts with teammate running back Greg Desrosiers Jr. #31 after a touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers in the second half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Thursday, August 20, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Chargers fell 20-18 to the Rams in a back-and-forth matchup inside SoFi Stadium. Justin Herbert and the majority of the starters got four plays on the night, headlined by a 65-yard touchdown pass to Quentin Johnston. The stars of the night for the Chargers were third-string quarterback D.J. Uiagalelei and running back Greg DesRosiers Jr. “DJU” led the team with 141 passing yards with a completed pass for a two-point conversion. DesRosiers took nine carries for a whopping 118 yards, including a bruising 34-yard touchdown run. Defensively it was a fine day as the Chargers stood their ground on fourth downs several times, but otherwise got diced up by rookie Ty Simpson who completed 18-of-23 passes. The Rams offense has always looked to get the ball out fast which made it tough for the Chargers pass rush to make plays. With the preseason now over, final cuts are next. The deadline to cut a roster down to 53 players is this Sunday (August 30th) by 4:00 p.m. First Quarter After receiving the opening kickoff, the Rams offense found early momentum with a nine-yard pass to CJ Daniels and a two-yard run by Jordan Waters to move the chains. The Chargers starters then allow just five yards on the next three plays to force the first punt of the game. Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense got started with a nine-yard pass to Charlie Kolar who authored a similar play to begin last week’s game against the 49ers. Unfortunately the starters’ first drive of the game was cut short after Herbert fumbled a handoff to Omarion Hampton and the Rams recovered. Chris O’Leary’s unit held strong after the sudden change and held the Rams to a short 27-yard field goal as they took the 3-0 lead. The second Chargers drive of the game was also just two plays, but the end result was as far as you can get on the other side of the spectrum. Herbert took the snap, faked a handoff right, and lofted a moonshot to Quentin Johnston who caught it in stride for a 65-yard touchdown. Simpson took the Rams on a long 17-play drive before the end of the quarter, but the Chargers shut the door on fourth down near the goal line to keep points off the board. Linebacker Marlowe Wax and safety Tony Jefferson each authored big stops on third and fourth down. Second Quarter Trey Lance took over for Herbert to begin the second quarter but his opening drive of the night was a three-and-out. Punter JK Scott, who has had a rough preseason thus far, shanked his first punt of the night for only 20 yards. Simpson and the Rams quickly turned it into a five-play drive that ended in an 11-yard touchdown pass to wideout Brennan Presley. The Chargers offense was more successful on their next drive as they went 10 plays and 50 yards without Lance needing to complete a pass. Unfortunately Lance was sacked on fourth down at the LAR 30-yard line which forced a turnover on downs. Simpson continued to slice and dice the Chargers defense on another lengthy drive that stretched 13 plays and 61 yards before stalling in the red zone. Harrison Mevis came on again to bang home a 27-yarder to push their lead to 13-7. With less than 30 seconds remaining in the half, D.J. Uiagalelei stepped in for Lance and immediately brought the Chargers downfield with a pair of throws that went 21 and 20 yards, respectively. With nine seconds left, Uiagalelei was sacked for six yards and Dicker came on to attempt a 49-yard field goal but he pushed it wide right. Third Quarter The third quarter was a fast one as both teams leaned on their run games throughout. The Chargers took the second half kickoff and put together a nine-play drive that only went 23 yards due to a facemask penalty on rookie offensive lineman Alex Harkey. Scott’s second punt of the night went just 33 yards, continuing his very poor preseason performance. The Bolts held the Rams to another punt after a short six-play drive. UDFA running back Greg DesRosiers Jr. then put the team on his back with runs of 15 and 14 yards. After stalling just inside the red zone, Dicker came on and converted from 34 yards out to bring the Chargers within three points. Fourth Quarter Rams quarterback Mattew Caldwell helped march their offense down the field on a seven-play, 60-yard drive that spanned over the break. Caldwell capped it off with an eight-yard pass to running back Dean Connors which pushed their lead back to 10 points. DesRosiers Jr. ripped off a huge 34-yard run touchdown run on the ensuing drive, breaking numerous tackles on the way. Uiagalelei then found tight end Evan Svoboda for the two-point conversion which brought the score to 20-18. After a short drive ending in a punt for either team, the Rams found their offensive momentum again. Caldwell moved the Rams 44 yards in 12 plays but could not overcome an ill-timed penalty near midfield. Once backed up, the Rams turtled up and the Chargers stuffed several runs before they punted once more. Fortunately for the Rams, their punter pinned the Bolts all the way back to their one-yard line. But did that matter to Uiagalelei? Apparently not. DesRosiers started the drive with a three-yard run to create some breathing room. Then, Uiagalelei found wideout Liam Clifford for a gain of 13 before hitting Gary Jennings for 24 yards. With a fresh set of downs and facing a first-and-five at the Rams 40-yard line, things quickly evaporated. Uiagalelei was sacked for six yards, despite looking as if he pitched the ball before the whistle. On the very next play, DJU was stripped from behind and the Rams recovered to snuff out the final comeback attempt.

full_text: Woodland Hills, - June 08:Rams Puka Nacua (12) at Rams practice on Monday, June 8, 2026. (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) g | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett have been missing Rams practices throughout August due to injury , with no clear indication on when either player will be back in the fold. Though the expectation (as far as we know) is both players would be able to suit up on a gameday, we asked fans if they were worried about either Nacua or Garrett missing time? 69% of fans are simply not worried about Nacua or Garrett missing any time, so far. 19% of the fans surveyed claimed to be worried about both players, while 12% are split between worrying about Nacua and Garrett respectively. Whether you think that means Matthew Stafford has a bad day without Nacua, or that Terrance Ferguson goes off in Nacua’s place, you can make those bets and more on FanDuel ! If you can think of it, you can likely bet it. Bet responsibly and have fun with it. You never know, the next big winner could be you! And keep an eye on who will be suiting up for Week 1, nothing is decided until it’s official, and until an official roster is shown, nothing is decided, but as it stands, Rams fans expect their starters to be good to go in Australia.

title: Rams 53-man roster projection: Final pre-cuts edition
summary: In the final stages of building out their 2026 roster, the Los Angeles Rams took time out to knock off their roommates, the L.A. Chargers, 20-18 in the preseason finale. In perfect Hollywood fashion, the game and roster build was shrouded in mystery, a last-minute plot twist, and a touch of drama. Mystery still surrounds […]
full_text: Sean McVay is looking to score with the Rams 2026 opening roster (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the final stages of building out their 2026 roster, the Los Angeles Rams took time out to knock off their roommates, the L.A. Chargers, 20-18 in the preseason finale. In perfect Hollywood fashion, the game and roster build was shrouded in mystery, a last-minute plot twist, and a touch of drama. Mystery still surrounds the fate of Aaron Donald’s return. Just hours before the kickoff, the Rams turned the the table on roster projections by trading running back Jarquez Hunter , in the midst of a heated roster battle, for wide receiver Tutu Atwell, a roster lock. The controversy, amongst fans at least, is that Atwell had spent his first five years in L.A. with more potential than distinction and wasn’t offered a contract after the 2025 season. For the Rams newcomers, this roster was gong to be tough to make, there were just a few positions in play. General Manager Les Snead has filled the coffers with players that fit into Head coach Sean McVay’s exacting protocols. The Rams coaching staff has put together a mentally/physically tough squad that plays hard to the whistle. While the Charger game had a few watch-worthy individual performances, It appeared that the game had little effect on a roster reset. In fact, it was the few players that didn’t/hardly participate that told the story. Here’s my final roster reset, an opening 53 projection ( players in bold ), a 17-man practice squad (PS), and individual snap counts (in parentheses) from the Rams/Chargers game. Quarterback (3) Matthew Stafford, Ty Simpson (48), Stetson Bennett No changes, the only debate is the “official’ naming of QB#2. Simpson looked decisive and sharp on the short throws and it was cool to see Matthew Caldwell (26) get some play time. McVay doesn’t usually give his QB#4 camp arms that much action. TRENDING: Ty Simpson’s BEST PASSES from his first preseason in the NFL. 47/60 (78%), 382 passing yards, 3 TD’s, 0 INT’s, 19 FD’s, 109.9 passer rating 😳🎯 pic.twitter.com/lcUZveANt9 — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 28, 2026 Running back (3) Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, Ronnie Rivers All of the roster battle debate went out the window before kickoff with the trade of Jarquez Hunter. The Rams do not usually give up on draft picks, unless their just not a fit. I’m going with Dean Conners (38) over Jordan Watwers (36) for a PS berth. Wide receiver (6) Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, Xavier Smith, Tutu Atwell Welcome home, Tutu. “You can check out anytime you like, but you can never leave.” His addition almost assures that both CJ Daniels (34) and Brennan Presley (53) are the odd men out. Both are likely destined for the PS. I thought Presley was outstanding throughout the preseason slate, the best of the L.A. receivers. Tyler Scott (42) showed flashes over the preseason, but as is in his past, not near enough to justify a roster spot. Goodbye to Tru Edwards (38) and Alex Bachman (32). Tight end (5) Colby Parkinson, Terrance Ferguson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, Max Klare (41) No surprises, most fans would agree that this was always going to be the lineup. Mark Redman (24) to the PS for sure and the Rams initial monetary investment in Dan Villari (20) gets him there as well. Rohan Jones (12) only received a handful mop-up offensive reps over three games. Offensive line (10) Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon, Beaux Limmer, David Quessenberry, Justin Dedich, Keagan Trost, Dylan McMahon Throwing in Dylan McMahon as the surprise 10th offensive lineman, he really played solidly in the first two games and got the night off in the finale. RG Austin Blaske, C Wyatt Bowles, LT AJ Arcuri, and RT Bryce Henderson all played every snap, 74. Bill Murray (30) was the fifth starter. In the first two drives, against most of the Chargers first teamer’s, they had their hands full, but over a body of work, all handled themselves quite well. Blake Hance stepped in for Murray. Tough battle for the PS. As much as I liked Wyatt Bowles effort and C/G versatility, the combination of AJ Arcuri, Austin Blaske and Bill Murray offers the Rams comprehensive versatility insurance. Special teams (3) Ethan Evans, Harrison Mevis, Joe Cardona No need to worry about the specialists, all three are solid. Again, double-teaming the gunner’s on punt returns, could really open things up. Upgrade onkick coverage? Well, fans will believe it when they see it. What a beaut from @ethanevans 🤩 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/Oy7kp5nRIB — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 28, 2026 Defensive line (5) Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Poona Ford, Tyler Davis, Ty Hamilton The defensive interior, as a whole, has not played well in preseason. Bill Norton (30) has led the way, he’s tough to move, but doesn’t get much push. Tim Keenan (24) needs plenty of seasoning. Larrell Murchison (26) looks to be near the end. Although Payton Zdroik (27) and Jaxson Moi (27) both looked to have improved over three games, neither are ready to contend with higher grade competition. Edge (5) Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart, Desjuan Johnson, Wesley Bailey (2) The biggest recipient of the defensive line’s ho-hum play will be Bailey. I think the Rams will want to protect him, he strikes me as the only player at the bottom of the roster that would not clear waivers. Darryl Peterson (42) improved incrementally over his three outings and wins a PS role. Latecomers Tomon Fox (45) and Devean Deal (23) were always here as camp bodies. Darryl Peterson has been going crazy… someone to look at during final cuts 👀 possibly a practice squad player. pic.twitter.com/964EkMKBFQ — Rams Tapes 🇵🇷 (@RamsTapes) August 28, 2026 Off-ball linebacker (4) Nate Landman, Omar Speights, Shaun Dolac, Grant Stuard Another position where the end result was never in doubt. Nikhai Hill-Green (49) got in a lot of work over three games and while not outstanding, showed enough for a PS berth. Elias Neal (21) is cut from the same cloth, a good guy to have on the practice squad. Monty Rice (26) was added just for preseason games. Safety (5) Kamren Curl, Quentin Lake, Kamren Kinchens, Jaylen McCollough, Nick Andersen (8) I’m going to stay with Andersen (8) making the 53. He appears to be from the Rams toughness/effort/IQ mold and played generally well. Nate Valcarcel (42) doesn’t justify a opening roster bid, but is a good prospect for the PS. Alex Cook (49) could challenge for the PS, but doesn’t have as much growth potential. Coaches love Tanner Ingle (29) for his hustle and work ethic, but he still struggles to take good angles. Cornerback (4) Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Emmanuel Forbes, Josh Wallace The Rams got Cam Lampkin (36) plenty of work both outside and in the slot, but I’m not sure his preseason play was enough to crack the billet. AZ Hamilton (44) had some flashes and will get development work on the practice squad. Didn’t see enough consistency from Alex Johnson (17) over three games, but he could sneak onto the PS. Nyzier Fourqurean (39) is in the same boat. Steven Gilmore (10) mopped up. Practice squad (17) RB Dean Conners WR Brennan Presley WR CJ Daniels TE Mark Redman TE Dan Villari OL Austin Blaske OL Bill Murray OL AJ Arcuri DL Tim Keenan DL Bill Norton E Darryl Peterson LB Nikhai Hill-Green LB Elias Neal S Nate Valcarcel CB Cam Lampkin CB AZ Hamilton P Jack Bouwmeester (Exchange) The AD effect and final roster thoughts If the Rams do come to terms and activate Aaron Donald by Monday, I would guess that edge Wesley Bailey becomes the odd man out. Bailey does strike me as the likely most sought after of the Rams final cuts and could therefore be snapped up, but 9 of 10 Rams fans would prefer Donald back in horns over a youngster who still needs a lot of development work. The opening roster may be in line for a couple of tweaks before the opener with the…
