title: Tua Tagovailoa set to return to Miami as Falcons visit Dolphins
summary: The third week of the NFL Preseason schedule typically does not include major storylines as everyone focuses on the depth players who are trying to make the roster more than the players who, in two weeks, will be starting and major contributors in the regular season. Roster cuts are coming due, with each team needing […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Atlanta quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) reacts during the NFL pre-season game between the Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons on August 14th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The third week of the NFL Preseason schedule typically does not include major storylines as everyone focuses on the depth players who are trying to make the roster more than the players who, in two weeks, will be starting and major contributors in the regular season. Roster cuts are coming due, with each team needing to drop 37 players in the hours between its preseason game and 6 p.m. Eastern time on Sunday. Typically is the keyword in that opening sentence. When it comes to the Miami Dolphins’ final preseason game, another storyline is set to play out. The Dolphins host the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night, and a familiar face will hit the field at Hard Rock Stadium, but he will wear white, red, and black instead of aqua and orange. Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, Miami’s 2020 first-round pick, was released this offseason and now returns as the Falcons’ signal caller. Tagovailoa is expected to start in Friday’s game for Atlanta. He will be the first “franchise” quarterback for the Dolphins to return to South Florida with another team – Bob Griese and Dan Marino never left Miami and Ryan Tannehill never faced the Dolphins in Miami after he moved to the Tennessee Titans. Tagovailoa highs and lows in Miami In six seasons with the Dolphins, Tagovailoa threw for 18,166 yards with 120 touchdowns and 59 interceptions. He led the league with 4,624 passing yards in 2023 and earned a Pro Bowl selection that year. He was the league’s completion percentage leader in 2024 and the passer rating leader in 2022. He is the team’s all-time leader in passer rating and completion percentage and ranks fourth in franchise history in passing yards and touchdown passes. Injuries, particularly concussions, played a major role in the decline of Tagovailoa’s play, ultimately leading to his release. He succeeded when he could anticipate routes and use his accuracy to thread passes through tight defenses. Over the last two years with Miami, the timing seemed off, his arm lost strength, and his confidence seemed shot – both in himself and in his offensive line. Salary cap impact of Tagovailoa’s release It was time for a new start for Tagovailoa and for the Dolphins – even as his release costs Miami $55.4 million in cap space this season and another $43.8 million next year. Are the Falcons getting the quarterback who can lead the league in major passing statistics or are they getting the quarterback who was eventually benched last year for a seventh-round rookie? To get an idea of what the Falcons have in Tagovailoa, I spoke with Jeanna Kelley from The Falcoholic, SB Nation’s Falcons team site. She provided a great breakdown of Tagovailoa’s time in Atlanta. Tua’s roller coaster summer Kelley: Tua’s performance has definitely been up-and-down this summer, but there are several caveats. One, Atlanta’s right tackle Kaleb McGary retired unexpectedly this offseason, and Jawaan Taylor was brought in as the probable replacement, but he was working through some injury issues early on that delayed his ability to really integrate with that unit. You know what it’s like when an offensive line hasn’t quite developed the chemistry they need to be effective, and in addition to adjusting to a new scheme and developing his timing and chemistry with his new receivers, that hasn’t made Tua’s life easier. Door open for Tagovailoa to start If Tua’s able to play well, I think it would be bonkers to make a change when Penix is ready to play. Kelley: I do not think Michael Penix will be able to start Week 1. I believe he is healthy, but given how recently he was medically cleared and that he’s just had three days of practice, I feel like the season is creeping up too quicky for Penix to be ready, so I think Tua will be the starter. And if Tua’s able to play well, I think it would be bonkers to make a change when Penix is ready to play. Tua’s work ethic on display Kelley: Tua’s biggest strengths, in my opinion, are his maturity, intelligence (general intellect and football IQ), and work ethic. If it is at all possible for Tua to put himself in a position to succeed — if that is actually something that is within Tua’s control — I believe with his mindset and work ethic, he will get it done. If it’s out of Tua’s control, though — for example, if he (and I truly, truly hope he does not) gets another concussion, then all bets are off. Fans frustrated but Tagovailoa the best option Tua has not been perfect, but I still firmly believe he’s the Falcons’ best option Week 1 unless Michael Penix’s status changes dramatically Kelley: Falcons fans are generally over the Tua experiment and would rather see either Penix regardless of whether he’s fully physically ready, or Jack Strand, the UDFA dynamo who’s shown out against guys buried deep on the depth chart, but needs quite a bit of development coming out of Minnesota-Moorhead. No, Tua has not been perfect, but I still firmly believe he’s the Falcons’ best option Week 1 unless Michael Penix’s status changes dramatically much faster than I expect. And Tua is such a good guy; I can’t help but hope it works out for him — if not in Atlanta long-term, given what they invested into Penix, then I hope he’s able to show enough this season to get another shot at a starting gig elsewhere.

title: Dolphins roster predictions: 53-man projection before Falcons preseason game
summary: The Miami Dolphins closed out their 2026 training camp this week and host the Atlanta Falcons later tonight in the final preseason game of the year. We are closing in on the roster cut deadline, with teams required to drop from the 90-man preseason limit to the in-season 53-man roster size by 6 p.m. Eastern […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 22: Miami Dolphins linebacker Cameron Goode (53) leaves the field following the preseason NFL game between the New York Giants and the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins closed out their 2026 training camp this week and host the Atlanta Falcons later tonight in the final preseason game of the year. We are closing in on the roster cut deadline, with teams required to drop from the 90-man preseason limit to the in-season 53-man roster size by 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday, August 30. Before last week’s loss to the New York Giants, I posted my first projection for the Dolphins’ 2026 53-man roster. A week later, it is time to update. I will be back on Sunday with my final projection with any changes after tonight’s game. Miami Dolphins offense (24) Quarterback (2) Malik Willis Quinn Ewers Cut: Cam Miller, Mark Gronowski Changes: None. This seems pretty straightforward now. Unless Ewers reaggravates his injury or Miller absolutely balls out tonight, there should not be a change to the quarterback plan. Running backs (4) De’Von Achane Jaylen Wright Ollie Gordon II Jarquez Hunter Cut: Coleman Bennett, Donovan Edwards, Carlos Washington, Jr. Changes: Add Hunter Miami traded for Hunter on Thursday, a day after signing Bennett. They are clearly looking for additional depth at running back. Hunter could prove to simply be a body for Friday’s game, but the trade and the signing could signal concern that Gordon’s rib injury might slow him for a little while. Adding Hunter gives the team some flexibility at the position. Fullbacks (0) Cut: DJ Herman Changes: Cut Herman I think Herman has a pathway to the roster, but the Dolphins listing Sims as their starting fullback, even though he is a tight end, is a concern. The Dolphins signed free-agent linebacker Stephen Dix, Jr. and assigned him the same number (34) as Herman; that cannot be a good sign. Herman could be a practice squad option. Tight ends (3) Greg Dulcich Will Kacmarek Ben Sims Cut: Ethan Conner, Seydou Traore, Jeremiah Franklin Changes: Cole Turner from cut to injured reserve; Cut Ethan Conner after signing this week No major changes here. Sims makes the roster as the primary fullback option if the Dolphins want to use him there. There is an assumption that Sims will be healthy and ready for the start of the year – otherwise, I will have to find a way to add Herman back to the roster. Kacmarek has had a good training camp and preseason, showing his ability to be a strong option as a sixth offensive lineman. Dulcich starts. Traore is added to the practice squad with the exemption for being an International Player Pathway member. Offensive lineman (9) Tackles Patrick Paul Austin Jackson Caedan Wallace Guards Kadyn Proctor Jonah Savaiinaea DJ Campbell Josh Priebe Centers Aaron Brewer Andrew Meyer Cut: Gottlieb Ayedze, Jim Bonifas, Charlie Heck , Kevin Cline, Marques Cox, James Ester Changes: Cut Charlie Heck; Jim Bonifas removed after Dolphins cut him this week Heck gets cut here because I need the roster space – mostly because I had an extra player on the roster last week. My math was all over the place and I should have triple-checked my count. Heck is on the roster bubble, however, and could make it depending on what the Dolphins decide for the center position. Bonifas was listed as a cut last week, then the Dolphins moved on from him. Meyer’s position is not guaranteed at center, with Priebe possibly filling in as a backup at both guard and center – though I would not say Priebe’s roster spot is locked in, especially once Miami starts making waiver claims after other teams cut linemen. Wide receivers (6) Malik Washington Caleb Douglas Chris Bell Kevin Coleman, Jr. Jalen Tolbert Jalen Reagor Cut: AJ Henning, Donaven McCulley, Terrace Marshall, Jr., Ryan Miller, Theo Wease, Jr. Changes: Tutu Atwell removed after trade to Los Angeles Rams; Cut Ryan Miller after being a waiver claim by the Dolphins this week; Tahj Washington removed after being waived No changes for the six players projected to make the roster. The locks are Washington and the three rookies (Douglas, Bell, Coleman). Tolbert is close to a lock, but the Dolphins could consider swapping him out in a waiver claim after the cuts. Reagor is a bubble player who hangs on for special teams purposes; Henning has played well enough to push ahead of Reagor, especially with a strong performance tonight. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Miami Dolphins defense (26) Defensive ends (6) Chop Robinson Josh Uche Robert Beal, Jr. Max Llewellyn Clelin Ferrell Cameron Goode Cut: Seth Coleman-Lyles, Rodney McGraw, David Ojabo Changes: Cut David Ojabo; Add Cameron Goode; Add Clelin Ferrell Last week, I had Ojabo ahead of Ferrell, but I think Ojabo’s stock has continued to fall and now he is on the wrong side of the bubble. Of course, this is assuming Ferrell and Goode are both healthy enough to make it to the roster – or that they will be on the roster then placed on injured reserve once waiver claims begin. Goode makes the roster to provide an additional edge rusher with the injury to linebacker Trey Moore. Defensive tackle (5) Zach Sieler Kenneth Grant Jordan Phillips Zeek Biggers Matthew Butler Cut: Keith Cooper, Jr., Alex Huntley, Fatorma Mulbah, Cam Rice Changes: Cut Mulbah; Add Butler The bubble watch last week had Mulbah on the roster and Butler being cut. They flip this week. Mulbah had a strong opening preseason game, but Butler has probably been more consistent all summer. Plus, Mulbah should be able to be stashed on the practice squad. Linebackers (6) Jordyn Brooks Jacob Rodriguez Tyrel Dodson Kyle Louis Ronnie Harrison, Jr. Willie Gay, Jr. Cut: Stephen Dix, Jr., , Cam Riley, Jackson Woodard IR: Trey Moore Changes: Add Gay; Trey Moore off roster to IR Last week, I wrote, “Harrison and Gay are in a position battle to claim the final spot among the linebackers.” That changes this week because of Moore’s injury; he likely will start the season on IR, opening the roster spot Gay needs. Woodard needs to stay with the team, probably on the practice squad, unless the Dolphins are concerned he would be claimed off waivers – which could push Gay back off the roster. Miami cracked the seal on trades on Thursday, sending wide receiver Tutu Atwell to the Los Angeles Rams; Dodson and Gay could both be trade candidates as Miami looks to churn the roster. Cornerbacks (5) Chris Johnson JuJu Brents Jason Marshall, Jr. Ethan Bonner A.J. Green III Physically Unable to Perform list: Darrell Baker, Jr., Storm Duck Cuts: Alex Austin, Miles Battle, Ahmari Harvey, Jai’Onte McMillan, Marco Wilson Changes: Cut McMillan after waiver claim from Colts; Cut Wilson from roster Johnson, Brents, and Marshall are locked onto the roster. Bonner probably is safe as well. Green slides on as the final depth option. Wilson falls off the roster because of spot math: linebacker Trey Moore is injured which makes me think the team will keep an extra defensive end (Cameron Goode) which former me to make a cut here. If you told me any of the cuts were to make the roster over Green, I would not argue with you. Safeties (4) Dante Trader, Jr. Zayne Anderson Michael Taaffe Major Burns Cuts: Lonnie Johnson, Jr., Louis Moore I am sticking with my projection last week, but I am not locked into Burns making the roster. If either Johnson or Moore have a stellar game tonight or Burns slips, there could be a change to the prediction come Sunday. Special Teams (3) Long Snapper (1) Tucker Addington Changes: None Kicker (1) Riley Patterson Changes: None Punter (1) Bradley Pinion Changes: None

title: Dolphins trade Tutu Atwell to Rams
summary: The Miami Dolphins on Thursday traded Tutu Atwell to the Los Angeles Rams, returning the wide receiver to the team that selected him in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft. After four seasons with the Rams, Atwell had signed as a free agent on a one year contract with Miami this offseason but […]
full_text: Jul 31, 2026; Miami Gardens, FL, USA; Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tutu Atwell (4) works during practice at Baptist Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Miami Dolphins on Thursday traded Tutu Atwell to the Los Angeles Rams, returning the wide receiver to the team that selected him in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft. After four seasons with the Rams, Atwell had signed as a free agent on a one year contract with Miami this offseason but he was struggling to find a space on Miami’s depth chart. He will now return to the Rams. In return, the Dolphins received running back Jacquez Hunter. A 2025 fourth-round pick, Hunter played special teams for the Rams last year, appearing in five games early in the season before spending the final 11 games of the year inactive. ESPN’s Adam Schefter first reported the trade . Atwell was expected to provide a veteran presence in the wide receiver room, where Miami is relying on several rookies, but he was never able to find a chemistry with quarterback Malik Willis and was sliding closer and closer to the cut line. Veteran wide receiver Jalen Tolbert, who signed as a free agent this year, is set to fill the role Atwell was attempting to hold this season. Rookie receivers Caleb Douglas (third-round draft pick), Chris Bell (third-round draft pick), and Kevin Coleman, Jr. (fifth-round draft pick), are all expected to see significant playing time during the season. Miami is also returning receiver Malik Washington, who appears to be entrenched as a starter. The Dolphins have been looking to add depth to their running back group, where De’Von Achane is locked in as the starter. Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II appear set to be the primary backups, but Miami continues to make moves around the position. On Wednesday, the Dolphins signed running back Coleman Bennett. Gordon suffered a ribs injury in the team’s Preseason Week 2 loss to the New York Giants. Miami could be bolstering the position group simply to have enough running backs to finish the preseason, or they could be adding depth in case Gordon’s rib injury costs him more playing time than anticipated. Miami closed out their 2026 training camp on Wednesday. They will play their final preseason game on Friday when they host the Atlanta Falcons.

title: Vikings Preseason Finale: McCarthy’s Future, Roster Battles, and What to Watch
summary: J.J. McCarthy’s ankle, Max Brosmer’s tape, and Friday’s roster auditions in Denver dominate The Real Forno Show as Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano preview Minnesota’s last exhibition. Tyler opened with the only question that still moves the building: will McCarthy play Friday at 8 p.m. CT against the Broncos? He missed Wednesday so the deltoid […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings walks off the field after the preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images J.J. McCarthy’s ankle, Max Brosmer’s tape, and Friday’s roster auditions in Denver dominate The Real Forno Show as Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano preview Minnesota’s last exhibition. Tyler opened with the only question that still moves the building: will McCarthy play Friday at 8 p.m. CT against the Broncos? He missed Wednesday so the deltoid ankle sprain could settle. Forness’s read is blunt. “If he does play, and especially coming off of an injury like this, I think it’s another stronger signal that he’s done in Minnesota.” He still expects McCarthy gone by Sunday’s 3 p.m. cut deadline — trade or waiver — and listed Jets, Dolphins, Chargers (Jim Harbaugh), Cowboys, and Cardinals as the shops worth watching, while parking rumor-mill “he wants out” items until Rapoport, Schefter, or Pelissero confirm them. The blame pie is split on purpose. “I think you’re going to have to put blame on both the coaching staff, Kevin O’Connell included, and J.J. McCarthy.” Forness will not settle that argument until McCarthy’s next stop plays out: Darnold renaissance or flameout. Dave asked who Friday is supposed to impress. Tyler’s answer: not the fans first. “I think McCarthy really needs to prove to himself that he can be that guy again… he’s lost that confidence.” The Raiders tape from two years ago is the standard. The meniscus, the slump, and too many voices in his ear (O’Connell, the QB coach, Wes Phillips) are the wreckage. Grant Udinski’s exit is “worth considering at a high level,” Forness said — “I am also not willing to sit here confidently and say that it’s everything.” Brosmer is the other face on the thumbnail. Last year’s UDFA earned QB3 over Brett Rypien, then got thrown into real games he “shouldn’t have had to play.” Friday he may see almost the whole night. Tyler wants last year’s preseason version: anticipation, middle-of-the-field answers, no telegraphed picks. “The only way he’s on the roster is if J.J. McCarthy’s gone.” If McCarthy stays, Brosmer is fighting for a practice-squad tape dump. What they’re watching Friday: J.J. McCarthy’s future : Rumblings from insiders suggest McCarthy wants out and teams have called about a trade. Forness expects resolution by Sunday. Max Brosmer’s opportunity : The undrafted QB may play nearly the entire game. “I wanna see the Max Brosmer of last preseason and I wanna see it take a little bit of a step forward,” Forness said. RB3 battle — Demond Claiborne vs. Zavier Scott : Claiborne needs to prove his speed translates: “Speed only matters if you can use it in a football context.” Scott must show he can block and contribute on special teams. WR6 — Dillon Bell vs. Dontae Fleming : With Jeshaun Jones suspended three games (DUI arrest, per Ben Goessling’s reporting), the sixth receiver spot is open. “Bell had a lot of hype coming into training camp and he’s kinda fallen flat,” while Fleming has been “inconsistent, but solid.” Tight end — Gavin Bartholomew vs. Ben Yurosek : The long-term TE1 conversation is live. “Who do they think can maybe develop into your tight end one next year?” Offensive line depth concerns : Beyond the top six, Forness was blunt: “After that, Dave, it’s kind of stinky.” EDGE/DL: Edge 3 is the hole. Chaz Chambliss (now No. 40 so he can play fullback without reporting) has ST value. Elijah Williams is ahead of Isaiahh Loudermilk. Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins profiles as a 5-tech Linebacker shakeup : Ivan Pace Jr. could be expendable. “If you get enough from both [Jacob] Roberts and Bangally Kamara to where, hey, Ivan Pace expendable, you’re gonna save almost $2.7 million.” Jakobe Thomas (drafted safety) vs. Jacob Thomas (UDFA safety) : “Jacob Thomas has outshined everybody in that secondary, but it’s also UDFA in the preseason. I wanna see the third-round pick play.” CBs: Charles Demmings and Da’Veawn Armstead for CB4/5; Zemaiah Vaughn is the sneak. Jake Golday’s role : Forness envisions a Dallas Turner-like development path — sub-packages only, not a full snap load yet. Punter battle : Johnny Hekker vs. Brett Thorson — watch hang time, direction, and ball placement. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: “Everybody is expendable. Everybody,” Forness said. That is the whole finale. Live Two-Minute Warning lands around 10:45 p.m. CT Friday; Two Old Bloggers takes the 3 p.m. Sunday cutdown. Fan with Us!!! What do you think? Watch the full Real Forno Show from Vikings 1st & SKOL and Bleav, then tell us: if McCarthy takes the first snap in Denver, is that development — or a goodbye tape? Does J.J. McCarthy playing Friday mean the Vikings are already done with him? Do you think McCarthy has played his last snap in purple?

title: Fans grade Patriots’ trade of Kayshon Boutte
summary: The New England Patriots officially traded wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans this week, receiving safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028th seventh-round draft pick in return. Boutte’s departure comes after a long offseason full of speculation over his future. The 24-year old requested a trade this past spring as he enters a contract […]
full_text: Feb 8, 2026; Santa Clara, CA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (9) against the Seattle Seahawks during Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots officially traded wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans this week, receiving safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028th seventh-round draft pick in return. Boutte’s departure comes after a long offseason full of speculation over his future. The 24-year old requested a trade this past spring as he enters a contract year and was set to see both his playing time and production dip after the Patriots upgraded their wide receiver depth chart with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Mike Vrabel even revealed Boutte would have been inactive during the season, barring injuries. As New England’s wide receiver room remained deep even beyond Brown and Doubs, the decision was made to move off of Boutte, who never eclipsed the 600-yard mark, to add depth elsewhere on the roster and open up more opportunities for players like Kyle Williams. But for a Patriots team that remains Super Bowl hopeful — where they currently are tied with the fifth-highest odds on FanDuel Sportsbook to hoist the Lombardi Trophy this season — many believed the team should have kept the pass catcher, who has strong chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye. That is why in the results of the latest SB Nation Reacts survey, 30% of participants voted the trade as a neutral C. Much of comment section agreed, largely do to what was viewed as a minimal return: SlotMachinePlayer The grade for this draft depends on two things: Brown staying healthy, since Boutte was the guy most likely to fill that role if he’s hurt. Reed turning into a useful depth player; something Boutte was. The draft pick was meh. Could have likely gotten a higher comp pick if Boutte went elsewhere at the end of the year. Looking like a D right now, since safety wasn’t a position of need, and Reed didn’t play much. PatriotPapa C. Should have gotten a much higher draft pick beyond the 1-for-1 player trade. Patriots had Houston needing to make the trade having just lost Jayden Higgins with torn ACL. Getting much needed help in run defense was a solid move, but a higher draft pick IN 2027 should have been demanded. For Pats Sake F- Patriots got fleeced. Should have been for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2027 3rd or 4th Round Pick. Instead we got a freaking 2028 7th and a player that has not been as productive as Boutte. Sportsbozo52 I think they got what they wanted. A viable player and a 28 draft choice. Boutte will do well in Texas. May he continue to grow! I am a fan of his and will remain a fan of his, just not when he plays the Patriots. I don’t know much about Jaylin Reed, let’s hope he sticks with the Patriots and can be a contributor for the upcoming season. new_phal3123 I think C+ in the sense that it’s just right down the middle. It’s the reality of the market for that type of WR. I think Boutte is a valuable player but in his role with 1 year left, there’s just not a huge market. The plus comes from getting an immediate contributor rather than just a future day 3 pick. Todger Thirty two teams could be looking for a replacement WR, due to a season ending injury, within one week of the season start All in all, this week’s survey results look as follows: Some were in favor of the trade, as 5% of voters graded the move as an A with 24% giving the deal a B. That may have to do with the potential of Jaylen Reed taking on a larger defensive role in New England and becoming the third safety the team was looking for to pair with Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson. Most fans were on the opposite end of the spectrum, however, as 16% of voters grading the trade as a F with another 25% awarding it a D. Following the move, the Houston Texans are now tied with the Patriots in Super Bowl odds on FanDuel Sportsbook . According to executive vice president of player personal Eliot Wolf, the Patriots were not worried about sending Boutte to a fellow AFC contender . “No, there was no concern about that, and I don’t think there was any concern for them to send us a safety that we think can play,” Wolf said.

title: Patriots final 53-man roster projection ahead of NFL cuts
summary: Training camp is over, the preseason is a wrap, and the New England Patriots are officially on to building their first 53-man roster for the upcoming season. What the reigning AFC champions will do is anybody’s guess, but here is our final projection with the NFL cutdown deadline looming. By Sunday, Aug. 30, at 6 […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 22: Kindle Vildor #28 of the New England Patriots reacts to a near interception during a preseason game between the New England Patriots and the Philadelphia Eagles on August 22, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Training camp is over, the preseason is a wrap, and the New England Patriots are officially on to building their first 53-man roster for the upcoming season. What the reigning AFC champions will do is anybody’s guess, but here is our final projection with the NFL cutdown deadline looming. By Sunday, Aug. 30, at 6 p.m. ET we will know what they will have done. For now, here is what we think Mike Vrabel and company will do. Quarterback In (2): Drake Maye, Tommy DeVito Out (1): Behren Morton Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito have been the clear 1-2 at the quarterback position throughout the summer. The former is an MVP-caliber quarterback with clear franchise player qualities, while the latter is an experienced player who had some really good moments leading the second-string offense through training camp and preseason. The biggest question is the status of rookie Behren Morton. The seventh-round draft pick showed some promise, but ultimately would be too much of a luxury to have on the 53-man team. He is a prime practice squad candidate, though, even if waiving him comes with some risk. Running back In (4): Rhamondre Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson, Hassan Haskins , Lan Larison Out (2): Jam Miller , JaMycal Hasty IR (1): Myles Montgomery The running back competition might not have been of the highest quality, but it has nonetheless been entertaining. Under normal circumstances, Terrell Jennings probably would be RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. With him being sent to injured reserve and subsequently waived, however, the race reopened. Based on the full body of work after Jennings’ departure from the active team, we project two players to make the cut: Hassan Haskins and Lan Larison, the former as pure running back depth and the latter adding a receiving and kickoff return element to the mix. Of course, there is a chance the Patriots go below 53 players in order to create space for potential waiver claims. In that case, either could be a cut candidate. Fullback In (1): Reggie Gilliam Out: N/A When Reggie Gilliam joined the Patriots as a free agent in March, the Patriots had three fullbacks listed on their roster. Five months later, he is the last man standing: Brock Lampe was released early in training camp while Jack Westover converted back to tight end. Gilliam will make the team to serve as the lead blocker out of I-formation and serve as a potential H-back as well. Wide receiver In (6): A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III Out (4): Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon, Nick DeGennaro, Tejhaun Palmer IR (2): Jimmy Kibble, Jeremiah Webb The Kayshon Boutte trade to the Texans creates a clearer picture at wide receiver. Whereas the team was looking at potentially carrying seven wideouts — even though Boutte’s role on the game day roster would apparently have been non-existent to begin with — it now has six players as relatively safe bets to make the cut: A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs will be the top duo, with DeMario Douglas the starting slot; Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism provide depth behind them. The other wideouts are all candidates for the practice squad, with Cameron Dorner and Kyle Dixon in particular worth keeping an eye on. Dorner was the most consistent depth receiver over the course of the summer, while Dixon has looked good during the last two preseason games. Tight end In (3): Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon , Tanner Arkin Out (2): Jack Westover , C.J. Dippre IR (1): Julian Hill As mentioned above, the Patriots might cut their roster below the 53-man deadline in order to create extra space for waiver-wire pickups. In that case Arkin might find himself one of the odd men out. For the time being, we do see him make the team as the top blocking tight end behind the projected top two of Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. Among those, Henry is likely to hoard reps while Raridon will be more of a package and part-time piece despite showing some flashes over the last month. Offensive tackle In (6): Will Campbell, Morgan Moses, Caleb Lomu, Marcus Bryant, James Hudson III, Dametrious Crownover Out (2): Jack Conley, Lorenz Metz (exempt) Six offensive tackles might seem excessive given the questions about depth elsewhere on the team, but hear us out. Will Campbell and Morgan Moses are the top two, with Caleb Lomu and Marcus Bryant the next men down the depth chart. Both are facing questions, though: the former about his regular season readiness, the latter about the ankle injury he sustained in the second preseason game against the Eagles. Unless Bryant starts the year on injured reserve with a return designation in place of other projected candidates to be mentioned later, we do see the Patriots carry both on their 53-man team. In addition, James Hudson’s tackle-guard flexibility is a plus (and something Lomu could theoretically also provide), while Dametrious Crownover making it through waivers is not a given and releasing him therefore a plan too risky for our liking. Interior offensive line In (4): Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson, Mike Onwenu, Greg Van Roten IR-DFR (1): Ben Brown Out (5): Mehki Butler, Jacob Rizy, JonDarius Morgan, Darrian Dalcourt, Joseph Michalski While we see the Patriots keep a relatively high number of tackles, we see them start the year thin along their interior offensive line. Behind starters Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Mike Onwenu, we only see one other player make the cut: recent free agent signing Greg Van Roten, whose mix of versatility and experience — let alone his contract — points toward him beating out the competition. We do think the Patriots have another interior lineman in their plans for 2026, though. Ben Brown, who was banged up in the preseason opener, could start the year on injured reserve with the return designation. A reminder: teams can move up to two players to IR with the intention of bringing them back if they are properly designated on cutdown day. Interior defensive line In (6): Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, Cory Durden, Joshua Farmer, Leonard Taylor III, Eric Gregory Out (3): Isaiah Iton , Jeremiah Pharms Jr, Casey Rogers Milton Williams and Christian Barmore are as disruptive an interior duo as there is in the NFL today, but the depth behind them is a question mark. Cory Durden projects as the third option, while the trio of Joshua Farmer and Eric Gregory as well as Leonard Taylor III offer depth against the run (Farmer, Gregory) and pass (Taylor). The numbers are solid and every one of the backups has had his moments in training camp. Overall, however, Williams and Barmore are the only truly-proven commodities in their projected roles. Defensive edge In (3): Dre’Mont Jones, Elijah Ponder , Gabe Jacas PUP (1): Harold Landry III Out (5): Bradyn Swinson , Quintayvious Hutchins, Xavier Holmes, Jesse Luketa , Amari Gainer Harold Landry is not guaranteed to miss the start of the season, per his head coach, but we still see the team keep him on the physically unable to perform list for the first few games. This, in turn, means that the Patriots will start the year quite thin on the edge: with none of the depth pieces truly rising to the occasion, only Dre’Mont Jones, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas have earned spots on the team — for a variety of reason. Fact is, after all, that Jacas in particular has had his issues; the preseason game against the Browns made it painfully clear that he has a long way to go before he can be trusted in an extensive role. As a consequence, this is a position where we can see definitive reinforcements coming through the waiver wire or free agency. As…

title: Patriots vs. Browns: The good, the bad, the s—t that gets you beat
summary: Ahead of his first training camp as New England Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories. The Patriots’ 37-13 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night saw mostly the second of those categories: there was little of the good, but a lot […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Drew Biber #43 of the Cleveland Browns runs the ball during the third quarter of a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of his first training camp as New England Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories. The Patriots’ 37-13 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night saw mostly the second of those categories: there was little of the good, but a lot of the bad and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, let’s follow his lead and break down Patriots-Browns accordingly. The good: No major injuries As noted above, the Patriots’ loss to the Browns was mostly bad. There were still a few positives such as wide receiver Kyle Williams scoring his third touchdown in three preseason games, linebacker Namdi Obiazor being active on defense and special teams, or the kicking operation looking good. The biggest positive from our perspective, however, was the lack of any significant injuries. The only scary moment came midway through the second quarter, when left tackle James Hudson — the Patriots’ starter at that spot in lieu of usual backup LT Marcus Bryant — got banged up. However, Hudson eventually reentered the contest and finished with 37 of 59 snaps. It remains to be seen whether or not Hudson actually factors into the 53-man roster mix come Sunday evening. However, the fact that his was the only issue and still seemingly minor in nature is good news for a New England team that lost three valuable players over the first two weeks of preseason: backup interior offensive linemen Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich against the Colts, followed by Bryant versus the Eagles. The bad: Money downs The Patriots were unable to deliver in most areas on Thursday, but one that stands out in particular were key situations on offense and defense. Offensively, the team went only 4-for-12 on third down, followed by a 1-for-2 fourth down performance (with one of those failed fourth downs a Behren Morton interception that was returned 36 yards to the New England 12-yard line). The unit also finished an uninspiring 0-for-2 in the red zone. The defense, meanwhile, allowed Cleveland to move the chains on eight of 13 third downs. The Browns also went 4-for-6 in the red area, and a perfect 3-for-3 in goal-to-go situations. It wasn’t great. The s—t that gets you beat: Lack of juice Mike Vrabel was hired by the Patriots in January 2025 in large parts because of his reputation as a culture-builder, and he has indeed done a commendable job turning the team around after back-to-back 4-13 seasons. Thursday night, however, saw little of that. Instead, Vrabel’s team showed little juice and was simply outclassed by its opponent from start to finish. The positive is that the team that took on the Browns will not be the one that will face the reigning world champion Seahawks in just under two weeks. None of the true core Patriots were on the field Thursday, and even roster-worthy depth options that struggled — think: Charles Woods and Kindle Vildor — should benefit from the “rising tide lifting all boats” effect. But if we look at the Browns game in a vacuum, none of that matters. For those 60 minutes, the performance and demeanor simply were not good enough.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Browns preseason game
summary: The New England Patriots played a horribly boring and just downright horrible game on Thursday in Cleveland to close out their preseason. Even though their 37-13 loss to the Browns was disappointing very much from start to finish, there are always lessons to be learned. Let’s get into what the Patriots’ final preseason contest of 2026 […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: CJ Dippre #81 of the New England Patriots catches a pass during the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots played a horribly boring and just downright horrible game on Thursday in Cleveland to close out their preseason. Even though their 37-13 loss to the Browns was disappointing very much from start to finish, there are always lessons to be learned. Let’s get into what the Patriots’ final preseason contest of 2026 taught us about the team. Depth concerns The Patriots didn’t play any starters on Thursday night, and, truthfully, they probably didn’t play many backups either. The lack of depth was still startling. They were outmatched at pretty much every position on the field, and blown out by a team that could be one of the worst in football this year. The Browns also didn’t start anyone of consequence, so it’s not like they were facing tougher competition. It just illustrates the point that head coach Mike Vrabel had made last week about New England’s depth . When looking at the starter level, the Patriots have gotten significantly better as a team. If you start to look down the depth chart, that falls apart pretty quickly. It is like that for a lot of teams, but the Patriots need to continue to string good drafts together and find competent UDFAs to help fill out that depth. The hope is that they can do that moving forward, because it was tough to watch some of the guys out there on Thursday. RB3 competition heating up Hassan Haskins isn’t going to be returning kicks any time soon, but he did look good running the ball. He ran tough and picked up yards even while getting hit behind the line of scrimmage. Conversely, Lan Larison had two straight drops when he was on the field, and, while JaMichael Hasty had a few nice runs, I don’t think he’s the guy who the Patriots want as their third back either. This all might be moot, because Jam Miller didn’t even have a carry, which could signal that the Patriots already know that he’s the RB3, and they didn’t really need to see anything else from him on Thursday night. If I had to put money on it, I’d put my money on Miller, but I guess we’ll find out this weekend. Gabe Jacas, error repeater The Patriots knew that they might not be getting the best out of Gabe Jacas early on with him missing time in the spring and at the beginning of camp, but I can’t imagine they thought he would look quite this bad in actual game action. What worries me is not the lack of production when it comes to rushing the quarterback, or even stopping the run, but the fact that he keeps making the same mistakes. He is continually burned on bootleg, RPO, and option plays, and instead of holding the outside integrity, he comes flying in and gives up the edge. It’s happened in every game that he’s played in. At a certain point, you need to ask whether or not he’s ever going to figure it out. I know we’re not even into the regular season of his rookie year, but I would love to see more from him particularly against replacement-level opponents. Until he figures it out, the Patriots simply cannot put him out on the field on a regular basis — which is not good news considering that he currently projects as the team’s third edge. For the love of god, please sign Christian Gonzalez The depth shouldn’t even matter when we’re talking about Christian Gonzalez, but my goodness, it was even worse than anyone could have expected. Kindle Vildor looked awful, Karon Prunty played okay, but had trouble finishing his tackles. Meanwhile, Kobee Minor and Marcellas Dial Jr. both had horrendously bad plays that led to touchdowns. Again, this should have next to no impact on the Patriots signing one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL, but it certainly can’t hurt. Not sure what exactly the hold up has been for the Patriots, or why they wouldn’t be willing to extend one of not only their best players, but one of the best players in the league, but there is no excuse to them not getting something done. Dominated at the line of scrimmage The Patriots obviously didn’t play any starters, or even a lot of second-stringers, but they were completely dominated on both sides of the line. I thought that Caleb Lomu was able to hold his own when he was in there, but I didn’t see much from anyone else on the offensive line. On defense, they got almost no pass rush and couldn’t stop the run either. It was as bad of a night as you could imagine, with no one showing much of anything. I really like the starters that they have on both sides of the ball, but, as soon as guys start going down, there isn’t a lot of depth behind them. Do we have a punter competition? New England brought in a new punter, Matt Haack, because Bryce Baringer got banged up in the game against the Eagles last weekend. Haack had four punts in his Patriots debut, with thrree of them pinning the Browns inside the 20, including a 63-yarder that was downed at the 2. Baringer looked pretty solid in camp, and it’s clear that kicker Andy Borregales is comfortable with him as his holder. That said, Borregales went 2-for-2 on field goal attempts on Thursday night, and the punts looked great from Haack as well. I think there’s going to be a conversation about which punter to keep starting the season, especially with Baringer a little banged up. Kyle Williams might be a one-trick pony, but it’s a heck of a trick There was a whole lot of concern at the beginning of camp about Kyle Williams. He wasn’t getting enough time with the starters, and people were worried that he was on a worrisome trajectory. Well, he might not be a WR1 at this point in his career (or maybe ever), but he had consistently shown that he does one thing extremely well: he is untouchable on a go-route, especially with no safety help. This single skill should be enough to earn him a few looks a game from Drake Maye, one of the best deep ball throwers in the NFL. I am hoping that he will eventually add more tools to his bag, but having the ability to quickly win off the line and consistently beat coverage deep is a valuable skill, and one which I believe is going to be an important part of the Patriots offense this year. Namdi Obiazor makes a few plays On a night where most guys looked terrible, sixth-round draft pick Namdi Obiazor looked at least pretty good. Starting linebackers Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss weren’t dressed, and neither was the injured Khalil Jacobs, leaving Obiazor to look like the best linebacker on the team on Thursday. Granted, that might not be a high bar, but the youngster nonetheless was one of the few defenders to show up on Thursday. It also helps that he plays a bunch of special teams. This, plus his potential to develop into a player on defense, would be a big boost for a team who doesn’t have any noteworthy long-term depth behind Spillane and Elliss. Behren Morton is unimpressive I have mostly liked what I’ve seen from Behren Morton in training camp, and when he has been given reps, he has made pretty good decisions. He looked pretty poised for a rookie, and looked to be a good candidate to eventually become a backup to Drake Maye. All of that went out the window on Thursday. Morton looked frazzled, made some really bad decisions, and missed on a few throws that could have been big plays — all while going against players who mostly will be out of a job come Sunday night. Ultimately, I think he’s a good guy to keep on the practice squad to see if you can develop him into a usable backup, but, after seeing what I saw Thursday, I’m not going to be super upset if someone claims him off of waivers if the Patriots cut him this weekend. Cutdown day is looming The Patriots have to trim their roster from 91 all the way down to 53 by Sunday afternoon, and they have some tough decisions to make. The first few they are…
author: Pat Lane

title: Mike Vrabel doesn’t rule out Harold Landry activation ahead of Week 1
summary: The New England Patriots concluded their 2026 preseason on Thursday night after falling handily on the road to the Cleveland Browns 37-13. Head coach Mike Vrabel spoke to the media after the contest, and while the team wants to remain careful with the situation, he kept open the possibility of defensive edge Harold Landry being […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 18: Harold Landry III #2 of the New England Patriots runs during an NFC Divisional Playoff game against the Houston Texans at Gillette Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots concluded their 2026 preseason on Thursday night after falling handily on the road to the Cleveland Browns 37-13 . Head coach Mike Vrabel spoke to the media after the contest, and while the team wants to remain careful with the situation, he kept open the possibility of defensive edge Harold Landry being activated off the PUP list before the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks on Sept. 9. Special teams ace Brenden Schooler, who was placed on the NFI (Non-Football Injury/Illness) list on July 24 ahead of training camp, was also included as a potential activation by Vrabel. “I think we’ll just continue to see when we get back,” Vrabel said about whether he anticipates the two being activated before roster cuts. “Brenden Schooler and Harold [Landry] both stayed back, and they have to be able to pass certain things because once you take them off [the lists], that’s kind of what it is. “And so, we just want to be very careful and smart with them and not force them into anything. But on the same note, if they can do and relatively perform where we expect them to and where they expect themselves to, that could be a possibility that we could be able to bring those guys off.” Landry dealt with a lingering knee injury during the latter half of last season, which caused the veteran to miss the AFC Championship Game. As a result, Landry underwent knee surgery earlier in the offseason and has been on the PUP (Active/Physically Unable to Perform) list since July 21 . Following last week’s preseason victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, Vrabel said he doesn’t think the Patriots have a very deep roster when asked about personnel usage heading into the Cleveland matchup. He later explained on Monday, appearing on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show , that those remarks were not a shot at the front office and instead a focus on developing the team’s young players. Throughout the summer, the lack of depth on the defensive edge without Landry, paired with the free-agency signing of Dre’Mont Jones, has been a prominent topic. If the 30-year-old is not activated before the NFL’s roster cutdown deadline on Sunday, Aug. 30, he will miss at least the first four games of the regular season. On Thursday evening, New England’s defense as a whole struggled to make an impact. “Not good enough,” Vrabel said about the defense’s effort. “They felt like we got a couple of sudden-change stops and forced them to kick field goals, which I think is always positive. But just not enough. Couldn’t match up to the speed of the quarterback on the zone read and some of those things. But we’ll get back to work and figure out who we’re going to get back to work with.” While the Patriots struggled to consistently stop the Browns’ rushing attack, they also had difficulties containing dual-threat quarterback Taylen Green, who ran for 66 yards. On a second-half third-down, Cleveland ran a read-option play with the quarterback. Rookie defensive edge Gabe Jacas bit too far into the backfield in preparation for a run play, leaving Green the edge to convert the first down and more. Looking ahead to Sunday, New England will need to make roster cuts by 6 p.m. ET. “We’ll make those decisions tonight, tomorrow morning and over the weekend. We’re always going to try to strengthen the roster. Find guys with Eliot [Wolf] and his staff,” Vrabel said. “It’s a very fluid process. “There are going to be players who are going to be with us, and there are going to be [players] maybe picked up by somebody else. We’re going to be looking at people. We’re 31st in the [waiver] claim. It’s just about being patient and figuring out where the right guys are.” All transactions made in the coming days will be made in preparation for compiling a roster strong enough to compete with the Seahawks to kick off the new season with a Super Bowl rematch.
author: Andrew Guindon

title: 5 winners and losers from Patriots’ preseason loss to the Browns
summary: The New England Patriots concluded their preseason Thursday night in Cleveland with a 37-13 loss to the Browns. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ preseason opener. Winners WR Kyle Williams: Another week, another long Kyle Williams touchdown. The second-year receiver played just nine snaps over the Patriots’ […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Wide receiver Kyle Williams #18 of the New England Patriots celebrates scoring a touchdown in the first quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots concluded their preseason Thursday night in Cleveland with a 37-13 loss to the Browns. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ preseason opener. Winners WR Kyle Williams: Another week, another long Kyle Williams touchdown. The second-year receiver played just nine snaps over the Patriots’ first two offensive series but quickly made his mark, hauling in a 45-yard touchdown down the left sideline from Tommy DeVito. It was similar to his touchdowns from the previous two weeks, as Williams once again showcased his elite release package and vertical speed. Williams also caught a 10-yard curl on DeVito’s first pass of the night. KYLE WILLIAMS CAN'T STOP SCORING pic.twitter.com/C8t9Htl7Sh — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) August 28, 2026 P Matt Haack and K Andy Borregales: The kicking game was one of the few bright spots for the Patriots on Thursday. New punter Matt Haack, who was signed on Monday following Bryce Baringer’s injury, impressed in his debut with three i20’s — the best coming on a 63-yard punt that downed itself at the two-yard line. Haack also assumed holding duties for kicker Andy Borregales, who knocked through all of his kicks (two field goals, one extra point). LB Namdi Obiazor: In a depleted linebacker room, the sixth-round rookie played 39 snaps along the second level Thursday night. Obiazor posted a game-high 12 tackles as he was often around the football and seemed to read things well upon first watch in the run game. The rookie has assumed a top special teams role throughout training camp which likely will earn him a 53-man roster spot. Losers Depth cornerbacks: The Patriots’ depth cornerbacks were picked on by Dillon Gabriel and the Browns’ pass catchers throughout the night. Charles Woods and Marcellas Dial Jr. each gave up a touchdown, while Kindle Vildor and Karon Prunty allowed downfield completions (21 and 19 yards, respectively), with the veteran also flagged for defensive pass interference. Woods, who has been the fourth cornerback throughout training camp, played the duration of the third quarter. Kobee Minor then missed a tackle in the run game to directly lead to a touchdown early in the fourth quarter. The group entered Thursday night with question marks behind Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis and Marcus Jones, and the performance from the depth players did little to provide confidence ahead of cutdown day — leading the whole defense’s struggles Thursday night. “Not good enough,” Mike Vrabel said. “We got a couple sudden change stops, forced them to kick field goals, which I think is always positive. But, just not good enough. Couldn’t match the speed of the quarterback in a zone read and some of those things. But we’ll get back to work and figure out who we’re going to get back to work with.” Honorable mentions Behren Morton took a step back after last week’s positive showing. He took three sacks and threw a pair of interceptions. Lan Larison started Thursday’s game but dropped a third-down pass (slightly behind him). Hassan Haskins continued to run hard between the tackles behind him. Kyle Dixon posted a game-high eight catches (on eight targets) for 71 yards. He is a practice squad candidate. Caleb Lomu played nine snaps at right tackle over the Patriots first two drives. He appeared clean in his six pass blocking snaps. Fellow rookie tackle Dametrious Crownover continues to generate good push in the run game, as the whole line found success in the short-yardage run game. Gabe Jacas played 19 snaps in the finale and logged one pressure but also bit again on a zone-read play. He might have been expecting a force defender to play the quarterback, but Jacas has been on the wrong side of the play often this summer. The Patriots went the whole preseason without recording a kick return of 30 yards or more. Perhaps Kyle Williams assumes that role in the regular season, but the unit didn’t generate much confidence elsewhere. To end on a positive: No major injuries to end the preseason.

title: NFL waiver wire, explained: What is the process, and how does it affect the Patriots?
summary: After a preseason showdown against the Cleveland Browns, the New England Patriots will begin cutting down their 90-man roster. The team needs to make 37 moves ahead of the NFL’s deadline on Sunday, Aug. 30, at 6 p.m. ET. A majority of those personnel changes will come through the most straightforward roster reduction method: cutting […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 9: A detailed view of an official Wilson NFL football on the grass field during an NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the New England Patriots at Raymond James Stadium on November 9, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a preseason showdown against the Cleveland Browns, the New England Patriots will begin cutting down their 90-man roster. The team needs to make 37 moves ahead of the NFL’s deadline on Sunday, Aug. 30, at 6 p.m. ET. A majority of those personnel changes will come through the most straightforward roster reduction method: cutting players. However, not all 37 transactions will be the same. The NFL has separate protocols for so-called vested veterans and players with less league experience. Veterans immediately enter the open market as free agents after being released, while the latter must pass through the waiver wire, where they can be claimed by another franchise or enter free agency if unclaimed. What exactly does all of this mean for a Patriots team with the sixth-best Super Bowl odds in the league, per FanDuel Sportsbook ? Let’s break it down. What is the NFL waiver wire? Franchises will make their final preparations before the season, with substantial changes being made to league rosters. Players will either be waived or released, but not all will instantly become free agents and be free to sign with any team. When a player is “waived,” they are subject to the waiver wire, where any team can claim them and assume their current contract. Currently, the waiver wire order is dependent on the NFL Draft order from this past April, but without any trades. Teams file waiver claims at the same time. That being said, only the team with the highest claim in the order will successfully pick up the player and their current contract. Which NFL players are subject to go on waivers and not be released? A player’s time in the NFL determines whether they enter the waiver wire or become a free agent. Players with at least four years of accrued NFL service time are released. If a player is released, their contract has ended, and they are eligible to sign with any team. However, if a player has less than four years of service time, they are waived and subject to waiver wire claims. Any player who is not claimed after being waived is eligible to sign wherever they’d like, including their former team’s practice squad. The group of players being waived primarily consists of those who are not currently eligible for unrestricted free agency status entering the season. They would instead be either an exclusive rights free agent (less than three years of service) or a restricted free agent (three years of service). Which Patriots cuts are subject to waivers? In total, 40 of the Patriots’ depth players (not including starters and primary backups, or “roster locks”) will first have to pass through the waiver wire, where they might get claimed by any NFL team, before entering the open market. QB Mehren Morton RB Lan Larison RB Jam Miller WR Cameron Dorner WR Kyle Dixon WR Nick DeGennaro WR Tejhaun Palmer TE Tanner Arkin TE Jack Westover TE C.J. Dippre OT Dametrious Crownover OT Lorenz Metz OL Jacob Rizy OL Joseph Michalski OL Darrian Dalcourt OL Jack Conley OL Mehki Butler OL JonDarius Morgan DT Eric Gregory DT Isaiah Iton DT Jeremiah Pharms Jr. DT Casey Rogers DT Leonard Taylor III ED Bradyn Swinson ED Xavier Holmes ED Quintayvious Hutchins ED Amari Gainer LB Khalil Jacobs LB Namdi Obiazor LB Riley Wilson CB Karon Prunty CB Charles Woods CB Kobee Minor CB Channing Canada CB Marcellas Dial Jr. CB Brandon Crossley S Dell Pettus S John Saunders Jr. S Eric Butler S Peter Manuma Which Patriots cuts are not subject to waivers? Seven of New England’s depth players are vested veterans. If released, they would become free agents as soon as the respective moves were made official, meaning that they would all be free to sign with any team of their choosing. RB JaMycal Hasty RB Hassan Haskins OT James Hudson III OL Greg Van Roten LB Chad Muma LB K.J. Britt CB Kindle Vildor What is the NFL waiver order right now? The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order. Once we get through four games, it resets to the current NFL standings. So, the Las Vegas Raiders have the first crack at every player on waivers. Las Vegas Raiders New York Jets Arizona Cardinals Tennessee Titans New York Giants Cleveland Browns Washington Commanders New Orleans Saints Kansas City Chiefs Cincinnati Bengals Miami Dolphins Dallas Cowboys Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Tampa Bay Buccaneers Indianapolis Colts Detroit Lions Minnesota Vikings Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers Pittsburgh Steelers Los Angeles Chargers Philadelphia Eagles Jacksonville jaguars Chicago Bears Buffalo Bills Houston Texans San Francisco 49ers Los Angeles Rams Denver Broncos New England Patriots Seattle Seahawks How does the NFL waiver system work? Let’s assume the 31st-ranked Patriots and 32nd-ranked Seahawks are the two teams to place a claim for a player. He will end up in New England due to the organization’s superior ranking. The team with the lowest bid will always end up with the player. Teams can add as many players through waivers as they want, but they might have to make corresponding roster moves to fit them on their 53-man team and/or under the salary cap. Have the Patriots made any moves yet? In order to stay on top of every transaction involving the Patriots’ roster cutdowns on Sunday, ahead of the waiver claim deadline on Monday, make sure to regularly visit our Patriots roster cut tracker .

title: Mike Vrabel provides new insight into Patriots’ decision to trade Kayshon Boutte
summary: Had Kayshon Boutte remained on the Patriots’ roster for Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks, he would have been inactive. Head coach Mike Vrabel revealed that detail Thursday night, speaking for the first time since Boutte was traded to the Houston Texans on Monday. “That was one place where we do have some depth, and […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 14: Kayshon Boutte #9 of the New England Patriots is congratulated by head coach Mike Vrabel after scoring a touchdown reception against the Miami Dolphins during the first quarter in the game at Hard Rock Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images Had Kayshon Boutte remained on the Patriots’ roster for Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks, he would have been inactive. Head coach Mike Vrabel revealed that detail Thursday night, speaking for the first time since Boutte was traded to the Houston Texans on Monday. “That was one place where we do have some depth, and I think for all parties involved, that was probably the best thing,” Vrabel told reporters in Cleveland. “Without injuries, Kayshon probably would have been inactive. Unfortunately, it just, it’s kind of the way it was. It’s just with him not playing special teams.” As Vrabel noted, New England’s wide receiver room is the deepest position on the roster, with A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism. All six are expected to be on the team’s 53-man roster. The Patriots added both Brown and Doubs to the mix this offseason, pushing Boutte down the depth chart. Vrabel made sure to show appreciation for Boutte, as he often did throughout last season. “I tried to thank Kayshon as many times I could. I texted him again today,” Vrabel said. “It’s just his maturity, his growth, his ability to put into words last year and share his own personal struggle, but also the growth that he made from that. That’s positively going to affect a lot of people. And I know that that wasn’t easy for him to do, and I tell him all the time about how much I respect him for being able to do that.” The Patriots traded Boutte to the Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick. Reed will add depth at safety while also providing another option on special teams.

title: Patriots vs. Browns: Final score, stats, game recap from NFL preseason
summary: The New England Patriots concluded their preseason with a 37-13 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night. With Drake Maye and the Patriots frontline players out again, it was a rough showing from New England’s depth players on both sides of the ball — outside of an early highlight from Kyle Williams scoring on […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Wide receiver Luke Floriea #81 of the Cleveland Browns scores a touchdown against cornerback Kindle Vildor #28 of the New England Patriots in the first quarter of a preseason game at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots concluded their preseason with a 37-13 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night. With Drake Maye and the Patriots frontline players out again, it was a rough showing from New England’s depth players on both sides of the ball — outside of an early highlight from Kyle Williams scoring on another deep ball touchdown. Here’s everything that went down in the preseason finale. Final score: Patriots 13 : 37 Browns Thursday, Aug. 27, 8 p.m. ET | Huntington Bank Field, Cleveland, OH | Broadcast information | Game day roster First Quarter The Patriots lost the coin toss putting the defense on the field first against Dillon Gabriel and the Browns reserves. A third-down defensive pass interference penalty downfield on Kindle Vildor quickly put Cleveland outside the red zone. From there, the Browns needed just four plays to find the end zone. [Patriots 0 : 7 Browns] Tommy DeVito drew the start for the Patriots with QB coach Ashton Grant calling offensive plays. After quickly working across midfield, DeVito and Kyle Williams struck again as they connected on a 45-yard touchdown down the left sideline. [Patriots 7 : 7 Browns] Tommy DeVito drops it in to Kyle Williams for 6️⃣ NEvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/agDyHm0clX — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 The Browns offense quickly got back to work. Rookie Gabe Jacas bit on a zone-read to allow Gabriel to pick up a third-down with his legs, before the left quarterback found a pair of chunk gains through the air over the middle — the second being a 14-yard touchdown. [Patriots 7 : 14 Browns] New England then went three-and-out on their next possession as a third-down pass was slightly behind and dropped by Lan Larison out of the backfield. New punter Matt Haack then punted away. Cleveland’s first play of its new drive goes 52 yards on a deep connection to wide receiver Ben Patterson. Multiple Patriots defenders wrap up Gabriel behind the line of scrimmage on third down in the red zone for a registered sack before kicker Andrew Szmyt adds three to the Browns’ column from 35 yards out. [Patriots 7 : 17 Browns] Nearing the end of the first quarter, seventh-round rookie Behren Morton replaces DeVito at the helm of the offense. But the signal-caller’s first pass attempt of the evening bounces off the foot of tight end CJ Dippre and falls into the hands of the opposing defense. Second Quarter As a result, the Browns took over at New England’s 31-yard line. And after a three-play sequence, Szmyt splits the uprights once more. [Patriots 7 : 20 Browns] Looking for a response, Morton drove the Patriots offense into the red zone, where kicker Andy Borregales made a 26-yard field goal attempt midway through the frame. New England’s quarterback scrambled for a gain of 14 before connecting for 19 more yards with Kyle Dixon, sitting in a zone coverage soft spot, to cross midfield on the drive. [Patriots 10 : 20 Browns] Starting its response series just past midfield in New England territory after outside linebacker Amari Gainer was flagged for roughing the passer, Gabriel found running back Ahmani Marshall in the flat, who shed a tackle to secure the score. Cornerback Charles Woods allowed two chunk conversions totaling 39 yards prior. [Patriots 10 : 27 Browns] The Patriots, taking over with just over two minutes remaining until halftime, had Borregales drill a 33-yard field goal with seven seconds left on the clock. A defensive pass interference call that overturned a deep Morton interception set the Patriots up in Cleveland territory before the no-huddle tempo took effect. [Patriots 13 : 27 Browns] Third Quarter Opening the second half, Browns defensive tackle Coziah Izzard broke into New England’s backfield, sacking Morton on a first-down snap. The Patriots were forced to punt after the setback, but seventh-round rookie Quintayvious Hutchins brought down the scrambling returner at the two-yard line after he attempted to create extra yardage. As Taylen Green replaced Gabriel on Cleveland’s following drive, his offense couldn’t overcome the poor field positioning, going three-and-out. Despite New England quickly regaining possession, a three-and-out of its own sent the ball right back to the opposition. Recently signed punter Matt Haack delivered a 63-yard kick, pinning the Browns at their own two-yard line halfway through the third. Fourth Quarter Nevertheless, to end the quarter-long scoring drought, Cleveland running back Davon Booth capped off a nine-minute, 98-yard scoring drive. The ball carrier broke a missed tackle by Patriots cornerback Kobee Minor, easily waltzing into the end zone for the touchdown. [Patriots 13 : 34 Browns] The Patriots, operating in an even larger scoring deficit, followed with an offensive series that only lasted five plays. Punting from midfield, Haack’s punt sailed to the Browns’ 19-yard line for a fair catch with 12 minutes remaining. Cleveland’s goal to close out the game is to chew the clock, which it did for five and a half minutes during a nine-play possession, securing three first downs. New England then attempted to put together a scoring drive, starting from its own 11, but Morton was hit as he threw on a fourth-and-two play, resulting in an interception. The Browns returned the takeaway to the Patriots’ 12-yard line, turning the defensive stop into a successful field goal just ahead of the two-minute warning. [Patriots 13 : 37 Browns] Morton completed a couple of passes on the final drive of the contest as the clock ran out.

title: Saints vs. Cowboys 2026 Preseason: TV Schedule, Online Streaming, Radio, Mobile, and Odds
summary: The New Orleans Saints face the Dallas Cowboys in the final game of the 2026 NFL Preseason.  This game is Kellen Moore’s final chance to evaluate talent to round out the 2026 roster, so don’t expect any starters to play any type of significant time.  The certified starters, who have their roster spots locked up, will likely not see any time on […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 18: Spencer Rattler #2 of the New Orleans Saints throws during joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 18, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints face the Dallas Cowboys in the final game of the 2026 NFL Preseason. This game is Kellen Moore’s final chance to evaluate talent to round out the 2026 roster, so don’t expect any starters to play any type of significant time. The certified starters, who have their roster spots locked up, will likely not see any time on the field today as the Saints should be expected to protect their stars for the regular season opener on September 13th. title: Interview with the Enemy: Dallas Cowboys
summary: The New Orleans Saints will head to Arlington to face the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL preseason. To break it down, David Halprin of Blogging The Boys joins us to preview this weekend’s matchup. NJ: At this point, everyone knows the joint practice between New Orleans and Dallas was chippy as […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 18: Donovan Ezeiruaku #6 of the Dallas Cowboys pulls off Taliese Fuaga #75 of the New Orleans Saints helmet during joint practice at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 18, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints will head to Arlington to face the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL preseason. To break it down, David Halprin of Blogging The Boys joins us to preview this weekend’s matchup. NJ: At this point, everyone knows the joint practice between New Orleans and Dallas was chippy as all get out. Before that joint practice and since then, the Saints haven’t really had any issues with scuffles. Has that kind of intensity and physicality been a consistent theme throughout the Cowboys’ offseason? DH: I would say the intensity has been there through training camp, a certain amount of energy, but we haven’t had the scuffles we saw in that joint practice. Christian Parker is our new defensive coordinator and he has brought a swagger back to the defensive side of the ball, and that has led to some trash-talking during practices as a very poor Cowboys defense from 2025 gets a complete makeover. Brian Schottenheimer is also a high-energy coach so there has been some friendly banter and interplay between the offense and defense, but only OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku, who was thrown out of the Saints practice, was also told to leave a practice earlier in training camp for a similar fighting problem. That appeared to be a very isolated incident because we never saw much else like that until the joint practice. I don’t know what happened during the joint practice, but the fighting seemed out of the ordinary for how the Cowboys had conducted most of their practices. NJ: Which Dallas position battle or group of players has the most to gain from the additional preseason reps against New Orleans? DH: The Cowboys are sorting out quite a few position battles. One of the ones that has been watched a lot is who will be RB2 behind Javonte Williams. Jaydon Blue, Malik Davis, Phil Mafah and Israel Abanikanda are all fighting for reps, with Davis in the driver’s seat right now. The Cowboys are also closely looking at their depth at cornerback as they have a cluster of players all trying to get attention. This one may end up needing some outside help once cutdown day happens. There was a good battle at QB2 going on, but many feel like Joe Milton III has locked that up with a couple of excellent performances in preseason. There is also some competition going on along the backup offensive line. NJ: What are you hoping to learn about the Cowboys from Friday’s matchup against the Saints, and what did you learn from training camp and the first two preseason games that you’d like to see the team build on? DH: For most of the offseason, training camp and preseason, Cowboys fans have been eyeing the changes on defense and hoping they make the team better. Last year, the defense was horrible and totally scuttled the season. First-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker has changed the scheme and has overhauled much of the personnel on that side of the ball. So far, it looks like it is working as the defense has played much better. The continuation of that is what Cowboys fans need to see. We know our offense is powerful and can score points, last year they were great. It is all down to the defense if we are going to have success in 2026. NJ: Who is one Cowboys player you think Saints fans should keep an eye on Friday—someone who may not be receiving much national attention but could make a strong impression? DH: Wide receiver Camden Brown went undrafted as a rookie. He only had one strong college season in his senior year after he transferred, and wasn’t really on our radar after the Cowboys signed him. In training camp, he exploded. He just kept making plays and catching the attention of everybody. Then in the first preseason game he had two spectacular touchdown catches, and in the last game he added a 69-yard catch-and-run pass completion. He has come out of nowhere to the brink of making the roster. If he shines again on Friday, the Cowboys will have to keep him on the roster, it would be criminal negligence not to. NJ: According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Cowboys (-126) are currently 2.5-point favorites over the Saints (+108) in Sunday’s matchup; what is your final score prediction? DH: Predicting scores for preseason games feels like a losing proposition all around because you never know who will play for how long, and what the coaches want to look at that might not be the best strategy for winning the game. But since you asked, I’ll go with Cowboys 24 Saints 13. Thank you again to David Halprin for joining us to preview this week’s matchup! You can check out the rest of his work here .
